research.area: turkic-turkish: Turkish NLP landscape as high-resource Turkic anchor (2024-2026), for porting KazQAD/MTEB-style protocols and Less-is-More embedding recipe, positioning Kazakh in the Turkic resource hierarchy, and scouting pan-Turkic benchmark territory

findings.claim: TUMLU is the only native (non-translated) pan-Turkic MMLU-style benchmark and gives a direct, same-protocol Turkish-vs-Kazakh-vs-Uzbek-vs-Azerbaijani-vs-Kyrgyz-vs-Uyghur comparison at 5-shot: [tr] Claude-3.5-Sonnet 85.7%, GPT-4o 83.7%, Qwen2.5-72B 73.9%, Llama-3.1-70B 64.9%; [kk] Claude-3.5-Sonnet 83.0%, GPT-4o 81.0%, Qwen2.5-72B 62.6%, Llama-3.1-70B 56.4%; [az] Claude-3.5-Sonnet 84.4%; [crh] (Crimean Tatar) 81.2%; [ky] 75.7%; [ug] 71.3%; [uz] 69.1% (lowest of the eight). Notably Kazakh trails Turkish by only 2.7pp on the strongest closed model but by 11.3pp on Qwen2.5-72B and 8.5pp on Llama-3.1-70B — the gap is much wider for open-weight models than frontier closed ones.
findings.source: arXiv:2502.11020 (TUMLU, ACL 2025 Findings), github.com/ceferisbarov/TUMLU
findings.numbers: 38,139 questions, 8 languages (az, crh, kaa, kk, ky, tr, ug, uz), 11 subjects, TUMLU-mini=100 q/subject; kk 83.0/81.0/62.6/56.4 vs tr 85.7/83.7/73.9/64.9 (Claude-3.5-Sonnet/GPT-4o/Qwen2.5-72B/Llama-3.1-70B)
findings.relevance: Directly answers decision (2): quantifies where Kazakh sits vs Turkish and siblings on IDENTICAL native (non-MT) questions; shows open-weight-model gap (8-11pp) is the honest number to cite, not the closed-model gap (2.7pp) which flatters resource parity.

findings.claim: CulturaX's per-language token counts give an exact, checkable resource ratio across the whole Turkic family: [tr] Turkish 64.29B tokens (94.2M docs, 1.02% of the 6.3T-token corpus); [kk] Kazakh 2.80B tokens (2.73M docs, 0.04%); [az] Azerbaijani 3.51B tokens (5.08M docs, 0.06%); [ky] Kyrgyz 501M tokens (0.01%); [ug] Uyghur 77.7M tokens; [uz] Uzbek 75.25M tokens (only 87K docs) — Uzbek is the most under-represented major Turkic language in CulturaX despite ~35M speakers. Turkish is ~23x larger than Kazakh, ~854x larger than Uzbek, ~128x larger than Kyrgyz, ~828x larger than Uyghur in this specific corpus.
findings.source: huggingface.co/datasets/uonlp/CulturaX (per-language stats table); arXiv:2309.09400
findings.numbers: tr 64.29B tok; kk 2.80B tok; az 3.51B tok; ky 501M tok; ug 77.7M tok; uz 75.25M tok (tt/ba/tk/cv/sah lack published token counts, only doc counts: tt 218K docs, ba 72K, tk 14K, cv 22.6K, sah 22.1K)
findings.relevance: Directly answers decision (2)/resource ratios; flags that Uzbek — the language with a live collaboration offer — is WORSE off than Kazakh in raw web-corpus terms (0.04% vs far under 0.01%), so an Uzbek port cannot assume Kazakh-level pretraining data availability.

findings.claim: The CulturaX-derived Turkish:Kazakh ratio (23x) CONFLICTS with the KB's existing XLM-R/CommonCrawl-derived ratio (Kazakh 5.8x smaller than Turkish, not ~23x). Both are legitimate but measure different corpora/cleaning pipelines; the ratio is corpus-pipeline-dependent, not a fixed constant.
findings.source: huggingface.co/datasets/uonlp/CulturaX vs KB node from arXiv:2411.14198 (citing XLM-R/CC stats)
findings.numbers: CulturaX: tr 64.29B / kk 2.80B = 22.9x. XLM-R/CC (KB): kk is 5.8x smaller than tr.
findings.relevance: Direct conflict flag per protocol: any 'Kazakh is Nx smaller than Turkish' claim in the atlas must cite which corpus it's measured in — do not average 5.8x and 23x.

findings.claim: [tr] Kumru-2B (VNGRS, Sept 2025) is the best-executed from-scratch Turkish SLM and dwarfs SozKZ's data scale: 500GB deduplicated corpus, 300B training tokens for a 2B model (150:1 tokens/param) vs SozKZ's 9B tokens for 600M (15.3:1) — a 10x higher data:param ratio. Base+instruct+the full training corpus were open-sourced (transparency move). Runs on 16GB VRAM (RTX A4000/3090) or on-device at 4.8GB unquantized. Context 8,192 tokens; other open-source models spend 38-98% more tokens than Kumru's custom tokenizer while having larger vocabularies.
findings.source: huggingface.co/vngrs-ai/Kumru-2B, huggingface.co/vngrs-ai/Kumru-2B-Base, erkansaka.net/2025/10/14 launch coverage
findings.numbers: 500GB corpus, 300B tokens, 2B params (150:1 tok/param); context 8,192; 4.8GB device footprint; 38-98% tokenizer efficiency vs peers
findings.relevance: Sets the honest 'what a well-resourced from-scratch Turkic SLM looks like' bar — SozKZ's 9B-token/600M-param Kazakh effort is 10x less data-intensive per param than the best Turkish from-scratch precedent, partly explaining its weaker knowledge scores (30.3% MC-QA) relative to Kumru's reported quality.

findings.claim: [tr] cosmosGPT (YTU COSMOS, Apr 2024) is architecturally near-identical prior art to SozKZ one Turkic step earlier: monolingual from-scratch GPT-2-style models (355M, 774M params), dedicated ByteLevel BPE 50,257-token vocab trained on 100GB, total pretraining corpus 275GB (250GB cleaned/deduped CulturaX + 25GB other Turkish sources), trained on TPUv3-8. In direct ELO-based human-preference comparison it LOSES to the larger adapted Trendyol-LLM-7B (cosmosGPT-Large ELO 969 / 43.19% win-rate vs Trendyol-7B 1194 ELO / 70.34% win-rate) despite matched vocab size and from-scratch monolingual training.
findings.source: arXiv:2404.17336 (cosmosGPT), huggingface.co/ytu-ce-cosmos
findings.numbers: 355M/774M params; 50,257 BPE vocab (identical size to SozKZ's); 275GB corpus (250GB CulturaX-derived); ELO 969 vs 1194; win-rate 43.19% vs 70.34%
findings.relevance: Cross-Turkic corroboration of the SozKZ finding already in the Kazakh KB: from-scratch small monolingual Turkic models with a great dedicated tokenizer consistently lose to larger adapted/continual-PT models on the SAME family, strengthening the case that the Kazakh Frontier Lab's architectural differentiation (Engram/memory) rather than 'from-scratch + good tokenizer alone' is the right bet.

findings.claim: [tr] VBART (VNGRS, Jan 2024, precursor to Kumru) achieves 1.33 tokens/word with a 32K-vocab SentencePiece Unigram tokenizer trained on only 10GB of Turkish text, vs 3.10 tok/word for OpenAI's BPE tokenizer on the same text (2.33x more compact). VBART-Large (374M, mBART architecture) matches mT5-Large (1.2B, 3.2x more params) on Turkish question generation/answering.
findings.source: medium.com/vngrs/vbart-the-first-turkish-llm-6f0f6f227ed4
findings.numbers: 1.33 tok/word (VBART) vs 3.10 (OpenAI BPE), 2.33x compaction; 32K vocab; 10GB tokenizer-training text; VBART-Large 374M matches mT5-Large 1.2B
findings.relevance: Turkish's achievable fertility floor (1.33) is even better than Sherkala's tuned Kazakh fertility (2.04) or the lab's <2.0 target — confirms Turkish's simpler morphology-to-token mapping (or smaller effective vocabulary need) gives it a structural tokenization advantage Kazakh cannot fully close even with a dedicated tokenizer.

findings.claim: [tr] Cetvel (KUIS AI / Koç University, EACL 2026, arXiv Aug 2025) tested 33 open-weight Turkish-capable LLMs (up to 70B) across 23 tasks / 7 categories built from 22 Turkish datasets and found that Turkish-centric instruction-tuned models GENERALLY UNDERPERFORM general multilingual models (Llama-3, Mistral) despite language-specific tuning; grammatical error correction and extractive QA were the most discriminative tasks.
findings.source: arXiv:2508.16431 (Cetvel), github.com/KUIS-AI/cetvel
findings.numbers: 23 tasks / 7 categories / 22 datasets; 33 models up to 70B; CC BY-SA 4.0
findings.relevance: Directly parallels the Kazakh finding that SozKZ/from-scratch loses to general Qwen/Llama baselines — this is now a TWO-language pattern (Turkish AND Kazakh), making 'language-specific tuning alone underperforms general multilingual scale' a family-wide phenomenon worth citing in the atlas, not a Kazakh-specific anomaly.

findings.claim: [tr] TurkishMMLU (KUIS AI, ACL 2024 Findings) is the flagship Turkish knowledge benchmark: 10,032 questions (9,807 test + 225 dev), 9 subjects from Turkish high-school curricula. On the 900-question sub-benchmark at 5-shot: GPT-4o 83.1%, Claude-3 Opus 79.1%, Llama-3-70B-IT 67.3%, and the Turkish-adapted Trendyol-LLM-7B-chat-v1 only 34.1% — the weakest model tested, well below even much smaller general multilingual models like Aya-23-35B (55.6%).
findings.source: arXiv:2407.12402 (TurkishMMLU)
findings.numbers: 10,032 total (9,807 test/225 dev); 9 subjects; 5-shot 900-q subset: GPT-4o 83.1%, Claude-3-Opus 79.1%, Llama-3-70B-IT 67.3%, Trendyol-LLM-7B-C 34.1%, Aya-23-35B 55.6%
findings.relevance: Turkey's own dedicated 7B Turkish-tuned model (Trendyol) scoring worse than models 5-10x smaller (Aya-23 in relative terms) reinforces that instruction-tuning a strong multilingual base on Turkish text alone, without deeper adaptation (vocab extension, larger corpus), underperforms — informs the lab's Sherkala-style (vocab-extension) preference over naive fine-tuning.

findings.claim: [tr] A 2026 paper distills EmbeddingGemma-300M into a 200M Turkish-specialized embedder via tokenizer surgery (build 128K vocab: top-64K Turkish tokens from Cosmos Turkish Corpus + pruned teacher tokens + frequency-selected multilingual Wikipedia tokens) + weight-preserving embedding remapping (mean-composition of teacher embeddings) + offline distillation (cosine-similarity loss on 580K examples: 100K Turkish + 100K English + 10K/language across 40-language Wikipedia). Result: the 200M student BEATS its 300M teacher on Turkish STS (STSbTR Pearson 77.55% vs 73.84%, +3.71pp) at 33% fewer params, for $5-20 / ~4 A100-GPU-hours, but loses slightly on full TR-MTEB average (63.9% vs teacher's 65.2%, -1.3pp; task-specific gains of +4.6pp STS, +7.3pp NLI).
findings.source: arXiv:2605.29992 (Adapting Multilingual Embedding Models to Turkish via Cross-Lingual Tokenizer Surgery and Offline Distillation)
findings.numbers: 128K vocab (64K Turkish + pruned teacher + multilingual); 580K distillation examples; STSbTR 77.55/77.45 (student) vs 73.84/72.92 (teacher); TR-MTEB 63.9% vs 65.2%; cost $5-20, ~4 A100-hrs; 200M vs 300M params
findings.relevance: A genuinely portable, CHEAPER alternative/complement to the lab's Less-is-More recipe for Kazakh: tokenizer surgery + distillation from a strong multilingual teacher (e.g. EmbeddingGemma or mE5) is untested on Kazakh and could be run as an ablation alongside the 10k-noisy-pairs Less-is-More protocol — same budget class ($5-20).

findings.claim: [tr] TR-MTEB (EMNLP 2025 Findings, aclanthology 2025.findings-emnlp.471) built 34.2M weakly-supervised Turkish pairs across 26 datasets/6 task types (classification, clustering, pair-classification, retrieval, bitext-mining, STS) and confirms multilingual-e5-large remains the overall leader (highest Mean-Task/Mean-Type scores), while a narrower specialized model, TurkEmbed, reaches Turkish-specific SOTA on semantic tasks (STS Pearson 0.845 / Spearman 0.853) using roughly half the parameters of multilingual-e5-large-instruct — i.e. mE5 wins in aggregate but a lean specialized model can beat it on a task subset.
findings.source: aclanthology.org/2025.findings-emnlp.471 (TR-MTEB); arXiv:2511.08376 (TurkEmbed)
findings.numbers: 26 datasets, 6 task types, 34.2M weak pairs; TurkEmbed STS Pearson 0.845/Spearman 0.853 at ~half mE5-large-instruct's params; mE5-large leads TR-MTEB overall Mean(Task)/Mean(Type)
findings.relevance: Refines the KB's existing 'TR-MTEB: mE5 not surpassed' claim — it IS surpassed on STS specifically by a half-sized specialized model, so the lab's 'beat mE5-large on KazQAD' target should specify which task(s), since full-suite parity is the harder (and per Turkish evidence, still unbeaten) bar.

findings.claim: No pan-Turkic MTEB-style embedding/retrieval benchmark exists as of mid-2026: TR-MTEB (Turkish-only, 26 datasets) and the lab's planned kk-MTEB are both monolingual efforts; TUMLU (pan-Turkic, 8 languages) covers MMLU-style multiple-choice QA only, not embeddings/retrieval. No search turned up a 'Turkic-MTEB' or equivalent multi-language embedding suite.
findings.source: Search synthesis across aclanthology.org/2025.findings-emnlp.471, arXiv:2502.11020, and general web search for 'pan-Turkic MTEB'
findings.numbers: n/a (absence finding)
findings.relevance: Directly answers decision (3): a pan-Turkic-MTEB (using TR-MTEB's 6-task taxonomy as template, extended to kk/uz/az/ky at minimum) is unclaimed territory and would be a genuinely novel, adoptable lab artifact beyond the Kazakh-only kk-MTEB plan — natural collaboration surface with the live Uzbek offer.

findings.claim: Turkish NLP has four distinct institutional players with different strategies: KUIS AI (Koç University) builds EVALUATION infrastructure (Cetvel, TurkishMMLU) rather than models; Boğaziçi TABILAB builds both encoder (TabiBERT, ModernBERT-based, Dec 2025) and encoder-decoder (TURNA, 1.1B UL2/mT5-style, 43B tokens) foundation models; YTU COSMOS (TUBITAK-funded) builds from-scratch decoder SLMs (cosmosGPT 355M/774M) with rapid iteration (founded Jan 2024, shipped model within 2 months); VNGRS is a private company shipping the most resourced from-scratch efforts (VBART, Kumru-2B/300B tokens) with full open-sourcing including training corpora; Trendyol (e-commerce) does continual-PT of strong bases (Qwen2.5/Qwen3/Gemma3) for commercial chat/domain use, never from scratch.
findings.source: Synthesis of arXiv:2508.16431, huggingface.co/boun-tabi-LMG/TURNA, arXiv:2512.23065, arXiv:2404.17336, huggingface.co/vngrs-ai, huggingface.co/Trendyol
findings.numbers: TURNA 1.1B/43B tokens; TabiBERT (ModernBERT-based); cosmosGPT 355M/774M; Kumru-2B/300B tokens; Trendyol-LLM-8B-T1 on Qwen3-8B, 32K ctx
findings.relevance: Maps who to approach/cite for Uzbek-style collaboration playbooks: KUIS AI is the natural counterpart for Kazakh EVAL-protocol design (their Cetvel/TurkishMMLU methodology is directly reusable), VNGRS is the counterpart for from-scratch-SLM data-engineering practices (corpus release transparency), YTU COSMOS is the closest peer in team size/funding model to the lab itself.

findings.claim: [tr] Mukayese (ACL 2022 Findings, tdd-ai) remains the foundational Turkish NLP benchmarking platform — 18 baseline models across 8 tasks (spell-checking, sentence segmentation, LM, NLU) with 4 newly released benchmarking datasets — predating the 2024-26 wave of TurkishMMLU/Cetvel/TR-MTEB and establishing the 'benchmark-suite-per-language' template those later works followed.
findings.source: arXiv:2203.01215 (Mukayese)
findings.numbers: 18 baseline models, 8 tasks, 4 new datasets; ACL 2022 Findings
findings.relevance: Historical anchor showing Turkish's benchmark infrastructure build-out took ~4 years (Mukayese 2022 to Cetvel/TabiBERT 2025-26) — sets a realistic multi-year timeline expectation for the Kazakh atlas's own benchmark-maturity trajectory, not a one-paper sprint.

recommendations: For decision (1) — port target — prioritize Uzbek only for eval-protocol structure, NOT for raw data-availability assumptions: CulturaX shows Uzbek (75.25M tokens) is even more web-data-poor than Kazakh (2.80B tokens), a ~37x gap. Budget the Uzbek collaboration around synthetic/noisy-pair generation (Less-is-More style, 10k pairs) rather than assuming a Kazakh-scale web corpus exists to mine pairs from.

Adopt TR-MTEB's 6-task taxonomy (classification, clustering, pair-classification, retrieval, bitext-mining, STS) as the literal template for kk-MTEB rather than designing from scratch — it is the most mature Turkic-family precedent and was itself built to extend MMTEB; this also makes a future kk-MTEB directly comparable to TR-MTEB numbers.

Run the tokenizer-surgery + offline-distillation recipe (arXiv:2605.29992: 128K vocab surgery on a strong multilingual teacher + ~580K-example cosine distillation, $5-20/4 GPU-hrs) as a second embedding ablation alongside Less-is-More on Kazakh — it is cheaper, targets a different failure mode (vocabulary mismatch vs pair-noise), and beat its teacher on STS in the Turkish trial, which is untested for Kazakh's kk/ru code-switched Cyrillic case.

When citing 'Kazakh is behind Turkish', always specify the corpus: report BOTH the CulturaX ratio (~23x, tr 64.29B vs kk 2.80B tokens) and the XLM-R/CC ratio (5.8x) as distinct measurements — never average them; state which pipeline underlies each atlas figure.

Build the atlas's pan-Turkic resource table using CulturaX per-language token counts (tr 64.29B / az 3.51B / kk 2.80B / ky 501M / ug 77.7M / uz 75.25M) as the single consistent source for a same-corpus cross-Turkic comparison, supplementing with TUMLU's 5-shot accuracy numbers (tr 85.7/kk 83.0/az 84.4/crh 81.2/ky 75.7/ug 71.3/uz 69.1, Claude-3.5-Sonnet) as the outcome-side counterpart.

Flag a candidate lab artifact: a pan-Turkic-MTEB (extending TR-MTEB's task taxonomy to kk/uz/az/ky) is unclaimed as of mid-2026 and would out-scope a Kazakh-only kk-MTEB into a citable, collaboration-ready deliverable that directly leverages the live Uzbek offer — but only pursue after the ≥6-measured-result apparatus freeze lifts, per the lab's current apparatus-freeze rule.

Cite cosmosGPT (arXiv:2404.17336) and Cetvel's (arXiv:2508.16431) findings alongside SozKZ in the atlas/paper's related-work section as cross-Turkic corroboration that 'language-specific from-scratch/fine-tuned models underperform larger general multilingual models' is a family-wide pattern, strengthening the architectural-novelty (Engram) framing rather than relying on a single-language anecdote.
open_questions: Does TurkEmbed's task-specific STS win over mE5-large-instruct (arXiv:2511.08376) transfer to a RETRIEVAL-specific win anywhere in the Turkic family, or is mE5 retrieval-dominance (the axis the lab's KazQAD target cares about most) unbeaten everywhere in Turkic to date? Needs a direct fetch of TR-MTEB's per-task-type table (aclanthology 2025.findings-emnlp.471 full PDF) to confirm retrieval-specific numbers, not just the aggregate Mean(Task).

Is there a Belebele-tr exact score for any Turkish-adapted model comparable to Sherkala's Belebele-kk 30.6, to sanity-check whether Turkish's Belebele ceiling is proportionally higher given its larger corpus?

What are TabiBERT's exact benchmark deltas vs BERTurk (PDF extraction failed) — worth a follow-up fetch since it is the newest (Dec 2025) Turkish encoder and could be a stronger distillation teacher/reference than EmbeddingGemma for a kk encoder.
Does VNGRS's Kumru-2B open training corpus (500GB Turkish web text) get released with per-source breakdown comparable to SozKZ's 18-source recipe, enabling a direct data-recipe comparison?

research.area: turkic-uzbek — Non-Kazakh Turkic NLP landscape, Uzbek focus (with Turkish/pan-Turkic benchmark context), 2024-2026 emphasis

findings.claim: [uz] TahrirchiBERT-base: 110M-param encoder-only Transformer, 30,528-token byte-level BPE vocab, Latin script only, MLM objective. Trained on ~5B tokens from Uzbek Crawl (1.2M curated documents) + Uzbek Books (~4,000 preprocessed books), 1M steps, batch 512, seq len 512. Apache 2.0 license. No benchmark scores published on the model card as of this sweep ('paper coming soon').
findings.source: https://huggingface.co/tahrirchi/tahrirchi-bert-base
findings.numbers: 110M params, vocab 30,528, ~5B tokens, seq len 512, 1M steps, batch 512
findings.relevance: Direct Uzbek analog to SozKZ-scale monolingual pretraining; no reported downstream numbers means it cannot yet serve as a quantitative baseline for a joint kk/uz embedding effort — would need to be benchmarked first.

findings.claim: [uz] UzBERT (Mansurov & Mansurov, arXiv:2108.09814, 2021): 110M BERT-base (12 layers, 768 hidden, 12 heads), 30K WordPiece vocab, trained on Cyrillic-only news corpus of ~142M words (~1.9GB), MIT license. Massively outperforms mBERT on masked-LM accuracy: Top-1 match 64.06% vs 14.52% (news set), 32.25% vs 14.33% (encyclopedia set). No downstream task (NER/POS/QA) evaluation was possible at publication time because NO labeled Uzbek datasets existed at all.
findings.source: arXiv:2108.09814 (fetched PDF text directly)
findings.numbers: 110M params, 12L/768d/12h, vocab 30K, corpus 142M words / 1.9GB; MLM Top-1: UzBERT 64.06% vs mBERT 14.52% (news), 32.25% vs 14.33% (encyclopedia)
findings.relevance: Confirms Uzbek in 2021 had ZERO labeled downstream benchmarks (a starker starting point than Kazakh, which already had some NER/sentiment sets by then) — the resource gap direction (Uzbek behind Kazakh at t=2021) reverses somewhat by 2024-26 per TUMLU exam-difficulty findings below.

findings.claim: [uz] UzBERT paper explicitly documents Uzbek's dual-script reality: Cyrillic introduced 1956, Latin (re-)introduced 1995, both still coexist in real text; a dedicated ML-based Cyrillic-Latin-Cyrillic transliterator was built separately (Mansurov & Mansurov 2021, arXiv:2101.05162) precisely to bridge the script split for corpus building.
findings.source: arXiv:2108.09814 (fetched PDF text directly); arXiv:2101.05162 (cited, not independently fetched)
findings.numbers: Cyrillic since 1956; Latin since 1995
findings.relevance: Kazakh's Latin transition (~2031) is a future, planned, top-down event; Uzbek already lives the bi-script reality today and has a working transliteration tool as prior art the lab could adapt/cite when the kk Latin transition analysis is done.

findings.claim: [uz] Uzbek agglutination is demonstrated in the UzBERT paper as unbounded suffix chaining (e.g. уйдагилар -> уйдагилардигилар -> уйдагилардигилардагилар, each adding suffix -дагилар), explicitly flagged by the authors as harder than what a plain WordPiece/BPE tokenizer captures (e.g. менинг is kept as one token instead of stem мен + suffix нинг).
findings.source: arXiv:2108.09814 (fetched PDF text directly)
findings.numbers: n/a (qualitative, but load-bearing for tokenizer design)
findings.relevance: Same morphology class as Kazakh (agglutinative Turkic); no modern (2024-26) Uzbek tokenizer fertility number was found anywhere in this sweep — a genuine measurement gap the lab could fill with a joint kk/uz fertility comparison in the survey.

findings.claim: [uz] Behbudiy Labs (2024-2025, HF org 'behbudiy'): continual-pretrained + instruction-tuned Uzbek variants of Mistral-7B-Instruct, Mistral-Nemo-Instruct, and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct on 'over 5B Uzbek tokens' (mix of public + synthetic data), claiming '2x token efficiency vs global models' (no absolute fertility number given). Mistral-7B-Instruct-Uz vs base Mistral-7B-Instruct: FLORES+ BLEU Uz-En 7.47->29.39, En-Uz 0.67->16.77; COMET Uz-En 68.14->86.91, En-Uz 45.58->88.75; sentiment analysis 62.02%->79.13%; news classification 47.52%->59.38%; but English MMLU regressed 61.07%->55.72% (specialization tax). Apache 2.0.
findings.source: https://huggingface.co/behbudiy/Mistral-7B-Instruct-Uz
findings.relevance: Direct evidence of the same generative-target trade-off pattern the lab measures for Kazakh (Kazakh-specialization gains vs general-knowledge tax); no arXiv/technical report found, only HF model card, so the '2x token efficiency' and '5B tokens' claims are unverified beyond the card itself.

findings.claim: [uz][pan-turkic] UzLiB (Uzbek Linguistic Benchmark, github.com/tahrirchi/uzlib): MCQ benchmark testing Uzbek grammar/usage correctness, sourced from 4 Telegram quiz channels on Uzbek linguistics, manually verified and standardized, offered in both Cyrillic and Latin-converted forms with shuffled answer choices. Leaderboard (temp=1.0, top_p=0.95): Gemini 3 Pro Preview 0.8264, Gemini 3 Flash Preview 0.7953, Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview 0.7818, Claude 3.7 Sonnet 0.6513, DeepSeek-V4-Pro 0.6464, GPT-4o/GPT-5 range 0.6158-0.6319; human-voter baseline 0.5894; random-chance baseline 0.25; Llama-3.2-1B scores only 0.2332 (near/below chance).
findings.source: github.com/tahrirchi/uzlib (README + LEADERBOARD.md, fetched)
findings.numbers: Gemini 3 Pro 0.8264; Claude 3.7 Sonnet 0.6513; DeepSeek-V4-Pro 0.6464; human baseline 0.5894; random 0.25; Llama-3.2-1B 0.2332
findings.relevance: No sub-1B model clears even the random baseline on this native linguistics benchmark — confirms the same 'small models fail native-language competence tests' pattern the lab already sees on KazMMLU/TUMLU for Kazakh; exact question count could not be confirmed from accessible pages.

findings.claim: [uz][kk][az][tr][ky][tt][crh][kaa][ug] TUMLU (arXiv:2502.11020, ACL 2025) is a native (non-translated) MCQ benchmark across 9 Turkic languages with 38,139 total questions; TUMLU-mini per-language subset sizes: Kazakh 700, Uzbek 700, Azerbaijani 700, Turkish 700, Tatar 700, Kyrgyz 598, Uyghur 494, Crimean Tatar 316, Karakalpak 215. 7 core subjects: Biology, Chemistry, Geography, History, Mathematics, Native Language & Literature, Physics. 5-shot accuracy shows Kazakh consistently and substantially ABOVE Uzbek across every model tested: Claude 3.5 Sonnet 83.0% (kk) vs 69.1% (uz); GPT-4o 81.0% vs 65.4%; Gemini 1.5 Pro 78.4% vs 65.1%; Qwen2.5-72B 62.6% vs 50.4%; Llama-3.1-70B 56.4% vs 45.3% — an 11-16 percentage-point Kazakh advantage across all five frontier/large models.

findings.claim: [tr] TR-MTEB (Baysan & Güngör, Boğaziçi University, EMNLP 2025 Findings, aclanthology 2025.findings-emnlp.471) is the FIRST large-scale, task-diverse Turkish sentence-embedding benchmark: 26 datasets across 6 task types (8 classification, 2 clustering, 3 pair classification, 1 bitext mining, 1 STS, 11 retrieval — including 7 BEIR datasets machine-translated into Turkish via Cohere aya-expanse-8B, validated with an LLM-judge pipeline reaching 85.2% agreement with human labels, precision 92.9%, recall 84.4%, F1 88.4% on a 115-example calibration set).
findings.source: aclanthology.org/2025.findings-emnlp.471.pdf (fetched primary PDF pages 1-6 directly)
findings.numbers: 26 datasets, 6 task types (8/2/3/1/1/11), 7 BEIR sets translated, LLM-judge: 85.2% agreement, precision 92.9%, recall 84.4%, F1 88.4% (n=115 calibration examples)
findings.relevance: Directly answers decision 3 (pan-Turkic unclaimed territory): Turkish embedding-benchmark territory is ALREADY CLAIMED (published Nov 2025). Kazakh (kk-MTEB) and Uzbek MTEB-equivalents remain unclaimed as of this sweep — the lab's kk-MTEB plan is validated as still open, but should explicitly differentiate from/cite TR-MTEB rather than treat pan-Turkic MTEB as a fully greenfield idea.

findings.claim: [tr] TR-MTEB built a 34.2M-pair weakly-supervised Turkish sentence-pair training corpus (filtered down from 62.5M raw candidate pairs via a fine-tuned multilingual-e5-base filter model at a 0.4 cosine-similarity threshold, sourced from >50 public Turkish/translated/synthetic datasets), then contrastively pretrained + supervised fine-tuned both BERTurk-base and multilingual-e5-base. Results (Table 1, internal small-scale comparison): fine-tuned multilingual-e5-base scored Mean(Task)=62.73 / Mean(TaskType)=67.96, beating its own contrastive-pretrain-only checkpoint (57.77/65.92) and both BERTurk-base variants (uncased 53.62/53.38, cased 53.73/53.43).
findings.source: aclanthology.org/2025.findings-emnlp.471.pdf (fetched primary PDF, Table 1 read directly)
findings.numbers: corpus 34.2M pairs (from 62.5M raw, threshold 0.4); Mean(Task)/Mean(TaskType): mE5-base contrastive 57.77/65.92, mE5-base fine-tuned 62.73/67.96, BERTurk-uncased 53.62/53.38, BERTurk-cased 53.73/53.43
findings.relevance: This IS the lab's planned 'Less-is-More' mE5 continued-fine-tuning recipe, already executed and published for Turkish with exact numbers — a directly reusable methodology template (filter-then-contrastive-pretrain-then-supervised-finetune on mE5-base) for the kk/uz embedding pipeline, and independent validation that continued fine-tuning of mE5-base beats both the untouched mE5-base and from-scratch monolingual BERT encoders for a Turkic language.

findings.claim: [tr] TR-MTEB's own stated motivation mirrors the lab's kk-MTEB rationale exactly: 'At the time this work was initiated, the multilingual version of MTEB included only two datasets for classification and a single dataset for retrieval in Turkish' — i.e. even Turkish (the largest, best-resourced Turkic language) had near-zero native MTEB coverage before this 2025 paper.
findings.source: aclanthology.org/2025.findings-emnlp.471.pdf (fetched primary PDF, Section 1/3.1 read directly)
findings.numbers: pre-TR-MTEB multilingual-MTEB Turkish coverage: 2 classification datasets + 1 retrieval dataset
findings.relevance: Strong validating precedent for decision 3: the 'build a native MTEB extension' playbook is proven low-competition/high-value even for Turkish; Kazakh and Uzbek starting points are almost certainly still at or below that same near-zero baseline, so the lab's kk-MTEB PR plan is well-timed, not redundant.

recommendations: Decision 1 (protocol port order): Port the KazQAD-style retrieval protocol to Uzbek FIRST among non-Kazakh Turkic languages. Rationale: (a) no Uzbek open-domain QA/retrieval dataset with passage-level relevance judgments exists (confirmed absence finding above), so this is a genuine first, not a catch-up; (b) the Uzbek collaboration offer is live, giving native-speaker annotation capacity the lab lacks in-house; (c) FineWeb2 Uzbek corpus (~1.1B combined words) is workable scale, same order of magnitude as Kazakh's own starting corpus. Concretely: build 'UzQAD' mirroring KazQAD's construction (short-answer + passage-relevance judgments), but explicitly handle the Latin/Cyrillic split — either pick Latin as canonical (matches Uzbekistan's official 2023+ education-system direction) and transliterate the Cyrillic ~44% into it, or ship both, citing Mansurov & Mansurov 2021's Cyrillic-Latin-Cyrillic transliterator (arXiv:2101.05162) as the reusable bridging tool rather than building one from scratch.

Decision 1 (embedding recipe port): Replicate the TR-MTEB training recipe verbatim as the starting point for the kk-MTEB / qymyz-embed build, not just as inspiration: (a) collect native + machine-translated BEIR-style retrieval sets using an LLM translator (their choice: Cohere aya-expanse-8B) validated by an LLM-judge pipeline calibrated against ~100-150 human-annotated examples (they hit 85.2% agreement, F1 88.4% — use this as the target bar); (b) build a weakly-supervised sentence-pair corpus filtered via a fine-tuned mE5-base similarity threshold (they used 0.4 on 62.5M->34.2M pairs) rather than hand-curating pairs; (c) contrastively pretrain then supervised-fine-tune mE5-base specifically (not from-scratch monolingual encoders — their BERTurk-base variants scored ~10 points lower on Mean(TaskType) than fine-tuned mE5-base, replicating the lab's SozKZ-style 'from-scratch loses to adapted multilingual base' pattern already seen on the generative side).

Decision 2 (atlas positioning): Use the TUMLU 5-shot cross-Turkic table as the anchor comparison in the survey — it shows Kazakh AHEAD of Uzbek (83.0 vs 69.1 Claude 3.5 Sonnet; 11-16pp gap consistently across 5 frontier models), contradicting any naive 'Kazakh is the Central Asian laggard' framing. Pair this with the FineWeb2 word-count ratio (kk 1.837B vs uz ~1.109B combined, ~1.66x) as the resource-side explanation, but explicitly caveat with TUMLU's own finding that difficulty design (Uzbek/Turkish questions mimic university entrance exams) confounds a pure resource-ratio reading — do not present TUMLU scores as a clean resource proxy without this caveat.

Decision 2/3: Before writing the atlas's Turkic-family resource-ratio table, independently re-verify the TUMLU Table 2 numbers directly from the arXiv PDF (this sweep's extraction went through a WebFetch summarization pass, not raw text — flagged uncertain). Also independently verify the FineWeb2 word-count figures against the primary FineWeb2 dataset paper/card rather than the secondary web-search aggregation used here.

Decision 3 (unclaimed territory): Do NOT frame a Turkish-inclusive pan-Turkic MTEB as greenfield — TR-MTEB (EMNLP 2025 Findings) already claims that territory with 26 datasets and two trained embedding models. The lab's legitimate unclaimed slots are: (a) kk-MTEB specifically (Kazakh has near-zero native MTEB coverage, matching TR-MTEB's own pre-2025 Turkish baseline of '2 classification + 1 retrieval dataset'); (b) a comparable Uzbek MTEB extension (uz-MTEB), which appears equally unclaimed and could be a joint deliverable with the live Uzbek collaborator, positioning the lab as having built BOTH the Kazakh and Uzbek native-MTEB extensions using one shared recipe — a stronger 'force-of-adoption' artifact than either alone.

Track SIGTURK 2026 (held 2026-03-29, ACL Anthology 2026.sigturk-1) proceedings directly before any Kazakh/Uzbek benchmark publication to rule out a concurrent/duplicate submission; this is the active recurring venue for this exact research niche.
Flag 'tomaris.ai' as unconfirmed in the competitor ledger (competitor-saken-tukenov.md-style tracking) pending a direct primary source — this sweep found zero evidence of the entity under that name.

research.area: turkic-kyrgyz (non-Kazakh Turkic NLP landscape — Kyrgyz extreme low-resource case, Uzbek comparison, pan-Turkic tooling)

findings.claim: [ky] KyrgyzBERT is the first published monolingual Kyrgyz BERT: 35.9M params, custom WordPiece tokenizer (vocab 30,522), hidden 512, 8 attention heads, 6 layers, trained from scratch on a PRIVATE corpus of >1.5M Kyrgyz sentences on a single RTX 3090. Fine-tuned on kyrgyz-sst2 (SST-2 translated + manually-annotated gold test set of 1,821 sentences) it reaches weighted F1 0.8280 vs fine-tuned mBERT (177M) 0.8401 — only 1.2pp gap at 5x fewer params. Zero-shot base models are near-random: mBERT F1 0.3509, XLM-R F1 0.3221.
findings.source: arXiv:2511.20182 (Metinov, Kudakeeva, Kabaeva, KSTU Bishkek, Nov 2025)
findings.numbers: 35.9M params; vocab 30,522; hidden 512; 6L/8H; >1.5M sentences private corpus; kyrgyzbert_sst2 F1 0.8280 vs mbert-kyrgyz-sst2-finetuned F1 0.8401 (177M); zero-shot mBERT F1 0.3509, XLM-R F1 0.3221
findings.relevance: Directly analogous small-scale case: a 35.9M compact monolingual encoder nearly matches a 5x-larger multilingual model on Kyrgyz sentiment — supports the lab's own bet that a small purpose-built model can be competitive with big multilingual baselines on a Kipchak Turkic language. Also a template for a Kyrgyz-analog benchmark the lab could reuse/extend.

findings.claim: [ky] KyrText (2026) is the largest consolidated Kyrgyz corpus to date: 680.5M words (2.33M documents) aggregated from News (61.4%, 1.9M docs), Court decisions (23.9%, 172.8K docs), Legislation (9.9%, 157K docs), Wikipedia (1.3%, Nov-20-2025 dump), and E-library/OCR'd literature (3.45%, using DeepSeek-OCR). Used for continual pretraining of mBERT/XLM-R-base/large/DeBERTaV3 and RoBERTa-from-scratch; best model xlm-roberta-large-kgz scores BoolQ 0.79, PAWS-X 0.85, XNLI 0.76, News-topic 0.92, SST 0.89 (all accuracy), a 7-19pp gain over the un-adapted xlm-roberta-large baseline.
findings.source: ACL Anthology 2026.loreslm-1.39 (Chubakov, LoResLM 2026 workshop)
findings.numbers: 680.5M words total; 2,334,281 docs; SentencePiece Unigram tokenizer vocab 64,000; xlm-roberta-large-kgz: BoolQ 0.79 (+7pp), PAWS-X 0.85 (+18pp), XNLI 0.76 (+19pp) vs base xlm-roberta-large
findings.relevance: Gives a concrete Kyrgyz-scale ceiling (680.5M words ≈ under 1B tokens) for what a from-scratch/continual-PT Kyrgyz effort can currently draw on — roughly an order of magnitude below the lab's own ~9-10B Kazakh token target, useful as a lower calibration point for the 'how much data does X Turkic language have' comparison table.

findings.claim: [ky][kk] The KyrText paper explicitly documents that Kazakh/Kyrgyz splits of major multilingual pretraining corpora (OSCAR, mC4, CulturaX) are cross-contaminated: 'a large ratio of the texts included in the Kyrgyz splits of these datasets is actually in other languages — predominantly in Kazakh,' attributed to poor langID performance on the two languages, which 'share a large common vocabulary.'
findings.source: ACL Anthology 2026.loreslm-1.39, Section 2.1
findings.numbers: qualitative finding, no contamination % given [UNVERIFIED extent]
findings.relevance: DIRECT actionable risk for the lab's own Kazakh corpus: any CulturaX/mC4/OSCAR-derived Kazakh training data likely contains uncounted Kyrgyz contamination, which would corrupt vocabulary/perplexity and dilute the from-scratch tokenizer's fertility advantage. Recommend adding an explicit kk-vs-ky binary classifier pass (not generic langID) to the lab's own data-cleaning pipeline.

findings.claim: [kk][ky][uz] CulturaX per-language token counts for the three Central Asian languages: Kazakh 2,802,485,195 tokens (2,733,982 docs); Kyrgyz 501,442,620 tokens (570,922 docs); Uzbek 75,250,787 tokens (87,219 docs) — i.e. Kazakh has 5.6x Kyrgyz's tokens and 37.2x Uzbek's, in this specific corpus.

findings.numbers: kk 2.80B tok / 2.73M docs; ky 501M tok / 571K docs; uz 75.25M tok / 87.2K docs; kk:ky ratio 5.6x; kk:uz ratio 37.2x

BUT the Uzbek figure is suspiciously low given Uzbekistan's 34M population and should be checked for script-code artifacts (CulturaX may register only one script variant under 'uz').

findings.claim: [kk][ky][ba] In a 2026 Turkic MT shared-task paper, ORIGINAL (non-synthetic) parallel training data sizes were: Russian-Kazakh 367,095 samples, Russian-Kyrgyz 35,429 samples, Russian-Bashkir 1,190,773 samples — i.e. Kazakh has 10.4x more original RU-parallel data than Kyrgyz, and Bashkir (a non-state, autonomous-republic language) has 33.6x more than Kyrgyz and 3.2x more than Kazakh.
findings.source: arXiv:2602.04442 (Karpov, 'No One-Size-Fits-All', Feb 2026)
findings.numbers: ru-kk 367,095 train / 9,845 val; ru-ky 35,429 train / 4,845 val; ru-ba 1,190,773 train / 9,997 val; kk:ky ratio 10.4x
findings.relevance: Gives a second, independent-of-CulturaX resource-ratio datapoint (parallel-corpus axis rather than monolingual-web axis) confirming Kazakh's mid-tier lead over Kyrgyz among Kipchak Turkic languages — useful cross-check for the atlas's 'who is ahead on what axis' table.

findings.claim: [kk][ky][ba][tt][cv] Same paper: for the better-resourced languages (Kazakh, Bashkir) fine-tuning NLLB-200-distilled-600M with LoRA/DoRA beat zero-shot LLM prompting (Kazakh chrF++ 49.93 LoRA vs 47.54 best zero-shot MiMoV2; Bashkir 49.53 LoRA vs 41.59 zero-shot). For Kyrgyz, the pattern INVERTS: zero-shot LLM prompting (MiMoV2 46.61, submitted result 45.61 chrF++) beat NLLB fine-tuning (LoRA only 36.29, single-task fine-tune 27.04) — fine-tuning on Kyrgyz's smaller pretraining allocation could not catch up to a frontier LLM's zero-shot multilingual knowledge.
findings.source: arXiv:2602.04442, Table 1 & Table 2
findings.numbers: Kazakh: LoRA 49.93 > zero-shot best 47.54; Bashkir: LoRA 49.53 > zero-shot 41.59. Kyrgyz: LoRA 36.29 < zero-shot MiMoV2 46.61 (final submission chrF++ 45.61)
findings.relevance: Signals a resource-crossover threshold: below some pretraining-data floor, adapting a dedicated MT model underperforms just prompting a frontier LLM — evidence that Kyrgyz sits below that floor while Kazakh sits above it. Relevant when the lab decides whether a from-scratch/continual-PT strategy is even worth it for a target language before porting the recipe.

findings.claim: [kk][ky] LaBSE nominally supports both Kazakh and Kyrgyz, but the same paper notes that stacking translations by LaBSE cosine-similarity 'led to a minor deterioration' and cites prior work that 'the quality of the multilingual BERT on any given language is strongly correlated with the size of the pretraining data' — i.e. LaBSE's Kyrgyz embeddings are lower-fidelity than its Kazakh embeddings purely due to pretraining-data imbalance, not architecture.
findings.source: arXiv:2602.04442, Section 6 (citing Karpov & Burtsev 2023)
findings.numbers: qualitative; LaBSE-based reranking underperformed single-model baseline for both kk and ky [UNVERIFIED exact delta]
findings.relevance: Warns that reusing an off-the-shelf multilingual embedder (LaBSE, mE5, BGE-M3) for a Kyrgyz-analog retrieval eval will likely show a bigger multilingual-vs-dedicated gap than the lab already measured for Kazakh (mE5-large on KazQAD), because Kyrgyz's pretraining allocation in these encoders is smaller still.

findings.claim: [ky] Apertium-kir provides a 'Stable'-quality finite-state morphological analyzer/generator (Kymorph) for Kyrgyz built with HFST, originally developed for a Turkish→Kyrgyz MT prototype, and Apertium ships a dedicated apertium-kaz-kir bidirectional Kazakh↔Kyrgyz translation pair (leveraging the two languages' high mutual intelligibility).
findings.source: wiki.apertium.org/wiki/Apertium-kir; github.com/apertium/apertium-kir; github.com/apertium/apertium-kaz-kir
findings.numbers: qualitative (no error-rate numbers published)
findings.relevance: Confirms rule-based morphological tooling for Kyrgyz already exists and is architecturally compatible with Kazakh's own Apertium morphology work — a cheap starting point if the lab ever wants a morphology-aware tokenizer ablation ported to Kyrgyz.

findings.claim: [ky][kk][az][uz][tt][ug][kaa] TUMLU-mini (already in KB) covers Kyrgyz among its 8 natively-authored Turkic languages (38,139 4-choice questions, 11 subjects); no ≤1B model has been evaluated on it and the Kazakh subset (700 Q) tops out at Gemma-2-9B 49.1 among small-open models — Kyrgyz-specific per-language scores were not extracted in this sweep and should be pulled from the full leaderboard table before using as a design input.
findings.source: arXiv:2502.11020 (TUMLU, 2025) — extending KB entry
findings.numbers: 8 Turkic langs, 11 subjects, 38,139 Qs total; Kazakh subset 700 Q, best small-open Gemma-2-9B 49.1
findings.relevance: TUMLU is the one pan-Turkic knowledge benchmark already claiming cross-lingual generative-eval territory; the lab should check whether its Kyrgyz subset is large/clean enough to reuse instead of building a bespoke Kyrgyz MC-QA set.

findings.claim: [ky][kk][uz][ug][tt][ba][az][tr][sah][alt][tyv][kjh][chv][kaa][nog][krc][crh][gag][tk] TurkicNLP is a 2026 unified toolkit covering 24 Turkic languages (Oghuz/Kipchak/Karluk/Siberian/Oghur/historical branches) offering tokenization, morphology, POS/dependency parsing, NER, transliteration, cross-lingual embeddings, and MT via one API. For Kyrgyz specifically: Apertium FST morphology ('Stable', 60% sentence-detection, 100% analysis coverage, 76% feature coverage), Stanza/Glot500 POS+parsing (79.0% UPOS, 63.8% UAS, 40.9% LAS), Cyrillic+transliteration, NLLB-200 embeddings/MT — but NO NER support, unlike Kazakh which has KazNERD-backed NER and clearly stronger parsing (88.8% UPOS, 71.5% UAS).
findings.source: arXiv 2602.19174v4 (TurkicNLP toolkit, Hakimov et al.)
findings.numbers: Kyrgyz: 60% morph detection, 100%/76% analysis/feature coverage, 79.0% UPOS/63.8% UAS/40.9% LAS, no NER. Kazakh: 88.8% UPOS/71.5% UAS, has NER (KazNERD)
findings.relevance: Directly answers decision (3): a broad pan-Turkic TOOLING umbrella already exists (24 languages, unified API) so a 'yet another Turkic toolkit' artifact has no unclaimed territory — but it explicitly has NO embedding/retrieval benchmark layer, confirming that axis remains open for a lab contribution (Turkic-MTEB-mini).

findings.claim: [ky] Independent scientometric review of Kyrgyz NLP identifies the field as 'Scraping By' (severely under-resourced tier) based on analysis of 67 research works since 2011; existing corpora are fragmented: Manas-UdS (1.2M words, 84 literary texts), kyWaC (19M words, crawled Jan 2012), Leipzig Corpora Collection (news+community crawls, 'hundreds of thousands' of sentences), and TilCorpusu (reported variously as ~100M or 300M words, made public 2023) — no single consolidated large corpus existed until KyrText (2026).
findings.source: arXiv:2411.05503 (KyrgyzNLP: Challenges, Progress, and Future, 2024)
findings.numbers: 67 papers reviewed since 2011; Manas-UdS 1.2M words; kyWaC 19M words; TilCorpusu 100M words (one description) OR 300M words (conflicting description) [UNVERIFIED which is correct]
findings.relevance: Confirms Kyrgyz's fragmentation problem pre-2026 — the field lacked a single go-to corpus, which is why KyrText (680.5M words) is a meaningful step-change and why the lab should treat any pre-2026 Kyrgyz numbers with caution.

findings.claim: [ky][kk][tt][ug][uz][alt] Lexical similarity (Swadesh 215-word list) of Kyrgyz to sibling Turkic languages: Kazakh 91%, Tatar 79%, Uyghur 77%, Uzbek 76%, Altai 73%. Also: a single Kyrgyz verb can take 'thousands' of inflected forms vs a maximum of ~150 for a Russian verb.
findings.source: arXiv:2411.05503 (KyrgyzNLP challenges paper)
findings.numbers: Kazakh 91%, Tatar 79%, Uyghur 77%, Uzbek 76%, Altai 73% lexical similarity to Kyrgyz; Kyrgyz verb forms 'thousands' vs Russian ~150
findings.relevance: The 91% Kazakh-Kyrgyz lexical similarity is the single number that explains BOTH the langID-contamination problem (finding above) AND why cross-lingual transfer experiments (KB: 'Left Behind' arXiv 2603.21036) show Aya Expanse emitting Kyrgyz output for Kazakh prompts — it is the highest cross-language similarity in the whole family, making kk<->ky the most transfer-prone AND most contamination-prone pair the lab will encounter.

findings.claim: [ky] KyrgyzNER is the first manually-annotated Kyrgyz NER dataset: 1,499 news articles (24.KG portal), 10,900 sentences, 39,075 entity mentions across 27 entity classes. Multilingual RoBERTa variants achieved the best precision/recall balance in baseline evaluations; all tested models struggled on rare entity categories.
findings.source: arXiv:2509.19109 (Human-Annotated NER Dataset for the Kyrgyz Language, Sept 2025)
findings.numbers: 1,499 articles; 10,900 sentences; 39,075 entities; 27 classes
findings.relevance: Fills the TurkicNLP-toolkit-identified gap ('Kyrgyz: NER not available') at the dataset level (2025), though no production model/toolkit integration confirmed yet — worth checking before assuming Kyrgyz NER is a greenfield opportunity.

findings.claim: [ky] Kyrgyz Wikipedia has 76,170 article pages as of March 2026.
findings.source: Wikidata Q60799 (via WebSearch, March 2026 snapshot)
findings.numbers: 76,170 articles
findings.relevance: Direct input for building a Kyrgyz Wikipedia-grounded retrieval eval (KazQAD analog): article count is roughly on the same order as many low-resource-language Wikipedias used for FLORES/Belebele/SIB — sufficient scale for a small retrieval benchmark but far below Kazakh Wikipedia's size (needs separate check, not sourced this sweep).

findings.claim: [ky][kk][az][uz][tt][ug][kaa][crh] FLORES-200, SIB-200, and Belebele all include Kyrgyz (kir_Cyrl) natively as one of their 200+/205/122 covered languages/variants, meaning the KazQAD-style retrieval and MTEB-style classification protocols the lab already pins for Kazakh are directly reusable on Kyrgyz text with ZERO additional annotation — the same FLORES-200 passages underlie SIB-200 (topic classification) and Belebele (reading-comprehension MCQ).
findings.source: SIB-200 (arXiv 2309.07445 / EACL 2024); FLORES-200 GitHub README (facebookresearch/flores); Belebele HF card
findings.numbers: FLORES-200: 842 web articles, 3,001 sentences per language incl. kir_Cyrl; SIB-200: 205 langs/dialects; Belebele: 122 variants
findings.relevance: This is the concrete evidence for decision (1): Kyrgyz is 'free' to add to the lab's evallab classification/reading-comprehension suite (no new annotation), but retrieval specifically (KazQAD-analog passage-retrieval, not just topic-classification) has NO existing Kyrgyz benchmark — that gap must be built from scratch (e.g. from the 76,170-article Kyrgyz Wikipedia) if Kyrgyz retrieval is prioritized.

findings.claim: [kir_cyrl][kaz_cyrl][tat_cyrl][bak_cyrl][rus_cyrl][tur_latn][azj_latn] (already in KB, cross-checked) Kyrgyz's Cyrillic byte premium (1.964) is slightly WORSE than Kazakh's (1.765/1.76), and both are far worse than Latin-script Turkic (Turkish 1.044, Azerbaijani 1.076) — consistent with the byte-premium-explains-most-of-the-morphology-gap finding (KB: arXiv 2411.14198).
findings.source: catherinearnett/byte-premium-tool (KB digest, cross-referenced against this sweep's sources)
findings.numbers: kir_cyrl 1.964; kaz_cyrl 1.765-1.76; tat_cyrl 1.855; bak_cyrl 2.272; rus_cyrl 1.823; tur_latn 1.044; azj_latn 1.076
findings.relevance: Kyrgyz sits marginally worse than Kazakh on the tokenization-cost axis despite having less than 1/5 the CulturaX token volume — meaning any Kyrgyz from-scratch model would face a compounded disadvantage (worse byte premium AND far less data) relative to the lab's Kazakh effort, a useful 'why Kazakh-first, not Kyrgyz-first' argument for the atlas.

findings.claim: [uz] Uzbek has a comparatively mature encoder-model ecosystem: UzBERT (2021, MIT license, outperforms mBERT on Uzbek MLM accuracy), UzRoBERTa (pretrained on ~2M Uzbek news articles), BERTbek (2024, Latin-script-focused, improves on UzBERT; BERTbek-News-Big reaches 92.25% F1 on sentiment, beating both mBERT and UzBERT), plus UzLiB (Uzbek Linguistic Benchmark, sourced from Telegram grammar-quiz channels, manually verified) from the Tahrirchi/uzlm commercial AI ecosystem.
findings.source: arXiv:2108.09814 (UzBERT); aclanthology.org/2024.sigul-1.5 (BERTbek); github.com/tahrirchi/uzlib; huggingface.co/uzlm
findings.numbers: BERTbek-News-Big sentiment F1 92.25%; UzRoBERTa ~2M news articles pretraining
findings.relevance: Directly informs decision (1): despite CulturaX showing Uzbek with the LOWEST raw token count of the three (75.25M, likely undercounted), Uzbek has the MOST mature applied ecosystem (multiple BERT variants, a commercial AI company (Tahrirchi) actively building tools, its own linguistic benchmark) — resource maturity and raw corpus size diverge for Uzbek, unlike Kyrgyz where both are low. This supports prioritizing the live Uzbek collaboration for embedding-recipe porting on ecosystem-readiness grounds, not corpus-size grounds.

findings.claim: [ky] The WMT25 Open Language Data Initiative received a dedicated 'Kyrgyz Seed Dataset' submission from a multi-institution Central Asian team (incl. authors credited with Manas-UdS/Kasieva lineage), explicitly framed as expanding MT resources for an underrepresented FLORES-adjacent language — but exact sentence/token counts and quality metrics were not extractable from the PDF in this sweep.
findings.source: aclanthology.org/2025.wmt-1.84.pdf (WMT25 proceedings)
findings.numbers: not extracted [UNVERIFIED — size/BLEU/chrF numbers unavailable from this pass]
findings.relevance: Signals active 2025-2026 institutional interest in expanding Kyrgyz open MT data via the same WMT/FLORES ecosystem the lab already tracks for Kazakh — worth a follow-up primary-source read if Kyrgyz porting becomes concrete, since it may supply exactly the kind of small parallel seed corpus needed for a retrieval-negative-mining recipe.

recommendations: Decision 1 (protocol porting order): Port the KazQAD-style retrieval + Less-is-More embedding recipe to Uzbek FIRST (live collaboration + more mature applied ecosystem: UzBERT/UzRoBERTa/BERTbek/Tahrirchi/UzLiB), but before committing eval budget, verify Uzbek's TRUE monolingual corpus size independently of CulturaX's 75.25M-token 'uz' figure, which is almost certainly a script-code undercount (Uzbek is majority-Latin since ~1993/2019 reforms; CulturaX's language tag may miss the dominant script variant).

Port to Kyrgyz SECOND, leveraging the fact that FLORES-200/SIB-200/Belebele already include kir_Cyrl natively — the classification/reading-comprehension side of evallab's protocol needs zero new annotation for Kyrgyz. The retrieval side (KazQAD-analog passage retrieval) has NO existing Kyrgyz benchmark and must be built from scratch, most cheaply from the 76,170-article Kyrgyz Wikipedia (same scaffolding KazQAD used for Kazakh).

Before reusing ANY CulturaX/mC4/OSCAR Kazakh split for the lab's own corpus, add an explicit binary kk-vs-ky classifier pass (not generic langID) — KyrText (2026.loreslm-1.39) documents that these corpora's Kyrgyz splits are heavily contaminated with Kazakh text due to 91% lexical similarity, and the same failure mode very likely runs the other direction into the lab's Kazakh data.

For the atlas/survey's resource-ratio table (decision 2), use TWO independent axes rather than one: (a) CulturaX monolingual tokens — kk 2.80B : ky 501M : uz 75.25M(caveat script-undercount); (b) original parallel MT data — ru-kk 367,095 : ru-ky 35,429 samples (10.4x gap), cross-checked against a Bashkir reference (1,190,773, 3.2x above Kazakh) to show Kazakh is mid-tier, not top-tier, among Kipchak Turkic languages.

Cite the fine-tuning-vs-zero-shot crossover finding (arXiv 2602.04442) explicitly in any design-panel discussion of 'should we continual-PT vs just prompt a frontier LLM for language X': Kazakh and Bashkir cross a data-sufficiency threshold where dedicated fine-tuning wins; Kyrgyz does not yet cross it (zero-shot LLM prompting beats NLLB LoRA fine-tuning, 45.6 vs 36.3 chrF++) — use this as a go/no-go heuristic before spending compute on a from-scratch Kyrgyz or Uzbek run.

Decision 3 (pan-Turkic benchmark gap): do NOT build another general Turkic tokenization/morphology/POS toolkit — TurkicNLP (arXiv 2602.19174) already unifies 24 languages across that whole stack. The genuinely unclaimed territory is embedding/retrieval: propose a 'Turkic-MTEB-mini' built from FLORES-200-derived passages (already covering kir_Cyrl, kaz_Cyrl, uzn_Latn, tur_Latn, aze_Latn, tat_Cyrl, bak_Cyrl, and more) with Kazakh positioned as the flagship/reference language via the lab's own KazQAD work — this is the one artifact type with force-of-adoption upside noted nowhere else in the 2025-2026 literature surveyed.

Do not treat TilCorpusu's size as settled (conflicting 100M vs 300M word descriptions found in secondary sources) — if the atlas cites it, resolve via the primary TilCorpusu release page before publication.

Flag the KyrgyzBERT (35.9M, WordPiece 30,522 vocab) result as a useful small-model precedent to cite in the paper's related-work section alongside SozKZ: it demonstrates a <40M monolingual encoder nearly matching a 5x-larger multilingual baseline on a sibling low-resource agglutinative Turkic language, reinforcing (not contradicting) the lab's small-model thesis — but note it is an ENCODER (BERT-style, sentiment classification), not a generative/decoder model, so it is not directly comparable to the SozKZ/Qwen3-0.6B KazMMLU line of evidence.
open_questions: What is Uzbek's TRUE monolingual pretraining corpus size in the dominant Latin script? CulturaX's 'uz' tag (75.25M tokens) is suspiciously low relative to Uzbekistan's ~34M population and looks like a script-coverage artifact — needs a direct check of CulturaX's uz_Latn vs uz_Cyrl (if split) or a cross-check against mC4/HPLT Uzbek figures.

Does a Kyrgyz-analog of KazQAD (bespoke passage-retrieval benchmark, not just SIB-200/Belebele classification) exist anywhere in 2025-2026 literature? This sweep found none — needs a dedicated confirmation search (HF datasets, GitHub, Kyrgyz university theses) before the design-panel assumes it must be built from scratch.

TilCorpusu's actual word count: is it ~100M (July 2023 release, News-only due to legal restriction) or ~300M (December 2023, full release)? Two secondary sources disagree; resolve via the corpus's own release notes/HF page.

What does the WMT25 Kyrgyz Seed Dataset actually contain (sentence count, domains, quality metrics)? The PDF text extraction failed in this sweep for the numeric tables — worth a follow-up read if Kyrgyz MT/retrieval-negative-mining is prioritized.
Kazakh Wikipedia's exact article count was not re-verified in this sweep (only Kyrgyz's 76,170 was pulled) — needed to complete the Wikipedia-size ratio in the atlas table.

Is there a published Turkic-MTEB or kk-MTEB-adjacent embedding leaderboard already in progress by any group (e.g. via the TUMLU or TurkicNLP authors) that would make the proposed 'Turkic-MTEB-mini' redundant rather than novel? Not found in this sweep but worth one more targeted search before committing lab resources.

research.area: turkic-other-langs (non-Kazakh Turkic NLP landscape, Kazakh as comparison anchor only)

findings.claim: [pan-turkic] TUMLU (ACL Findings/arXiv:2502.11020, native-authored MCQA, 38,139 Qs, 11 subjects, 8 languages: Azerbaijani/aze, Crimean Tatar/crh, Karakalpak/kaa, Kazakh/kaz, Kyrgyz/kir, Tatar/tat, Turkish/tur, Uzbek/uzb) gives the only cross-Turkic ranking with exact per-language scores. 5-shot mean accuracy ranking (Claude 3.5 Sonnet): tur 85.7 > aze 84.4 > tat 84.0 > kaz 83.0 > crh 81.2 > kir 75.7 > kaa 75.3 > uig 71.3 > uzb 69.1 (mean 78.9). For the SMALLEST open model tested (Llama-3.1-8B), Kazakh is the SINGLE HIGHEST-scoring language (46.4, mean 40.3), and Gemma-2-9B also puts Kazakh above its own mean (49.1 vs 47.1) — i.e. Kazakh's relative advantage concentrates in the small/mid model regime, not the frontier regime where Azerbaijani/Turkish/Tatar lead.
findings.source: arXiv:2502.11020v2 (TUMLU), Table 2, fetched directly
findings.numbers: Claude 3.5 Sonnet per-lang: aze 84.4, crh 81.2, kaa 75.3, kaz 83.0, kir 75.7, tat 84.0, tur 85.7, uig 71.3, uzb 69.1 (mean 78.9). Llama-3.1-8B: aze 48.4, crh 35.7, kaa 33.7, kaz 46.4 (HIGHEST), kir 41.8, tat 44.1, tur 47.7, uig 35.0, uzb 29.9 (mean 40.3). Gemma-2-9B: kaz 49.1 vs mean 47.1.
findings.relevance: Directly answers decision (2): quantifies exactly where Kazakh sits in the Turkic family, and shows its comparative edge is strongest precisely in the ≤~9B open-model regime the lab's ≤600M model is adjacent to — a defensible, sourced atlas claim ('best-learnable mid/small-model Turkic language') rather than a vague ranking.

findings.claim: [uz][az][kaz][crh][kaa][ug] FineWeb2 script/word counts per language (as reported inside the TUMLU paper) give a directly comparable resource ladder: Kazakh 1,837,049,585 Cyrillic words / 0 Latin (100% Cyrillic); Uzbek 616,563,348 Latin + 492,264,125 Cyrillic (≈1.109B total, ≈56%/44% split); Crimean Tatar 21,365,608 Latin + 1,934,168 Cyrillic (≈23.3M total, 11:1 Latin:Cyrillic). Uyghur has ~0 presence in FineWeb2 (virtually all Uyghur text is Arabic-script, outside this corpus's script coverage).
findings.source: arXiv:2502.11020v2 (TUMLU), Section 5 body text, citing Penedo et al. 2024 FineWeb2
findings.numbers: kaz 1.837B (100% Cyr); uzb 616.6M Latin + 492.3M Cyr = 1.109B; crh 21.37M Latin + 1.93M Cyr = 23.3M
findings.relevance: Decision (2): gives an exact, sourced resource-ratio ladder (kaz ≈1.7x uzb ≈79x crh) for the atlas's 'who is ahead on data volume' axis, using one single corpus so the comparison is apples-to-apples (unlike mixing curated corpora of different provenance).

findings.claim: [uz] Uzbek is the WORST- or near-worst-performing language in TUMLU across nearly every model tested despite having more raw web text (FineWeb2 ≈1.1B words) than Kazakh's dedicated slice methodology would predict, and despite Tahrirchi's TahrirchiBERT being trained on ~5B tokens. This is consistent with Uzbek text being split roughly 56%/44% between Latin and Cyrillic scripts (vs Kazakh's ~100% Cyrillic concentration), which may fragment effective per-script training signal even though total-language volume is large.
findings.source: arXiv:2502.11020v2 Table 2 (Claude 3.5 Sonnet uzb 69.1, lowest of 8; Qwen2.5-72B uzb 44.1, lowest; Llama-3.1-8B uzb 29.9, lowest); TahrirchiBERT 5B-token claim via web search of Tahrirchi HF/GitHub pages
findings.numbers: uzb lowest in 3 of 4 models shown in Table 2 mean row context; FineWeb2 Uzbek Latin/Cyrillic split 616.6M/492.3M words
findings.relevance: Directly informs decision (1): before porting the pinned eval protocols/Less-is-More recipe to Uzbek for the live collaboration, the script-split confound (not code-switching, which is Kazakh's issue) should be isolated — recommend a controlled ablation (Cyrillic-only vs Latin-only vs mixed Uzbek fine-tune) rather than assuming the Kazakh kk/ru code-switch lesson transfers as-is.

findings.claim: [crh] Crimean Tatar's script-performance pattern is the OPPOSITE of Kazakh's and offers the closest available empirical natural-experiment for Kazakh's pending 2031 Latin transition: Crimean Tatar (FineWeb2: 21.37M Latin words vs only 1.93M Cyrillic, 11:1 ratio) scores markedly HIGHER when queried in Latin script (Claude 80.0 vs Cyrillic 66.1, a 13.9pp gap; Qwen2.5-72B 61.8 Latin vs 47.6 Cyrillic, 14.2pp; Gemma-2-27B 49.8 Latin vs 43.5 Cyrillic). Kazakh shows the mirror-image but SMALLER gap favoring Cyrillic (its dominant script today): Claude 82.7 Cyr vs 78.0 Latin (4.7pp); Qwen2.5-72B 64.3 Cyr vs 54.1 Latin (10.2pp); Gemma-2-27B 58.5 Cyr vs 46.3 Latin (12.2pp).
findings.source: arXiv:2502.11020v2 Table 6, fetched directly
findings.numbers: Crimean Tatar: Claude Latin 80.0/Cyr 66.1; Qwen72B Latin 61.8/Cyr 47.6; Gemma27B Latin 49.8/Cyr 43.5. Kazakh: Claude Cyr 82.7/Latin 78.0; Qwen72B Cyr 64.3/Latin 54.1; Gemma27B Cyr 58.5/Latin 46.3
findings.relevance: Decision (2)/atlas: quantifies the real accuracy tax Kazakh should expect on Latin-script queries even TODAY (5-12pp, despite near-zero Latin web presence, via generalization/transliteration) and gives a same-family reference point (Crimean Tatar's 14pp Latin-favoring gap) for forecasting how large the transition-era penalty could grow before web corpora rebalance post-2031.

findings.claim: [pan-turkic] The TUMLU paper's own text states 'TUMLU covers 8 Turkic languages... some major Turkic languages, such as Turkmen, Kyrgyz and Bashkir are not included' — but Kyrgyz (kir) demonstrably IS one of the 8 languages with full results throughout the paper's tables. This is an internal inconsistency in the source paper (likely a drafting error), not a lab measurement error.
findings.source: arXiv:2502.11020v2, 'Missing major languages' paragraph vs Table 2/Figure 1
findings.numbers: n/a — textual contradiction: Kyrgyz appears in Table 2 (kir column, e.g. Claude 75.7) despite being listed as excluded
findings.relevance: Flag so the atlas doesn't propagate this contradiction; Turkmen and Bashkir ARE genuinely absent from TUMLU and remain uncovered by any native MCQA benchmark.

findings.claim: [uz] Azerbaijani has the strongest published from-scratch encoder foundation of any non-Kazakh Turkic language found in this sweep, but has NO generative sub-1B LLM and NO embedding/retrieval benchmark: aLLMA family (45.9M/135.2M/369.5M params, WordPiece 64k vocab) trained on DOLLMA (651.1M whitespace-tokenized words: Wikipedia, translated Wikipedia, news, blogs, books, legal). aLLMA-BASE (135.2M) beats same-size and larger multilingual models on 4/6 created benchmarks (AZE-SCI 90.84 F1, WikiANN 91.26, LDQuAd 86.26) despite far less pretraining data than XLM-R-Large (560M, wins WikiANN 92.35/SQuAD 75.70) or mDeBERTa-v3-base (279M, wins MRPC 83.71/AZE-NSP 78.84).
findings.source: arXiv:2407.02337 (Isbarov et al., SIGTURK 2024, 'Open foundation models for Azerbaijani language')
findings.numbers: DOLLMA 651.1M words; aLLMA-SMALL 45.9M/BASE 135.2M/LARGE 369.5M; aLLMA-BASE: AZE-SCI 90.84, MRPC 79.74, WikiANN 91.26, SQuAD 71.30, AZE-NSP 75.95, LDQuAd 86.26; vs XLM-R-Large 560M (89.76/82.41/92.35/75.70/33.46/83.48) and mDeBERTa-v3-base 279M (87.13/83.71/91.87/72.27/78.84/85.29)
findings.relevance: Decision (1)/(3): Azerbaijani is a genetically distant (Oghuz, not Kipchak) contrast language with a real but encoder-only foundation and zero embedding-benchmark coverage — a candidate second/alternate port target for the pinned retrieval protocol that would avoid the Kazakh-Uzbek same-branch (Kipchak/mixed) confound.

findings.claim: [ky] KyrText (ACL LoResLM 2026, arXiv-adjacent, aclanthology 2026.loreslm-1.39) is the largest curated Kyrgyz corpus found: 680.5M words (2,334,281 docs) from news (61.4%, 1.91M docs), court decisions (23.9%), legislation (9.9%), Wikipedia (1.34%), and digitized e-library (3.45%, OCR'd via DeepSeek-OCR). Continual-pretrained xlm-roberta-large-kgz is the best resulting model, beating its own un-adapted xlm-roberta-large baseline by +19pp XNLI (0.76 vs 0.55), +18pp PAWS-X (0.85 vs 0.66), +7pp BoolQ (0.79 vs 0.72). RoBERTa trained FROM SCRATCH on only 680.5M words underperforms continual-pretrained multilingual models on tasks needing cross-lingual knowledge (PAWS-X, XNLI) despite competitive News/SST scores — a from-scratch-vs-adapt datapoint at ~680M-word scale.
findings.source: ACL Anthology 2026.loreslm-1.39 (KyrText), full PDF read
findings.numbers: 680.5M words total (Train 672.3M/Test 8.2M); News 1.91M docs/413.7M words (45.6% after upsampling), Courts 172,772 docs/160.8M words, Legal 157,021 docs/66.8M words, Wikipedia 89,657 docs/8.7M words (5x upsampled), E-library 629 docs/22.3M words (10x upsampled); xlm-roberta-large-kgz: BoolQ 0.79±0.006, PAWS-X 0.85±0.009, XNLI 0.76±0.002, News 0.92±0.005 vs base xlm-roberta-large 0.72/0.66/0.55/0.90
findings.relevance: Decision (1): the paper explicitly documents that OSCAR/mC4/CulturaX Kyrgyz splits are heavily contaminated by misidentified KAZAKH text ('poor performance of language identification libraries for Kyrgyz and Kazakh, which share a large common vocabulary') — a direct, actionable warning for the lab's own Kazakh corpus cleaning pipeline (check for Kyrgyz contamination in the reverse direction) and for any Kyrgyz-Kazakh joint data effort.

findings.claim: [ky] KyrgyzBERT (arXiv:2511.20182), the first monolingual Kyrgyz BERT, is compact (35.9M params, custom tokenizer) and reaches F1 0.828 on a translated-SST2 sentiment benchmark, 'competitive with a fine-tuned mBERT model five times larger' — but KyrText's own MLM-loss comparison shows kyrgyz-bert has by far the worst XNLI accuracy of any tested model (0.47) and the highest MLM loss (6.4), confirming monolingual-from-scratch-at-this-scale loses cross-lingual reasoning capability even when it wins narrow single-task benchmarks.
findings.source: arXiv:2511.20182 abstract; corroborated by ACL 2026.loreslm-1.39 Table 6
findings.numbers: KyrgyzBERT 35.9M params; sentiment F1 0.8280; KyrText's independent eval: kyrgyz-bert BoolQ 0.60, News 0.83, PAWS-X 0.58, SST 0.82, XNLI 0.47 (worst of all 11 models compared), MLM loss 6.4 (worst)
findings.relevance: Corroborates KB's SozKZ finding at a second Kipchak language: small from-scratch monolingual models can win narrow lexical/sentiment tasks but lose badly on reasoning/entailment tasks vs multilingual-adapted peers — reinforces the lab's own decision to prefer continual-PT-on-multilingual-base over from-scratch for the ≤600M Kazakh model.

findings.claim: [tt] Trans-tokenization for Tatar (KB already has the headline number) — re-confirming with exact provenance: swapping Mistral-7B's tokenizer to a dedicated Tatar one and continual-pretraining on only 107M tokens (41M embeddings-only + 66M with top/bottom-2 layers unfrozen) reaches PPL 10.96, 49.34% on SART word-analogy benchmark, chrF 53.7±0.2 on short-text MT. SART itself (arXiv:1904.00365, Khusainova & Khan, Innopolis) is the original Tatar word-embedding evaluation resource (similarity/analogy/relatedness), modeled directly on the Russian RUSSE benchmark design.
findings.source: arXiv:2408.04303 (already in KB) + arXiv:1904.00365 (SART, confirmed via search)
findings.numbers: Tatar swap-CPT: 107M tokens, PPL 10.96, SART analogies 49.34%, chrF 53.7±0.2
findings.relevance: Decision (1): Tatar (Kipchak, same branch as Kazakh) already has both a word-embedding intrinsic benchmark (SART) AND a validated tokenizer-swap+CPT recipe at 7B scale — useful cross-check corpus for the lab's own trans-tokenization ablation, though still no sub-1B swap-tax measurement (KB gap persists).

findings.claim: [ba] The only controlled from-scratch-vs-adaptation study for Bashkir (arXiv:2605.04948, LoRA/QLoRA comparison) used a small corpus (71,567 docs / 46.9M tokens, only 10,000 docs actually used for experiments) and found QLoRA rank sensitivity is severe: DeepSeek-7B QLoRA at r=8 catastrophically fails (PPL 129.55) while r=16 on the same model recovers to PPL 8.98 — a >14x perplexity swing from one LoRA-rank hyperparameter change. Best overall: GPT-2-medium full fine-tune PPL 3.34; best PEFT: Mistral-7B QLoRA r=16 PPL 3.79 and Phi-2 QLoRA r=8 PPL 3.81, 'with over 40x fewer trainable parameters' than full FT.
findings.source: arXiv:2605.04948v1, fetched directly
findings.numbers: Corpus: 71,567 docs, 46.9M tokens (10,000 docs used); GPT-2-medium full FT PPL 3.34±0.01; Mistral-7B QLoRA r16 PPL 3.79±0.02; Phi-2 QLoRA r8 PPL 3.81±0.03; DeepSeek-7B QLoRA r8 PPL 129.55±1.06 vs r16 PPL 8.98±0.10
