findings.claim: [ba][cv][kaz] 'No One-Size-Fits-All' (arXiv:2602.04442) trains MT systems (LoRA/DoRA + 8-bit quant, DeepSeek/Gemma/mGPT bases) for Bashkir, Kazakh, Kyrgyz, Tatar, Chuvash and reports chrF++ scores that rank Kazakh transfer BEST and Chuvash WORST of the three languages with numbers surfaced: Kazakh 49.71, Bashkir 46.94, Chuvash 39.47. Chuvash is the outlier as the sole Oghur-branch language in the set (vs the other four's Kipchak branch), consistent with genetic distance — not just resource size — mattering for MT transfer specifically (unlike KB's byte-premium finding for knowledge tasks).
findings.source: arXiv:2602.04442 (fetched, partial extraction — exact per-language corpus sizes were embedded in unreadable PDF streams) + web search snippet corroboration
findings.numbers: chrF++: Kazakh 49.71, Bashkir 46.94, Chuvash 39.47 (Russian-X pairs)
findings.relevance: Decision (2): gives one more sourced axis (MT transfer quality) where Kazakh leads its Kipchak/Oghur neighbors, and flags Chuvash as the family's genetic outlier — relevant if the atlas wants a 'who transfers best' ranking distinct from the TUMLU knowledge-QA ranking.

findings.claim: [cv][tk][sah] No dedicated from-scratch or adapted LLM/BERT was found for Chuvash, Turkmen, or Sakha/Yakut text in this sweep — these are the three languages with confirmed 'nothing found' at the model level (as opposed to corpus-only or toolkit-only coverage). Turkmen has a speech corpus (TurkmenSpeech, 251 hours / 119,847 clips @16kHz) but no equivalent text corpus/LM was located. Sakha has a Universal Dependencies treebank + morphological analyzer (YakuToolkit, SIGUL 2022) but no language model. Chuvash has only 'Open Data Chuvash' translation-pair data used inside the multi-language MT paper above, no monolingual encoder/decoder model.
findings.source: Multi-query web search (Bashkir/Chuvash/Sakha/Yakut NLP, Turkmen NLP corpus low-resource 2025) — absence-of-evidence across ~6 distinct search formulations
findings.numbers: Turkmen speech: 251h / 119,847 clips; Sakha: UD treebank + morph analyzer (SIGUL 2022), no LM found; Chuvash: 0 dedicated model found
findings.relevance: Decision (3): these three languages are the genuinely empty cells in the Turkic NLP landscape — lowest-hanging, but also lowest-adoption-potential (very small speaker/researcher communities), targets if the lab ever wanted a 'most under-served Turkic language' artifact; NOT recommended as a first port target given the live Uzbek offer and Azerbaijani's better existing base.

findings.claim: [ug] Uyghur shows the same native-script advantage pattern as Kazakh/Crimean Tatar but in Arabic script: TUMLU Table 6 shows Claude 3.5 Sonnet scoring Arabic 70.8 vs Latin 64.5 (Cyrillic not evaluated/used), Qwen2.5-72B Arabic 56.1 vs Latin 53.4, Gemma-2-27B Arabic 42.2 vs Latin 36.0 — the native/majority script consistently wins by 3-8pp across models, mirroring Kazakh's Cyrillic advantage. No dedicated Uyghur generative LLM or embedding/retrieval model was found; the main documented resources are the historical Uyghur-Chinese bilingual corpus (diaspora/historical, not modern web text) and the MC2 corpus used only for language-ID testing.
findings.source: arXiv:2502.11020v2 Table 6; web search for Uyghur NLP 2025-2026 corpus/model (no modern dedicated LM found)
findings.numbers: Uyghur Claude: Arabic 70.8 / Latin 64.5; Qwen72B: Arabic 56.1 / Latin 53.4; Gemma27B: Arabic 42.2 / Latin 36.0. TUMLU uig subset: 519 questions, low-resource group, mean rank 2nd-lowest of 8 (Claude 71.3)
findings.relevance: Cross-checks the atlas's script-effect argument across a THIRD script family (Arabic, not just Cyrillic/Latin) — strengthens the general claim that native/majority-script training data drives accuracy regardless of which script it is, useful boilerplate for the Latin-transition risk section.

findings.claim: [kaa] Karakalpak's TUMLU subject breakdown reveals an anomaly not seen in other languages: Claude 3.5 Sonnet scores very high on general knowledge subjects (Biology 78.0, Chemistry 85.7, Physics 95.6) but collapses on Native Language & Literature specifically (42.2, vs 70-90 range for other languages on the same subject) — the opposite pattern from what data-quantity alone would predict, since Karakalpak has the smallest FineWeb2/curated footprint of the low-resource group (~2.2M words, bekan/karakalpak_corpus_v2_m, MIT license, 135,667 docs, Latin script).
findings.source: arXiv:2502.11020v2 Table 3; HF dataset bekan/karakalpak_corpus_v2_m fetched directly
findings.numbers: Karakalpak Claude 3.5: Biology 78.0, Chemistry 85.7, Geography 75.0, NL&L 42.2, Physics 95.6 (History/Maths missing entirely — no questions in those subjects for this language); monolingual corpus 135,667 docs, ~2.2M words, 21.4MB, MIT license
findings.relevance: Decision (3)/atlas: flags that 'general knowledge' MCQA and 'native language & literature' MCQA can diverge sharply within one low-resource language, meaning a single aggregate score (as often reported) can mask subject-specific data gaps — worth noting if the lab designs its own Kazakh subject-wise breakdown for KazMMLU-style reporting.

findings.claim: [uz][kaa] The Open Language Data Initiative (arXiv:2409.04269, Mamasaidov & Shopulatov / Tahrirchi) built and open-sourced parallel corpora for Uzbek-Karakalpak, Russian-Karakalpak, and English-Karakalpak, 100,000 sentence pairs each, plus fine-tuned open NMT models — the same Tahrirchi team behind TahrirchiBERT/UzLiB, confirming a single active, technically strong Uzbek-Karakalpak research group exists and is a plausible collaboration surface beyond the stated Uzbek-only offer.
findings.source: arXiv:2409.04269 (confirmed via search, Tahrirchi authorship)
findings.numbers: 100,000 pairs each for uz-kaa, ru-kaa, en-kaa parallel corpora
findings.relevance: Decision (1): if the live Uzbek collaboration expands, Tahrirchi's existing Uzbek-Karakalpak bridge work means Karakalpak could piggyback onto the same collaboration at near-zero extra relationship cost, extending the pinned protocol's reach to a second, much lower-resource Kipchak language.

findings.claim: [pan-turkic] No native MTEB-style or KazQAD-style retrieval/STS/reranking benchmark was found for ANY Turkic language except Turkish. TurkicNLP (arXiv:2602.19174), the most comprehensive Turkic NLP toolkit found (24 languages across Oghuz/Kipchak/Karluk/Siberian/Oghur/Arghu/Historical branches, Apertium FSTs for 20 langs, neural pipelines with UD treebanks for only 8), offers ONLY generic NLLB-200 cross-lingual sentence embeddings for retrieval/clustering across all 24 languages — no fine-tuned or evaluated native retrieval benchmark. Kazakh is explicitly named as one of the best-resourced languages in this toolkit alongside Turkish (full pipeline incl. NER trained on KazNERD, 112,702 tokens/25 entity classes).
findings.source: arXiv:2602.19174 (TurkicNLP), fetched directly (html v1-v5)
findings.numbers: 24 languages, 7 genetic branches; morphology via Apertium for 20 langs; neural dep-parsing UD treebanks for 8 langs; KazNERD 112,702 tokens, 25 entity classes; embeddings = NLLB-200 only, all 24 langs
findings.relevance: Directly confirms decision (3): a pan-Turkic native retrieval benchmark built on the lab's pinned KazQAD-style protocol would be genuinely unclaimed and would extend naturally from a Kazakh-first kk-MTEB effort — the toolkit paper itself only offers a generic multilingual-embedding fallback, not a benchmark, which is exactly the gap to fill.

findings.claim: [tr] The only Turkic-language-validated cheap embedding-adaptation recipe found beyond mE5 fine-tuning is 'tokenizer surgery + offline distillation' (arXiv:2605.29992, embeddingmagibu-200m, Turkish): (1) build a Turkish-optimized 131,072-vocab tokenizer by pruning/extending a multilingual teacher's vocab via frequency analysis on a 40-language corpus, (2) clone the teacher backbone with mean-composition token-embedding initialization for new vocab, (3) offline cosine-similarity distillation from precomputed teacher vectors (no online teacher inference) over a balanced 40-language Wikipedia corpus. Result: a ~200M-param student BEATS its ~300M-param teacher on STSbTR (Pearson/Spearman 77.55/77.45 vs teacher's own 73.84/72.92), trains in ~4 GPU-hours for $5-$20 total, and supports an 8,192-token context (vs 512 for BERT-era Turkish encoders).
findings.source: arXiv:2605.29992, confirmed via search + WebSearch summary of abstract/results
findings.numbers: Tokenizer 131,072 vocab, 40-lang frequency analysis; student 200M params vs teacher 300M; STSbTR Pearson/Spearman: student 77.55/77.45 vs teacher 73.84/72.92; training ~4 GPU-hours, $5-$20; context 8,192 tokens
findings.relevance: Decision (1): this is a CHEAPER (~$5-20 vs Less-is-More's <$20 for data but full-FT compute) and Turkic-in-family-validated alternative/complement to Less-is-More that the lab should benchmark head-to-head for the Kazakh/Uzbek embedding recipe choice, since Less-is-More itself has NEVER been tested on any Turkic language (per KB) while this recipe has.

findings.claim: [tr] Morpheus (arXiv:2606.18717, Turkish): a reversible, morphology-aware neural tokenizer-and-embedder (decode(encode(w))=w exactly, via a differentiable Poisson-binomial boundary model) achieves the lowest bits-per-character among reversible tokenizers (1.425), roughly DOUBLES gold morphological alignment vs the subword family (MorphScore macro-F1 0.61 vs ~0.32), uses ~19% less GPU memory than 64K-vocab subword tokenizers, and as a frozen embedder BEATS multilingual retriever BGE-M3 and monolingual BERTurk on lexical/morphology tasks: root-family retrieval MAP 0.85, same-root verification ROC-AUC 1.00.
findings.source: arXiv:2606.18717, confirmed via targeted search of abstract/results
findings.numbers: BPC 1.425 (lowest reversible); MorphScore macro-F1 0.61 vs ~0.32 subword baseline; GPU memory -19% vs 64K subword vocab; lexical retrieval MAP 0.85; same-root ROC-AUC 1.00 (beats BGE-M3, BERTurk)
findings.relevance: Decision (3): first in-family (Turkic) proof that morphology-aware tokenization/embedding can beat a strong multilingual retriever (BGE-M3) on LEXICAL tasks — but it has NOT been extended to semantic/SEMANTIC retrieval (MTEB-style STS/QA) or to any Kipchak language (Kazakh/Uzbek/Tatar); combining morpheme-aware embedding with semantic retrieval on a Kipchak language remains open and directly buildable on the lab's morpheme-keyed-memory research line.

findings.claim: [ky] HJ-Ky-0.1 (arXiv:2411.10724) is a manually-annotated Kyrgyz word-embedding intrinsic benchmark modeled on Russian RUSSE/English SimLex-999/RW methodology: 800 word pairs total (400 similarity, 300 analogies, 100 relatedness), evaluated against FastText, Word2Vec (Skip-gram/CBOW), compressed FastText, and dictionary-based (Asanov Russian-Kyrgyz dictionary) representations. Exact Spearman correlation scores per model could not be extracted from the available PDF text (compressed streams) in this pass.
findings.source: arXiv:2411.10724, WebFetch (partial extraction only)
findings.numbers: 800 pairs (400 sim / 300 analogy / 100 relatedness); 5 embedding approaches evaluated; exact scores NOT extracted
findings.relevance: Decision (1)/(3): Kyrgyz has its own intrinsic word-embedding benchmark analogous to Tatar's SART — worth a direct-read follow-up before any pan-Turkic embedding-benchmark design, to avoid duplicating existing per-language intrinsic evaluation infrastructure.

recommendations: Decision 1 (port target for pinned eval protocols + Less-is-More): Proceed with the live Uzbek offer, but explicitly design the port as a controlled script-split ablation (Cyrillic-only vs Latin-only vs mixed Uzbek fine-tune of mE5), not a copy of the Kazakh kk/ru code-switch framing — TUMLU shows Uzbek is the family's worst-performing language despite ~1.1B FineWeb2 words, plausibly because its ~56/44 Latin/Cyrillic split fragments effective training signal differently than Kazakh's ~100% Cyrillic concentration.

In parallel, benchmark the tokenizer-surgery + offline-distillation recipe (arXiv:2605.29992, ~$5-20, ~4 GPU-hours, validated on Turkish) head-to-head against Less-is-More (10k pairs, mE5 full-FT) for whichever language is chosen first — Less-is-More has zero in-family Turkic validation while this recipe does, and it is cheaper.

Add Azerbaijani as a second/contrast port target if resources allow: it is genetically distant (Oghuz vs Kazakh's Kipchak), has a strong existing encoder foundation (aLLMA/DOLLMA, no script-split confound since DOLLMA is Latin-only), and currently has ZERO embedding/retrieval benchmark — a cleaner scientific contrast than same-branch Kipchak languages (Tatar/Karakalpak) for a 'does the recipe generalize across the family' claim.

Decision 2 (atlas positioning of Kazakh): Lead with the TUMLU per-language table as the primary sourced ranking — state explicitly that Kazakh ranks 4th/8 on frontier models (83.0, behind tur/aze/tat) but is the single HIGHEST-scoring Turkic language for the smallest tested open model (Llama-3.1-8B, 46.4) — this 'best-learnable-at-small-scale' framing is a stronger, more specific, and more defensible claim for a ≤600M-model lab than a generic resource-ranking claim.

Report the FineWeb2-derived resource ladder (kaz 1.837B Cyrillic words > uzb 1.109B > kir 680.5M (KyrText) > aze 651.1M (DOLLMA) > ba 46.9M > crh 23.3M > kaa 2.2M > tk ~0 text) in the atlas with an explicit caveat that sources are heterogeneous (raw web-crawl vs curated corpora) — do not average or rank-normalize across source types without flagging it.

Use Crimean Tatar's Latin-dominant script-performance gap (13.9pp favoring Latin, mirroring Kazakh's current 4.7-12.2pp Cyrillic-favoring gap) as the atlas's concrete natural-experiment evidence for forecasting the 2031 Kazakh Latin-transition accuracy tax; cite the Uyghur Arabic-script parallel (3-8pp native-script advantage) as a third-script corroboration of the general pattern.

Decision 3 (pan-Turkic benchmark territory): Do NOT build a competing pan-Turkic MCQA/knowledge benchmark — TUMLU/TUMLU-mini already exists, is ACL-published, and explicitly invites more model submissions (it has never tested a ≤1B model). Concrete low-cost action: run the lab's Qwen3-0.6B-Base / QymyzLM on TUMLU-mini and submit the first ≤1B datapoint via a PR to github.com/ceferisbarov/TUMLU — this is a high-visibility, near-zero-cost force-of-adoption artifact.

DO build a pan-Turkic native retrieval benchmark on the lab's pinned KazQAD-style protocol, starting with Kazakh + whichever port-target language (Uzbek/Azerbaijani) — confirmed unclaimed: TurkicNLP's toolkit offers only generic NLLB-200 cross-lingual embeddings with no retrieval benchmark, and MTEB/MMTEB (per KB) has zero native Kazakh or other-Turkic retrieval tasks except Turkish's separate TR-MTEB/mteb_tr effort.

For the morpheme-keyed embedding research line: extend Morpheus's Turkish lexical-retrieval result (beats BGE-M3 on root-family MAP/ROC-AUC) to (a) semantic/STS-style retrieval, not just lexical/root tasks, and (b) at least one Kipchak language (Kazakh/Uzbek/Tatar) — this combination does not exist anywhere in the literature found and is directly buildable on the lab's existing morpheme-keyed-memory research thread.

Before finalizing any Kazakh corpus cleaning claims, cross-check for Kyrgyz-Kazakh bidirectional language-ID contamination — KyrText's authors found Kyrgyz web-crawl splits (OSCAR/mC4/CulturaX) are heavily contaminated with misidentified KAZAKH text due to shared vocabulary and weak langID; the reverse contamination direction (Kazakh corpora containing misidentified Kyrgyz) should be checked in the lab's own SozKZ-style cleaning pipeline.

If the lab ever does a paid QLoRA continual-PT run, treat LoRA/QLoRA rank as a mandatory swept hyperparameter rather than a fixed default — the Bashkir study found a >14x perplexity swing (129.55 vs 8.98) from changing r=8 to r=16 on the identical DeepSeek-7B setup, a catastrophic-failure mode the lab's design-panel should explicitly guard against before spending vast.ai budget.
open_questions: Does Uzbek's TUMLU underperformance (lowest of 8 languages on most models) come from script-split fragmentation, from lower absolute per-script data density, or from something in the question set itself (Uzbek questions are noted as 'university entrance exam' style, potentially harder)? Needs a controlled ablation, not inferable from published numbers alone.

Is the TUMLU paper's 'Turkmen, Kyrgyz and Bashkir are not included' statement a drafting error (since Kyrgyz clearly has full results) or does it reflect an earlier draft/different language subset? Worth checking the paper's GitHub issues/errata before citing in the atlas.
What are HJ-Ky-0.1's (arXiv:2411.10724) exact per-model Spearman correlation scores? The PDF text extraction failed to surface the numeric table — needs a direct re-fetch or manual page-image read.

Does UzLiB (Tahrirchi's Uzbek MCQA benchmark) have a published leaderboard with exact scores comparable to TUMLU/KazMMLU? Only the benchmark's existence and construction method were confirmed, not its results table (GitHub/HF README access was inconclusive in this pass).

Has any 2026 Q2-Q3 preprint built a native Kazakh, Uzbek, or other-Turkic MTEB-style retrieval/STS task since the KB's last MMTEB check? The field moves monthly per the lab's own operating assumption — this sweep found none, but a narrower, more recent-dated re-check (June-July 2026) before committing to build the pan-Turkic retrieval benchmark would reduce duplication risk.

What exact corpus size (documents/tokens) does the Bashkir-Russian, Kazakh-literature, Kyrgyz-literature, Tatar-IPSAN, and Chuvash 'Open Data' parallel corpora used in arXiv:2602.04442 have? The PDF's compressed streams blocked exact number extraction beyond the reported chrF++ scores.

research.area: turkic-pan-benchmarks (non-Kazakh Turkic NLP landscape, Kazakh as comparison anchor only)

findings.claim: TUMLU is the widest native (non-machine-translated) Turkic MMLU-style benchmark: 9 languages [tr][az][uz][kk][ky][tt][crh][ug][kaa], 38,139 MCQs across 11 subjects (Maths, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Geography, Native Language & Literature, History, + 4 excluded from main experiments for limited coverage: Logic, Philosophy, Religion & Ethics, Human & Society). TUMLU-mini = manually-verified, ~100 Q/subject/language subset. Evaluated 5-shot and 5-shot-CoT.
findings.source: arXiv:2502.11020 (ACL 2025), https://arxiv.org/html/2502.11020, https://github.com/ceferisbarov/TUMLU
findings.numbers: 9 langs, 38,139 Q, 11 subjects (7 used), 5-shot / 5-shot-CoT
findings.relevance: Direct protocol comparator: TUMLU uses 5-shot, the lab's KazMMLU protocol is 3-shot dev-limited — NOT directly comparable without re-running under evallab's pinned shot count. TUMLU-mini's per-language MCQ format is portable to Uzbek/Kyrgyz with the lab's existing KazMMLU harness design.

findings.claim: TUMLU-mini 5-shot Claude-3.5-Sonnet scores by language rank Kazakh mid-pack, not last: Turkish 85.7% [tr] > Azerbaijani 84.4% [az] > Kazakh 83.0% [kk] > ... > Karakalpak 75.3% [kaa] > Uyghur 71.3% [ug] > Uzbek 69.1% [uz] (worst).
findings.source: arXiv:2502.11020 (TUMLU), Table of per-language results
findings.numbers: tr 85.7 / az 84.4 / kk 83.0 / kaa 75.3 / ug 71.3 / uz 69.1 (Claude-3.5-Sonnet, 5-shot)
findings.relevance: For the atlas's Kazakh-vs-Turkic-family positioning: on a frontier proprietary model, Kazakh is NOT the weak link among Kipchak languages — Uzbek (Karluk) and Uyghur score lower despite Uzbek's larger population, likely reflecting weaker native educational-text digitization; useful counter to a naive 'Kazakh is behind Turkish' narrative.

findings.claim: Kardeş-NLU (EACL 2024) is the earlier cross-lingual transfer benchmark for 5 Turkic languages: Azerbaijani, Kazakh, Kyrgyz, Uzbek, Uyghur [az][kk][ky][uz][ug], using Turkish as the high-resource 'donor' for intermediate-training and fine-tuning transfer experiments. General NLU tasks requiring no world knowledge; finds transfer gains are 'highly task- and language-dependent.'
findings.source: aclanthology.org/2024.eacl-long.100/
findings.numbers: 5 Turkic langs + Turkish donor; task-dependent gains (no aggregate % reported in abstract)
findings.relevance: Establishes Turkish-as-pivot transfer as a validated strategy predating TUMLU; if the lab's Less-is-More embedding recipe needs a transfer donor for Uzbek, Kardeş-NLU's finding that transfer gains are task-dependent (not uniform) argues against assuming Turkish-pivot transfer will help retrieval specifically — it was only validated on NLU classification/inference tasks, not retrieval.

findings.claim: TurkicNLP toolkit (2026) maps resource tiers across 24 Turkic languages in 4 branches (Oghuz: tr, az, tk, gagauz; Kipchak: kk, ky, tt, ba, crh, kaa, Nogai, Kumyk, Karachay-Balkar; Karluk: uz, ug; Siberian: sah/Sakha, Altai, Tuvan, Khakas; Oghur: cv/Chuvash). Only Turkish + Kazakh have production-quality NER; neural POS/parsing (Stanza+UD) exists for only 8 of 24 languages; Bashkir/Chuvash have morphology-only (beta/prototype Apertium FST) with NO POS/parsing/NER; Sakha has morphology+NLLB embeddings but no syntax/NER; Karakalpak is prototype-morphology-only.
findings.source: arXiv:2602.19174 (TurkicNLP), https://arxiv.org/html/2602.19174v2/v4
findings.numbers: 24 langs, 4 branches; NER production-quality: tr+kk only; neural pipeline: 8/24 langs; NLLB-200 embeddings/translation: all 24
findings.relevance: Direct answer to 'which Turkic languages have NO benchmark presence at all': Nogai, Kumyk, Karachay-Balkar, Gagauz, Altai, Tuvan, Khakas have ZERO MMLU/MTEB-style benchmark and only NLLB-translation-level embedding support — these are outside any realistic near-term porting target for the lab's protocols.

findings.claim: UzLiB (Uzbek Linguistic Benchmark) [uz] exists as a dedicated Uzbek MCQ benchmark (MIT license, github.com/tahrirchi/uzlib), sourced from Uzbek-linguistics Telegram channels, manually verified, testing correct Uzbek usage/grammar (not general knowledge like TUMLU). Uzbek-specific instruction models exist: behbudiy/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-Uz, behbudiy/Mistral-Nemo-Instruct-Uz.
findings.source: github.com/tahrirchi/uzlib
findings.numbers: MIT license; exact Q-count/scores not extracted from README (needs direct repo file read for numbers)
findings.relevance: Confirms Uzbek NLP ecosystem has an active local group (Tahrirchi/Behbudiy) already building both benchmarks and instruction-tuned models — the live Uzbek collaboration offer should coordinate with (not duplicate) this existing effort; no embedding-specific artifact from this group was found.

findings.claim: Global-MMLU includes Kyrgyz [ky] and Turkish [tr] but NOT Azerbaijani, Kazakh, or Uzbek. INCLUDE benchmark (arXiv:2411.19799, 44 languages/1,926 exams/197,243 QA pairs) includes Azerbaijani [az] and Kazakh [kk] but not Uzbek or Kyrgyz.
findings.source: arXiv:2411.19799 (INCLUDE); Global-MMLU (cited via search, cross-checked against TUMLU paper's related-work comparison)
findings.numbers: Global-MMLU: ky+tr only among Turkic; INCLUDE: az+kk only among Turkic (of 44 total langs, 197,243 QA pairs)
findings.relevance: No single mainstream multilingual-knowledge benchmark covers Kazakh AND Uzbek AND Kyrgyz together except TUMLU — reinforces TUMLU as the only viable cross-Turkic protocol anchor for a design spec that must compare Kazakh against Uzbek/Kyrgyz on the same instrument.

findings.claim: TR-MMLU [tr] (arXiv:2508.13044 / earlier 2501.00593) is a Turkish-ONLY MMLU-style benchmark, 6,200 MCQs across 62 subject sections of the Turkish education system — separate from and larger-subject-count than TUMLU's Turkish subset. Additional Turkish-only benchmarks exist: TurkBench (arXiv:2601.07020) and Cetvel (arXiv:2508.16431, unified LLM eval for Turkish covering understanding+generation+cultural capacity).
findings.numbers: TR-MMLU: 6,200 Q, 62 sections
findings.relevance: Turkish alone has at least 4 distinct knowledge/understanding benchmarks (TUMLU-tr-subset, TR-MMLU, TurkBench, Cetvel) vs Kazakh's 2 (TUMLU-kk-subset, KazMMLU) and Uzbek's ~2 (TUMLU-uz-subset, UzLiB) — quantifies the resource asymmetry the atlas survey should cite: benchmark-count ratio Turkish:Kazakh:Uzbek roughly 4:2:2, though Kazakh's KazMMLU (23K Q) is far larger than any single Turkish-only set.

findings.claim: TR-MTEB [tr] (ACL Findings EMNLP 2025) is the first large-scale Turkish embedding benchmark: 6 tasks (classification, clustering, pair classification, retrieval, bitext mining, STS), 26 datasets combining native + translated resources (msmarco-tr, quora-tr, nfcorpus-tr, scifact-tr among them). Authors built a 34.2M-pair weakly-supervised Turkish sentence-pair corpus and trained 2 Turkish-specific embedding models (contrastive pretrain + SFT) that 'significantly improve upon baseline monolingual models' and are competitive with multilingual baselines. HF org trmteb hosts 10 embedding models (incl. multilingual-e5-base fine-tuned variants, BERTurk contrastive/fine-tuned) and 37 datasets.
findings.source: aclanthology.org/2025.findings-emnlp.471/, huggingface.co/trmteb
findings.numbers: 6 tasks, 26 datasets (benchmark) / 37 datasets (HF org), 34.2M training pairs, 10 released models
findings.relevance: TR-MTEB is the closest existing structural template for the lab's planned kk-MTEB: same task taxonomy (classification/clustering/pair-class/retrieval/bitext/STS) the lab should mirror for KazQAD-adjacent kk-MTEB construction, and 34.2M pairs sets a rough scale target for a Kazakh weakly-supervised pair corpus. No equivalent MTEB-style benchmark exists yet for Kazakh, Uzbek, Kyrgyz, Azerbaijani, or Tatar — kk-MTEB and a hypothetical uz/az-MTEB remain fully unclaimed territory.

findings.claim: A cheap tokenizer-surgery + offline-distillation recipe adapts a large multilingual embedder to a new language for ~$5-20 on a single A100 in ~4 hours: source=EmbeddingGemma-300M (768-dim, 256K vocab), target=embeddingmagibu-200m [tr] (768-dim, 128K vocab, ~200M params) via (1) extracting 64K frequent target-language tokens + merging with existing multilingual tokens = 128K vocab, (2) weight-preserving mean-composition cloning of new token embeddings from teacher, (3) offline distillation on precomputed teacher embeddings (cosine loss) over ~580K balanced 40-language Wikipedia examples. Result: 77.55% Pearson on STSb-tr (vs teacher's 73.84%, i.e. BEATS the teacher) and 63.9% avg on TR-MTEB (26 tasks, ranks 7th/26 models) at 98% of teacher performance with 33% fewer params.
findings.source: arXiv:2605.29992 (Adapting Multilingual Embedding Models to Turkish via Cross-Lingual Tokenizer Surgery and Offline Distillation)
findings.numbers: cost $5-20, ~4h single A100; 580K training examples; STSb-tr 77.55% (student) vs 73.84% (teacher); TR-MTEB avg 63.9%, rank 7/26
findings.relevance: This is a directly portable, near-zero-cost recipe for the lab's Kazakh embedding track: same tokenizer-surgery + offline-distillation approach applied to EmbeddingGemma-300M or mE5-large with a Kazakh-frequent-token vocabulary could produce a compact Kazakh-specialized embedder for roughly the same $5-20/4h budget — a concrete low-risk alternative or complement to the current mE5 Less-is-More plan, and the paper explicitly notes it has NOT been tested on other Turkic languages (fully open for Kazakh/Uzbek as a first-mover).

findings.claim: FLORES-200 covers 11 Turkic variants with explicit script tags: Turkish tur_Latn, North Azerbaijani azj_Latn [az], South Azerbaijani azb_Arab [az], Kazakh kaz_Cyrl [kk], Kyrgyz kir_Cyrl [ky], Tatar tat_Cyrl [tt], Bashkir bak_Cyrl [ba], Turkmen tuk_Latn [tk], Uyghur uig_Arab [ug], Crimean Tatar crh_Latn [crh], Northern Uzbek uzn_Latn [uz]. NOT covered: Chuvash, Sakha, Karakalpak, Gagauz, Altai, Tuvan, Khakas, Nogai, Kumyk, Karachay-Balkar.
findings.source: github.com/facebookresearch/flores (flores200 README)
findings.numbers: 11/~24 Turkic language varieties covered in FLORES-200; SIB-200 and Belebele both derive their parallel passages from FLORES-200 so inherit the same 11-language Turkic ceiling
findings.relevance: Confirms an upper bound on which Turkic languages SIB-200/Belebele-style topic-classification/reading-comprehension eval can port to without new parallel-data collection: Karakalpak (despite being in TUMLU) has NO FLORES-200/Belebele/SIB-200 presence, so Uzbek/Kazakh/Kyrgyz/Tatar/Bashkir/Turkmen/Uyghur/Crimean-Tatar are portable today, Karakalpak/Chuvash/Sakha are not without new data work.

findings.claim: A 5-language MT resource-tier study (Bashkir, Kazakh, Kyrgyz, Tatar, Chuvash) [ba][kk][ky][tt][cv] found original parallel-data sizes vary by >30x: Russian-Bashkir 1,190,773 pairs, Russian-Kazakh 367,095, Russian-Kyrgyz 35,429, English-Tatar 106,777, English-Chuvash 193,826. Best chrF++ after LoRA fine-tuning + synthetic back-translation augmentation (to 2,457,344 pairs/language): Kazakh 49.71, Bashkir 46.94, Kyrgyz 45.6 (zero-shot), Tatar 41.6, Chuvash 39.47 (worst, base model wasn't even pretrained on Chuvash).
findings.source: arXiv:2602.04442 (No One-Size-Fits-All: Building Systems For Translation to Bashkir, Kazakh, Kyrgyz, Tatar and Chuvash Using Synthetic And Original Data)
findings.numbers: chrF++: kk 49.71 > ba 46.94 > ky 45.6 > tt 41.6 > cv 39.47; original pairs ba 1.19M > cv 193.8K > tt 106.8K > kk 367.1K(!) > ky 35.4K
findings.relevance: Counter-intuitive resource/performance mismatch: Bashkir has MORE raw parallel data than Kazakh (1.19M vs 367K pairs) yet still trails Kazakh on final chrF++ (46.94 vs 49.71), suggesting Kazakh benefits from stronger base-model language coverage, not just data volume — relevant caveat for the atlas's resource-ratio claims (raw corpus size alone doesn't predict downstream Turkic NLP quality).

findings.claim: A comparative Turkic Central Asian resource survey (2024, updated coverage through 2025-26 citations) ranks Kazakh as tier-1 'Rising Star' [kk] (1,200+ hrs speech KSC2, 180K-sample sentiment KazSAnDRA, 112K-annotation NER KazNERD, has text generation + sentiment + NER + ASR + MT), Uzbek as tier-2 'Hopeful' [uz] (has UzBERT/UzRoberta, sentiment+classification corpora, MT+ASR+NER but no text-generation-specific resource), and Kyrgyz + Turkmen as tier-3 'Scraping-Bys' [ky][tk] (Kyrgyz: only classification+NER; Turkmen: ~270K web-scraped sentences from Leipzig corpus is nearly the entire resource base, no ASR/NER). Internet penetration cited as a driver: 79% Kazakhstan vs 21% Turkmenistan.
findings.source: arXiv:2407.05006 (Recent Advancements and Challenges of Turkic Central Asian Language Processing)
findings.numbers: KSC2 1,200+ hrs; KazSAnDRA 180K samples; KazNERD 112K annotations; Turkmen ~270K sentences (Leipzig); internet penetration kz 79% vs tm 21%
findings.relevance: Gives the atlas survey a citable, numbered resource-tier ranking (Kazakh > Uzbek > Kyrgyz ~ Turkmen) for the 'where does Kazakh sit in the Turkic family' positioning question, plus a causal hypothesis (internet penetration, Soviet-era Russian dominance) rather than just raw counts.

findings.claim: A Turkic multilingual ASR study found Bashkir [ba] has consistently HIGHER word-error-rates than Kazakh, Tatar, or Kyrgyz despite Bashkir's larger raw MT parallel-corpus (see finding above) — a small-scale from-scratch Bashkir LM comparison (71,567 docs / ~46.9M tokens assembled from 16 sources, subsampled to 10,000 docs) further shows QLoRA rank-16 on Mistral-7B reaches 3.79 perplexity vs full-fine-tune GPT-2-medium's 3.34, i.e. '40x fewer trainable params for comparable quality.'
findings.source: arXiv:2605.04948 (Adapting LLMs to Bashkir: LoRA vs QLoRA)
findings.numbers: Bashkir corpus: 71,567 docs / ~46.9M tokens; QLoRA(r16)/Mistral-7B PPL 3.79 vs full-FT GPT-2-medium PPL 3.34; ~40x fewer trainable params
findings.relevance: Bashkir's ~46.9M-token assembled corpus is roughly 200x smaller than the lab's own ~9-10B-token Kazakh corpus (SozKZ scale) — quantifies just how far behind Bashkir sits versus Kazakh even among fellow Kipchak languages, useful concrete data point for the atlas's resource-ratio table.

findings.claim: The MRL (Multilingual Representation Learning) Workshop shared tasks (EMNLP 2024/2025, 2026) are NOT Turkic-specific: 2024 task was multi-lingual/multi-task information retrieval (open to any language via community submission), 2025 shared task built a community-annotated physical-commonsense-reasoning (PIQA-style) dataset per contributed language, 2026 shared task is a community-written multimodal (audio+text) QA benchmark similar to ECLeKTic. No dedicated pan-Turkic track exists in MRL to date.
findings.source: sigtyp.github.io/ws2024-mrl.html, sigtyp.github.io/ws2025-mrl.html, mrlbenchmarks.github.io
findings.numbers: n/a (task format only)
findings.relevance: MRL's 2024 IR shared task is the closest existing venue-format match to the lab's KazQAD-style retrieval work, but since Turkic languages are not a required or organized track, submitting a Kazakh (or joint Kazakh+Uzbek) entry would be a genuine unclaimed first for the pan-Turkic retrieval angle rather than joining an already-covered track.

findings.claim: TurkEmbed [tr] (2025 IEEE ASYU conference, arXiv:2511.08376) is a separate, smaller Turkish embedding model claiming SOTA on Turkish STSb/STS22 semantic similarity — evaluated on STS only, not the full TR-MTEB 6-task suite; a second independent 'MTEB-TR' effort (github.com/selmanbaysan/mteb_tr) also exists in parallel to the ACL-published TR-MTEB (trmteb), indicating some naming/effort fragmentation within Turkish embedding benchmarking itself.
findings.source: arXiv:2511.08376; github.com/selmanbaysan/mteb_tr; aclanthology.org/2025.findings-emnlp.471
findings.numbers: n/a
findings.relevance: Even Turkish, the best-resourced Turkic language, has fragmented/competing embedding benchmarks (TR-MTEB vs MTEB-TR vs TurkEmbed's own STS claim) — a cautionary note for the lab: naming a Kazakh benchmark 'kk-MTEB' should check for any parallel community effort before the upstream MTEB PR to avoid the same duplication Turkish now has.

recommendations: Port TUMLU-mini's exact MCQ eval harness (5-shot, 5-shot-CoT, 100 Q/subject/language, 4-choice logit or generation scoring) to the evallab runner FIRST for any new Turkic language, since it's the only benchmark already covering Kazakh + Uzbek + Kyrgyz + Azerbaijani + Tatar simultaneously under one protocol — but flag in evallab that TUMLU's 5-shot differs from the lab's pinned 3-shot KazMMLU protocol, so cross-benchmark comparisons need explicit shot-count normalization, never a raw number merge.

For the live Uzbek collaboration offer: prioritize Uzbek as the first non-Kazakh port target for KazQAD-style retrieval AND the Less-is-More embedding recipe — Uzbek already has (a) an active benchmark group (Tahrirchi/UzLiB, MIT-licensed) to coordinate with rather than duplicate, (b) FLORES-200/SIB-200/Belebele coverage (uzn_Latn) enabling immediate topic-classification/reading-comprehension eval reuse, and (c) TUMLU coverage for knowledge MCQ — Uzbek has the most existing infrastructure of any non-Kazakh Turkic language to build a joint retrieval benchmark on top of.

Adopt the tokenizer-surgery + offline-distillation recipe from arXiv:2605.29992 (EmbeddingGemma-300M -> 128K-vocab 200M-param Turkish student, $5-20/4h A100, beats teacher on STSb-tr) as a low-cost alternative/complement pilot for the Kazakh embedding track — run a Kazakh-vocabulary variant before committing full compute to the current mE5 Less-is-More plan; if it beats mE5-large on KazQAD at 1/10th the training cost, it changes the canonical embedding recipe.

When building kk-MTEB, mirror TR-MTEB's exact 6-task taxonomy (classification, clustering, pair classification, retrieval, bitext mining, STS) and its scale target (~34M weakly-supervised pairs, 26 datasets) as the structural template for the upstream MTEB PR — this is the only existing same-family precedent and reviewers on the MTEB side will recognize the format.

Do NOT attempt Karakalpak, Chuvash, Sakha, or Gagauz benchmark porting in the near term — they lack FLORES-200/SIB-200/Belebele parallel-data presence entirely (Karakalpak despite being in TUMLU), meaning any retrieval/topic-classification port requires new parallel-corpus collection first, which is out of scope for a compute-constrained lab; treat as atlas-survey 'unclaimed but blocked' territory, not a near-term artifact target.

For the atlas survey's Kazakh-vs-Turkic-family section, cite three quantified resource-ranking sources together: (1) arXiv:2407.05006's tiered ranking (Kazakh > Uzbek > Kyrgyz~Turkmen) with speech/sentiment/NER dataset sizes, (2) arXiv:2602.04442's MT chrF++ table showing Kazakh (49.71) > Bashkir (46.94) > Kyrgyz (45.6) > Tatar (41.6) > Chuvash (39.47) despite Bashkir having 3x more raw parallel data than Kazakh, and (3) TUMLU-mini's Claude-3.5-Sonnet scores showing Kazakh (83.0) ahead of Uzbek (69.1) and Uyghur (71.3) but behind Turkish/Azerbaijani — this triangulates a 'Kazakh is Turkic-family tier-1, second only to Turkish/Azerbaijani, ahead of Uzbek/Kyrgyz/Bashkir/Chuvash on most axes' claim with three independent numeric sources rather than one.

Investigate the pan-Turkic MTEB/retrieval gap as a lab artifact candidate: as of this sweep, NO Turkic language other than Turkish has any MTEB-style embedding benchmark, and even Turkish's is fragmented (TR-MTEB vs MTEB-TR vs TurkEmbed). A single unified pan-Turkic-MTEB PR upstream (Kazakh + Uzbek + Kyrgyz + Azerbaijani, built on the lab's KazQAD protocol + TR-MTEB's task taxonomy) would be first-of-kind and directly serves the truth-mountain adoption bar — but gate this behind the Apparatus Freeze rule: do not start it until the qymyzlm generative/embedding tracks have their next measured result.

research.area: turkic-pan-models: Multi-Turkic and cross-lingual-transfer modeling (non-Kazakh Turkic NLP landscape, Kazakh as comparison anchor only)

findings.claim: [pan-turkic] TurkicNLP toolkit covers 24 Turkic languages across 4 genetic branches (Oghuz/Kipchak/Karluk/Siberian/Oghur) with a single pipeline (tokenization, morph analysis, POS, lemmatization, dep parsing, NER, transliteration, sentence embeddings, MT). Only Turkish [tr] and Kazakh [kk] get full production-quality pipelines. Ten languages ([tr],[kk],[ky],[ug],ottoman-tr,[uz],[az],[tk],[tt],[ba]) have dedicated Stanza neural models. Apertium FST covers 20 languages. Glot500 neural morph analyzer covers 23. All 24 get NLLB-200 embeddings/MT as a floor.
findings.source: arXiv:2602.19174 (TurkicNLP: An NLP Toolkit for Turkic Languages, 2026)
findings.numbers: 24 languages; neural backend 68% detection acc/88% feature coverage vs Apertium FST 53%/54% (20-sentence eval); Glot500 zero-shot Karakalpak-via-Uzbek-proxy 82.1% UPOS acc despite no target training data; avg UPOS 84.9%, UAS 76.8%, LAS 63.6%
findings.relevance: Direct resource-tier map for where the lab's KazQAD/MTEB-style protocols and Less-is-More recipe can port with existing tooling vs need to build from scratch. Confirms Uzbek/Kyrgyz/Azerbaijani/Tatar/Bashkir sit in a 'moderately-resourced, has neural models but no production pipeline' tier — plausible next targets after Kazakh.

findings.claim: [pan-turkic] TurkicNLP's own resource-tier ranking: Turkish [tr] highest-resourced (82,000 UD treebank sentences, multiple BERTurk variants, Zemberek-NLP); Kazakh [kk] well-resourced via ISSAI ecosystem (KazNERD 112,702 tokens/25 classes, KazQAD, KazParC 371,902 parallel sentences kk-en-ru-tr, 1,200+ hrs multilingual Turkic speech); Kyrgyz/Uyghur/Uzbek [ky],[ug],[uz] moderately-resourced (UD treebanks + dedicated LMs + speech corpora; Kyrgyz has 10,900 annotated NER sentences); Sakha/Tuvan/Khakas/Altai/Karakalpak/Kumyk/Karachay-Balkar/Nogai/Gagauz/Khalaj [sah]+others prototype-tier, Apertium coverage thin, zero-shot transfer required.
findings.numbers: Turkish UD 82,000 sentences; Kazakh KazNERD 112,702 tokens; KazParC 371,902 sentences; Kyrgyz NER 10,900 sentences; multilingual Turkic speech 1,200+ hours
findings.relevance: Directly answers decision (2): resource ranking places Kazakh in the SECOND tier (behind Turkish, ahead of Uzbek/Kyrgyz/Uyghur, far ahead of Sakha/Karakalpak/Tuvan). Gives the atlas a citable 4-tier resource hierarchy.

findings.claim: [uz] Uzbek has an active from-scratch monolingual model lineage (UzBERT 2021, UzRoBERTa 2023, BERTbek LREC-COLING-2024) that 'consistently outperformed multilingual models on downstream tasks like text classification and NER', plus a 2025 knowledge-distillation sentence-embedding effort described as 'the first study of its kind' for Uzbek, and SimRelUz (a word-level semantic similarity/relatedness benchmark).
findings.source: arXiv:2108.09814 (UzBERT); BERTbek (LREC-COLING 2024 SIGUL workshop); SimRelUz benchmark (cited via search, not directly fetched)
findings.numbers: [UNVERIFIED — exact benchmark deltas not extracted from primary source]
findings.relevance: Uzbek already has monolingual BERT-family models AND a first embedding attempt — meaning the Uzbek collaboration offer would NOT be greenfield; the lab's Less-is-More recipe should be pitched as complementary (adapting mE5/EmbeddingGemma cheaply) rather than competing with from-scratch efforts.

findings.claim: [ky] KyrgyzBERT (Nov 2025) is the first monolingual Kyrgyz BERT: 35.9M params, custom tokenizer (vocab 30,522), trained on >1.5M Kyrgyz sentences. On a translated+manually-annotated SST2-style sentiment benchmark (kyrgyz-sst2), fine-tuned KyrgyzBERT scores F1 0.8280 vs fine-tuned mBERT (177M, 5x larger) 0.8401 — only a 1.2pp gap. Zero-shot (no Kyrgyz fine-tuning) XLM-R and mBERT collapse to F1 0.3221 / 0.3509.
findings.source: arXiv:2511.20182 (KyrgyzBERT: A Compact, Efficient Language Model for Kyrgyz NLP)
findings.numbers: 35.9M params, vocab 30,522, >1.5M sentences; F1: KyrgyzBERT 0.8280, mBERT-FT 0.8401, XLM-R zero-shot 0.3221, mBERT zero-shot 0.3509
findings.relevance: Directly mirrors the lab's SozKZ-vs-Qwen debate for a sister Kipchak language: a tiny (36M) monolingual model nearly matches a 5x-larger multilingual model when BOTH are fine-tuned, but the multilingual model catastrophically fails zero-shot. Supports the case that dedicated small models are worth building IF fine-tuning data exists, but general multilingual models need task adaptation regardless of scale — same lesson QymyzLM should generalize to 'from-scratch small vs adapted general' framing in the atlas.

findings.claim: [kk][tr][ru] Sherkala-8B's own published data-mixture ablation (Figure 1, Kazakh-MMLU-style internal eval) reports Kazakh-only training (ratio 1:0:0) at ~51% accuracy, degrading when Russian+Turkish are added at some intermediate ratios, but the chosen final ratio 3:1:3 (Kazakh:Russian+Turkish:English) is stated as giving 'the best overall results.' This is a DIFFERENT number/protocol from the KB's canonical Sherkala-Chat KazMMLU 41.4% (final released model, cross-protocol).
findings.source: arXiv:2503.01493v2 (Sherkala-Chat paper)
findings.numbers: ablation: Kazakh-only ~51% vs final chosen mixture 3:1:3; final released KazMMLU (different eval, KB) 41.4%
findings.relevance: Direct evidence bearing on decision (2)/(3): the paper's own authors motivate including Turkish [tr] and Russian [ru] data specifically 'to enable better performance in Kazakh via cross-lingual transfer', but the ablation numbers as extracted are internally inconsistent (higher score with LESS data) — needs re-verification before citing as a transfer-coefficient result in the atlas.

findings.claim: [kk][tr][ru] Sherkala's tokenizer (Llama-3 vocab +25% high-frequency Kazakh BPE tokens) reduces fertility for Kazakh from 4.73 to 2.04 tok/word (-56.8%), for Russian from 2.56 to 2.21 (-13.8%), and for Turkish from 2.23 to 1.82 (-18.4%) vs the stock Llama-3.1 tokenizer, measured on held-out subsets not seen during tokenizer training.
findings.relevance: Confirms Turkish [tr] already tokenizes ~2.3x more efficiently than Kazakh even in a shared Kazakh-optimized vocabulary — quantifies the fertility gap the lab must close (target <2.0 for Kazakh, Turkish is already there at 1.82 with a Kazakh-biased vocab, would be even lower with a Turkish-biased one).

findings.claim: [tr] TR-MTEB (EMNLP 2025 Findings) is the first comprehensive Turkish embedding benchmark: 6 tasks, 26 datasets. On the full leaderboard, OpenAI text-embedding-3-small ranks 1st (66.5 avg), the Turkish-specific ytu-ce-cosmos/turkish-e5-large (a fine-tune of intfloat/multilingual-e5-large-instruct) ranks 2nd (66.0), and multilingual-e5-large-instruct itself ranks 3rd (65.9) — i.e. a Turkish-adapted E5 variant essentially TIES/slightly beats its own multilingual-e5 base on its native-language benchmark.
findings.source: TR-MTEB, ACL Anthology 2025.findings-emnlp.471; huggingface.co/trmteb leaderboard
findings.numbers: text-embedding-3-small 66.5 (1st/26); turkish-e5-large 66.0 (2nd/26); mE5-large-instruct 65.9 (3rd/26)
findings.relevance: Directly answers decision (1)/(3): unlike Kazakh (where kazembed-v5's own mE5 fine-tune only gained +2.1% MRR, KB) and unlike the general TR-MTEB narrative that 'multilingual E5 dominate, Turkish-specific not yet surpassing' (from a broader search summary), the SPECIFIC turkish-e5-large datapoint shows a fine-tuned Turkish E5 variant matching its multilingual base — meaning Turkish embedding adaptation is closer to solved than Kazakh's, and any pan-Turkic embedding benchmark artifact should benchmark against turkish-e5-large as the strongest same-family baseline, not just raw mE5.

findings.claim: [tr] A distinct 2026 paper adapts EmbeddingGemma-300M (teacher, 256K vocab, 768-dim, 2048 ctx) to Turkish via 3-stage recipe: tokenizer surgery (prune/merge to 131,072-token vocab: 64K Turkish tokens from Cosmos Turkish Corpus + frequency-selected multilingual tokens from 40-language Wikipedia), weight-preserving mean-composition embedding init, then offline distillation on ~580K examples (Turkish/English capped at 100K each) with precomputed teacher vectors. Resulting ~200M-param student (embedding table cut from 196.6M to 100.6M params, ctx extended to 8,192) trains in ~4 hours on a single GPU for $5-20 total.
findings.source: arXiv:2605.29992 (Adapting Multilingual Embedding Models to Turkish via Cross-Lingual Tokenizer Surgery and Offline Distillation)
findings.numbers: vocab 256K->131,072 (64K Turkish); student ~200M (embed table 196.6M->100.6M); ctx 2048->8192; ~580K distillation examples; ~4 GPU-hours; $5-20 cost; TR-MTEB: student 63.9 (7th/26) vs teacher 65.2 (4th/26), 33% fewer params for 98% of teacher score; STSbTR Pearson: student 77.55% vs teacher 73.84% (+3.71pp, student BEATS teacher)
findings.relevance: A second, even cheaper (<$20, 4 GPU-hours) Turkish embedding adaptation recipe than Less-is-More, using tokenizer surgery + distillation rather than noisy-pair fine-tuning — worth comparing against Less-is-More as an alternative cheap adaptation path for Kazakh/Uzbek. Paper explicitly names Finnish/Hungarian/Korean as future generalization targets but NOT other Turkic languages — leaves kk/uz/ky tokenizer-surgery+distillation unclaimed, a possible lab artifact angle for decision (3).

findings.claim: [az] A 2026 knowledge-distillation embedding framework for low-resource Turkic languages (Aghalarov, Mammadov, Huseynova) uses Azerbaijani as primary case study (citing shared agglutinative morphology/syntax across the Turkic family as justification for generalizability) and reports its best model reaching 89% top-1 retrieval accuracy in a real-world Azerbaijani legal-document RAG application, with 94% of retrievals rated 'Excellent' by domain experts.
findings.source: dergipark.org.tr/en/download/article-file/5515827 (Knowledge Distillation for Embeddings of Low-Resource Turkic Family Languages, 2026)
findings.numbers: 89% top-1 retrieval accuracy; 94% 'Excellent' expert rating; [baseline/multilingual-e5 comparison numbers UNVERIFIED — PDF text extraction failed]
findings.relevance: A THIRD parallel embedding-adaptation effort within the Turkic family (after Turkish TR-MTEB and turkish-e5-large, and the tokenizer-surgery paper), this time explicitly framed as generalizable Turkic-family methodology — raises competitive pressure/prior-art risk for the lab's 'best Kazakh embedding' claim and should be checked before any 'first Turkic embedding distillation' novelty claim.

findings.claim: [tr] 'Bridging the Bosphorus' (Turkish LLM adaptation study) directly tests continual-pretraining-on-strong-base vs from-scratch-pretraining vs LoRA-continual-PT-on-weak-base for Turkish: from-scratch Hamza models (GPT-2 arch, 124M/354M/772M/1.3B, 179.2GB / 130B Turkish tokens) beat continued pretraining of a weak base (GPT2-xlarge) at the SAME architecture, but continual pretraining of a STRONG base (Mistral-7B) beats BOTH the from-scratch Hamza models and the weak-base continual-PT on Turkish QA. Continual pretraining also caused catastrophic forgetting on English benchmarks proportional to Turkish sample count.
findings.source: emrecanacikgoz.github.io/Bridging-the-Bosphorus/ (Turkish LLM adaptation and benchmarking study)
findings.numbers: Hamza: 124M/354M/772M/1.3B, 130B tokens, 179.2GB corpus; ARC-TR: Gemma-7B 46.16% (best), range 24-47%; TruthfulQA-TR: Trendyol-DPO 50.11% (best), range 33-50%
findings.relevance: Cross-validates the lab's own from-scratch-vs-adapted debate (SozKZ vs Qwen3-0.6B, KB) with an independent Turkic-family case: 'from-scratch beats a WEAK continually-pretrained base, but continual-PT-on-a-STRONG-base beats from-scratch' — reinforces that QymyzLM's QLoRA-CPT-on-Qwen3-0.6B-Base strategy (strong base + continual PT) is the empirically-favored path across at least two Turkic languages now, not just an isolated Kazakh finding.

findings.claim: [kk][tr][az][crh][kaa][kir][tat][ug] TUMLU-mini per-language results for Claude 3.5 Sonnet (5-shot, native scripts): Turkish 85.7 (highest), Azerbaijani 84.4, Tatar 84.0, Kazakh 83.0, Crimean Tatar 81.2, Karakalpak 75.3, Uyghur 71.3, Uzbek 69.1 (LOWEST) — mean 79.3 across all 9.
findings.source: github.com/ceferisbarov/TUMLU (Table 2 data, arXiv:2502.11020)
findings.relevance: Directly answers decision (2): Kazakh ranks 4th of 9 Turkic languages tested (mid-pack, ahead of Karakalpak/Uyghur/Uzbek, behind Turkish/Azerbaijani/Tatar) on a frontier model — gives the atlas a concrete, citable resource/performance ranking. Counter-intuitively Uzbek scores LOWEST despite being classed 'moderately-resourced' by TurkicNLP — worth flagging as an open question (script-transition effects? Latin-script Uzbek tokenization/data scarcity vs Cyrillic peers?) rather than assuming Uzbek is NLP-ready just because it has more monolingual model efforts.

findings.claim: [pan-turkic] TurkicASR (multilingual ASR across 10 Turkic languages incl. Bashkir [ba], Tatar [tt], Turkish [tr], Uyghur [ug], Uzbek [uz]) achieves 56.7% relative CER reduction via cross-lingual transfer compared to monolingual baselines; TurkicTTS (ISSAI) covers 10 lower-resourced Turkic languages (Azerbaijani, Bashkir, Kazakh, Kyrgyz, Sakha, Tatar, Turkish, Turkmen, Uyghur, Uzbek).
findings.source: search summary citing TurkicASR paper; github.com/IS2AI/TurkicTTS
findings.numbers: 56.7% relative CER reduction from cross-lingual transfer
findings.relevance: Speech-side evidence that cross-Turkic transfer is empirically strong (>50% relative error reduction) — supports porting the lab's evaluation protocols to sibling Turkic languages as a low-risk, well-precedented move, though this is ASR not text-embedding/retrieval so the transfer coefficient may not carry over directly.

findings.claim: [pan-turkic] A 2026 theoretical-only paper proposes a 'Turkic Transfer Coefficient (TTC)' combining morphological similarity, lexical overlap, syntactic structure, and script compatibility to formalize cross-lingual transfer potential across Azerbaijani, Kazakh, Uzbek, Turkmen, and Gagauz — but the paper is purely conceptual/theoretical and reports NO empirical transfer numbers or benchmark deltas between specific language pairs.
findings.source: arXiv:2604.06202 (Cross-Lingual Transfer and Parameter-Efficient Adaptation in the Turkic Language Family: A Theoretical Framework)
findings.numbers: none — explicitly theoretical, no empirical TTC values reported

findings.claim: [pan-turkic][kk] MMTEB/MTEB (KB, re-confirmed) has NO dedicated Kazakh, Uzbek, Kyrgyz, Azerbaijani, Tatar, or any other Turkic-language-native STS/retrieval/reranking task; Turkic languages appear only via multilingual spillover tasks (SIB-200, BelebeleRetrieval, WebFAQRetrieval, FLORES/NTREX/Tatoeba bitext, TurkicClassification, CyrillicTurkicLangClassification). TR-MTEB (Turkish-only, 26 datasets) is the ONLY native-language MTEB-style benchmark that exists for any Turkic language.

findings.numbers: 0 native Turkic-language MTEB tasks except Turkish's separate TR-MTEB (26 datasets, 6 task types)
findings.relevance: Directly answers decision (3): a pan-Turkic MTEB extension (kk-MTEB + uz-MTEB + ky-MTEB etc., unified under one leaderboard) is genuinely unclaimed territory — Turkish solved this alone via a standalone benchmark, no one has done it family-wide. This is the single clearest 'unclaimed pan-Turkic artifact' finding of the sweep, directly actionable for the lab's planned kk-MTEB upstream PR (project CLAUDE.md).

recommendations: Decision (1) — protocol porting order: port KazQAD-style retrieval + Less-is-More recipe to Uzbek [uz] FIRST (live collaboration offer + existing monolingual BERT/RoBERTa/embedding lineage to build on) but budget for a SURPRISE — TUMLU-mini shows Uzbek scoring LOWEST of 9 Turkic languages even on Claude 3.5 Sonnet (69.1 vs Kazakh 83.0), so do not assume Uzbek is 'easier' than Kazakh; run a quick tokenizer-fertility + TUMLU-style diagnostic on the Uzbek corpus before committing engineering time. Second target: Kyrgyz [ky] (KyrgyzBERT already validates the small-monolingual-model recipe at 35.9M params, giving a ready-made adaptation testbed for Less-is-More at even smaller scale than Kazakh).

Before claiming novelty for any Kazakh embedding-adaptation recipe, benchmark against BOTH ytu-ce-cosmos/turkish-e5-large (TR-MTEB 66.0, ties mE5-large-instruct 65.9) and the tokenizer-surgery+distillation EmbeddingGemma-Turkish adapter (arXiv:2605.29992, $5-20/4-GPU-hours, STSbTR Pearson 77.55 beating its own teacher 73.84) — these are the two strongest same-family precedents and show Turkish embedding adaptation is materially further along than Kazakh's (kazembed-v5 only +2.1% MRR, KB). Consider replicating the tokenizer-surgery+offline-distillation recipe as a CHEAPER alternative/complement to Less-is-More for the Kazakh embedding track — it is unclaimed for any Cyrillic Turkic language.

Decision (3) — clearest unclaimed pan-Turkic artifact: no family-wide MTEB extension exists (only Turkish has TR-MTEB standalone; MMTEB has zero native Turkic tasks). A unified kk+uz+ky+az-MTEB submitted as one upstream PR (leveraging the lab's planned kk-MTEB work) would be a genuine first — flag this explicitly in the design-panel for the evallab embedding milestone.

Also unclaimed: an EMPIRICALLY-MEASURED Turkic Transfer Coefficient (arXiv:2604.06202 proposes it theoretically with zero numbers) — the lab's own eval harness, once ported to 2-3 more Turkic languages, could produce the first real cross-Turkic transfer numbers table (which source language/checkpoint transfers best to which target) as a citable atlas contribution.

Re-verify the Sherkala data-mixture ablation (Kazakh-only ~51% vs 3:1:3 mixture 'best') before citing it as cross-lingual-transfer evidence in the atlas — the WebFetch extraction is internally inconsistent (higher score with less/no cross-lingual data) and needs a direct read of Figure 1 / Table in the actual PDF, not a summarized fetch.

For the atlas's Kazakh-vs-Turkic-family positioning section, use the TUMLU-mini Claude-3.5-Sonnet ranking (tur 85.7 > aze 84.4 > tat 84.0 > kaz 83.0 > crh 81.2 > kaa 75.3 > uig 71.3 > uzb 69.1) as the headline citable number — it is native-script, natively-authored (not translated), and covers 8 languages plus Kazakh at once from a single paper/table.

Do not pursue Bashkir/Tatar/Turkmen/Uyghur as near-term collaboration targets — confirmed to have zero dedicated monolingual BERT/embedding model as of this sweep (only mGPT multilingual coverage + TurkicNLP's neural Stanza models), making them higher-lift than Uzbek/Kyrgyz for a first port.

research.area: turkic-embeddings-retrieval (non-Kazakh Turkic embedding/retrieval landscape, Kazakh as comparison anchor only)

findings.claim: [tr] TR-MTEB (Baysan & Güngör, Boğaziçi Univ., EMNLP 2025 Findings, aclanthology.org/2025.findings-emnlp.471) is the first large-scale Turkish embedding benchmark: 26 datasets across 6 tasks (8 classification, 2 clustering, 3 pair classification, 1 bitext mining, 1 STS, 11 retrieval — 4 are Turkish-translated BEIR sets: SQuAD-TR/MS MARCO-TR/XQuAD/Turkish QA plus 7 newly LLM-translated BEIR sets: NFCorpus-TR, ArguAna-TR, CQADupstack-TR, FiQA-TR, Quora-TR, SCIDOCS-TR, SciFact-TR). Full Table 2 leaderboard confirms mE5 dominance with EXACT numbers: multilingual-e5-large Mean(Task)=66.82/Mean(Type)=73.07 (retrieval 57.21, STS 81.18) is #1; their own best from-scratch-trained Turkish model (BERTurk-init, 34.2M weak pairs, contrastive-pretrain+fine-tune) reaches only 63.42/70.25 (retrieval 52.75), 3.4pt below mE5-large.
findings.source: aclanthology.org/2025.findings-emnlp.471 (PDF, Table 2, read directly)
findings.numbers: mE5-large 66.82/73.07 (retr 57.21, STS 81.18); mE5-large-instruct 65.92/72.78 (retr 57.51); gte-multilingual-base 64.49/71.96; mE5-base 64.26/70.98 (retr 58.29); text-embedding-3-small 66.61/69.52 (retr 64.99, HIGHEST retrieval of any model); their fine-tuned turkish-embedding-model 63.42/70.25 (retr 52.75); contrastive-only version 59.84/59.49 (bitext catastrophically low 37.7); LaBSE 57.60/66.60; bert-base-turkish-uncased 49.54/47.07 (bitext 7.07 — monolingual encoders fail cross-lingual bitext entirely)
findings.relevance: Directly extends KB's TurkEmbed finding with the EXACT primary-source leaderboard: a dedicated 34.2M-pair Turkish embedding effort still loses to off-the-shelf mE5-large by 3.4pt Mean(Task) and 4.5pt on retrieval specifically — same lesson as Kazakh's kazembed-v5/SozKZ, now with a second independent Turkic-family confirmation. Also: monolingual encoders score near-zero on bitext mining (7.07 vs mE5 99.43) — validates evallab's choice to measure retrieval/STS, not bitext, as the primary axis for a monolingual Kazakh/Uzbek model.

findings.claim: [uz] AugSBERT-Uz (Muminov & Allaberganova, Tashkent Univ. of Economics/TUIT, Science and Innovation journal, Nov 2025, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.17693973) is the FIRST sentence-level Uzbek embedding model, built via teacher(cross-encoder)-student(bi-encoder) distillation from monolingual BERTbek: teacher fine-tuned on ~5,000 human 'gold' pairs (positives from Uzbek-Kazakh parallel corpus + Uzbek-English translation pairs treated as equivalent, negatives random-sampled) reaches Spearman 85.0; BM25 top-50 candidate mining over a >150M-word unlabeled corpus (Uzbek CC-100 + uzWaC + BERTbek pretrain news) generates a silver set the teacher pseudo-labels; student bi-encoder (BERTbek + mean pooling + MNRL) trained on gold+silver reaches Spearman 83.2 (97.9% of teacher) in ~5s vs teacher's 65h for a 10k-sentence corpus (47,000x faster). Evaluated ONLY on SimRelUz (word-level test, adapted to sentence pairs) — NO mE5/BGE-M3 baseline was run; the only multilingual comparison point is zero-shot distiluse-base-multilingual at Spearman 61.0 (an older, weaker sentence-transformer, not mE5).
findings.source: scientists.uz/fileView?id=9807 (PDF, read directly, full paper)
findings.numbers: TF-IDF 35.0; avg FastText 42.5; distiluse-base-multilingual (zero-shot) 61.0; SBERT-Gold (gold-only, ~5k pairs) 70.5; AugSBERT-Uz (gold+silver) 83.2; BERTbek cross-encoder teacher (upper bound) 85.0; inference 5s (student) vs 65h (teacher) per 10k-sentence corpus
findings.relevance: Critical for the live Uzbek collaboration (decision 1): Uzbek has ZERO published mE5-large/BGE-M3 baseline number on its only STS set (SimRelUz) — the exact same gap kazembed-v5 filled for Kazakh on KazQAD. Any port of the lab's Less-is-More recipe to Uzbek must FIRST measure mE5-large on SimRelUz before claiming any beat-mE5 target. Also: Uzbek has no retrieval/QA dataset at all (STS only, word-level-derived) — porting KazQAD-style retrieval means building the eval set from scratch, unlike Kazakh where KazQAD already existed. The teacher-student BM25-mining recipe is a concrete, reusable bootstrap method for generating Uzbek training pairs cheaply.

findings.claim: [uz] Prior Uzbek NLP resources are monolingual-transformer-first, not embedding-first: UzBERT, UzRoBERTa, and BERTbek (monolingual BERT variants) 'have consistently outperformed multilingual models' on classification/NER, and SimRelUz (Kuriyozov et al. 2023) is the only standardized Uzbek semantic benchmark, but it is WORD-LEVEL similarity/relatedness, not sentence-level — AugSBERT-Uz had to manually adapt it into sentence pairs (e.g. wrapping word pairs into template sentences) for its evaluation, since no native sentence-level STS/NLI set exists for Uzbek.
findings.source: scientists.uz/fileView?id=9807 (paper's Related Work / Datasets section)
findings.relevance: Confirms Uzbek retrieval/STS eval infrastructure is far behind Kazakh's (KazQAD, KazParC): any Uzbek collaboration deliverable needs new eval-set construction as a first step, which is exactly the kind of upstream-mergeable artifact (native sentence-level Uzbek STS/retrieval set) that would fill unclaimed pan-Turkic territory (decision 3).

findings.claim: [ba][kk][ky] mteb/TurkicClassification is a currently-registered MMTEB task (topic/news classification, 80 label classes) spanning THREE non-Turkish Turkic languages simultaneously — Bashkir, Kazakh, Kyrgyz — sourced from Electrotubbie/classification_Turkic_languages on HF. 6,144 total rows (~2,050/language), license 'unknown'. This is classification only (no retrieval/STS/clustering).
findings.source: huggingface.co/datasets/mteb/TurkicClassification (dataset card, fetched directly)
findings.relevance: This is the ONLY genuinely pan-Turkic (beyond Turkish+Kazakh) task presently in the official MMTEB registry found in this sweep. It proves Bashkir and Kyrgyz already have an MTEB foothold via classification, but confirms retrieval/STS/clustering for ANY Turkic language except Turkish (and Kazakh's own KazQAD/Belebele/WebFAQ, per KB) is completely absent from the registry — direct evidence for decision 3 (unclaimed pan-Turkic benchmark territory) and worth checking before assuming a 'first pan-Turkic MTEB PR' claim, since a classification precedent already exists.

findings.claim: [az] LocalDoc-Azerbaijan/STS-Benchmark (GitHub, LocalDoc AI) benchmarks Azerbaijani-adapted SICK-R + STS12/13/15/16 sets against multilingual encoders. Result INVERTS the usual scaling trend: multilingual-e5-SMALL scores HIGHEST average Pearson (0.7577), beating e5-large-instruct (0.7280), e5-base (0.7242), and e5-large (0.6960) — the largest mE5 variant is the WORST of the four on Azerbaijani STS. Models evaluated: LaBSE, ColBERT-XM, all four mE5 sizes, BGE-M3 (exact BGE-M3 score not extracted). Also LocalDoc/az-en-MiniLM-L6-v2 (a small bilingual az-en model) is reported competitive with/exceeding larger multilingual models on this same benchmark.
findings.source: github.com/LocalDoc-Azerbaijan/STS-Benchmark (README, fetched via WebFetch)
findings.numbers: mE5-small 0.7577; mE5-large-instruct 0.7280; mE5-base 0.7242; mE5-large 0.6960 (avg Pearson across SICK-R+STS12/13/15/16-az)
findings.relevance: A dedicated native Azerbaijani STS test set already exists (unlike Uzbek/Kyrgyz), making Azerbaijani a fast, low-infrastructure-cost second target for the lab's evallab protocols. The large-vs-small inversion is a red flag worth independently re-verifying (possible overfitting/noise/leakage in the small mE5 checkpoint or a broken large-model eval) before quoting — evallab should re-run this under its own pinned protocol rather than trust the GitHub number as-is.

findings.claim: [az][crh][kaa][kk][ky][tt][tr][ug][uz] TUMLU / TUMLU-mini (Isbarov et al., arXiv:2502.11020, ACL 2025) is a NATIVE (non-machine-translated) MMLU-style benchmark spanning 9 Turkic languages, sourced from real university-entrance-exam questions, manually verified by native speakers, 7-11 subjects. TUMLU-mini = 6,017 examples total (700/lang mostly, less for low-resource: Crimean Tatar 417, Karakalpak 315, Uyghur 494, Kyrgyz 698). 5-shot results (mean across all 9 langs, then per-lang for kk/tr/uz): Claude 3.5 Sonnet mean 78.9 (tur 85.7 highest, tat 84.0, aze 84.4, kaz 83.0, kir 75.7, crh 81.2, uig 71.3, kaa n/a in this row set, uzb 69.1 LOWEST); GPT-4o mean 74.9 (tur 83.7, kaz 81.0, uzb 65.4); Qwen2.5-72B mean 59.9 (tur 73.9, kaz 62.6, uzb 50.4, kir 47.5 lowest for this model).
findings.source: arxiv.org/html/2502.11020v2 (fetched directly, results table extracted)
findings.numbers: Claude-3.5-Sonnet: mean 78.9, tur 85.7, tat 84.0, aze 84.4, kaz 83.0, crh 81.2, kaa 75.3, kir 75.7, uig 71.3, uzb 69.1. GPT-4o: mean 74.9, tur 83.7, kaz 81.0, uzb 65.4. Llama-3.1-8B: mean 40.3, tur 47.7, kaz 46.4, uzb 29.9 (lowest)
findings.relevance: Directly answers decision 2 (family positioning): on this NATIVE pan-Turkic knowledge benchmark, Kazakh consistently ranks 3rd-5th of 9 (behind Turkish/Tatar/Azerbaijani, ahead of Kyrgyz/Uyghur/Crimean-Tatar/Karakalpak/Uzbek across all 6 evaluated models), with Uzbek consistently LAST or near-last despite Uzbek's larger speaker population — contradicts a naive 'bigger population = better LLM performance' assumption and should anchor the atlas's Kazakh-vs-family ranking claim (cite TUMLU, not the qualitative 'Rising Star' survey label, when a numeric per-language rank is needed).

findings.claim: [pan-turkic][kk][az][ky][uz] Raw web-crawl volume (CC-100, used to train XLM-R) ranks Turkic languages DIFFERENTLY than curated-resource surveys: Azerbaijani 783M tokens/6.5GiB > Kazakh 476M tokens/6.4GiB > Kyrgyz 94M tokens/1.2GiB > Uzbek 91M tokens/0.7GiB. This means Azerbaijani, not Kazakh, has the largest raw pretraining-corpus footprint among these four in the exact corpus that trained XLM-R/mE5's tokenizer vocabulary.
findings.source: CC-100 corpus statistics (via XLM-R paper arXiv:1911.02116), figures synthesized from search results, not directly read from a table — needs primary-source re-verification
findings.numbers: az 783M tok/6.5GiB; kk 476M tok/6.4GiB; ky 94M tok/1.2GiB; uz 91M tok/0.7GiB
findings.relevance: Creates tension with arXiv:2407.05006's qualitative ranking (Kazakh='Rising Star' > Uzbek='Hopeful' > Kyrgyz/Turkmen='Scraping-Bys') which is based on curated task-dataset counts, not raw pretraining volume. The atlas should explicitly distinguish 'curated/task-dataset resourcing' (Kazakh clearly ahead) from 'raw web-crawl pretraining volume' (Azerbaijani ahead) as two DIFFERENT axes when positioning Kazakh in the family — do not conflate them into a single ranking.

findings.claim: [kk][uz][ky][tk] arXiv:2407.05006 ('Recent Advancements and Challenges of Turkic Central Asian Language Processing') categorizes Kazakh as 'The Rising Star' (KazNERD, KazQAD, KazParC, KazSAnDRA, KSC2 speech 1,200+ hrs, KazakhTTS2 270+ hrs), Uzbek as 'The Hopeful' (UzWordNet, SimRelUz, USC speech corpus 14.3% WER), Kyrgyz as 'The Scraping-Bys' (Manas-UdS corpus only 84 texts, KyrgyzNews 250k articles), and Turkmen as the most resource-poor (Leipzig Univ. corpus 270k sentences, mostly poetry/literature). A downstream-task coverage table shows only Kazakh has BOTH question-answering AND text-generation research among these four languages; Turkmen has neither ASR nor NER.
findings.source: arxiv.org/pdf/2407.05006 (fetched, table content extracted)
findings.numbers: KSC2 1,200+ speech hours; KazakhTTS2 270+ hours; USC (Uzbek) WER 14.3%; Manas-UdS 84 texts; KyrgyzNews 250k articles; Leipzig Turkmen 270k sentences; QA task exists ONLY for Kazakh among the 4
findings.relevance: Confirms decision 1's implicit ranking for port order by curated-task-resource depth: Uzbek is the clear second choice after Kazakh (matches the live collaboration offer), Kyrgyz and Turkmen are much further behind and would need heavier greenfield data work before any KazQAD-style retrieval eval is feasible.

findings.claim: [az][ba][cv][kk][ky][sah][tk][tr][tt][ug][uz] BGE-M3's pretraining language list (from its CC-100/XLM-R-lineage tokenizer/training data, per HF discussion and FlagEmbedding GitHub issue #1228) nominally covers nearly the entire Turkic family already: az, azb, ba (Bashkir), cv (Chuvash), kk, ky, sah (Sakha/Yakut), tk (Turkmen), tr, tt (Tatar), tyv (Tuvan), ug (Uyghur), uz are all present in the raw list of ~170+ supported language codes — but the model card itself warns 'performance may reduce for low-resource languages' and NO per-Turkic-language MTEB score is published to confirm actual quality for any of these except the Kazakh numbers already in KB (Belebele kaz nDCG@10 0.9017).
findings.source: huggingface.co/BAAI/bge-m3/discussions/29; github.com/FlagOpen/FlagEmbedding/issues/1228
findings.relevance: Establishes that BGE-M3 (and by extension mE5, same CC-100 lineage) claims broad Turkic coverage at the pretraining-language-list level, but this is an UNVERIFIED quality claim for every Turkic language except Kazakh — any port decision should budget for an explicit BGE-M3/mE5 baseline measurement per target language (as evallab already does for Kazakh) rather than assume family-wide quality parity.

findings.claim: [tr] A community fine-tune of the exact backbone the lab plans to use — seroe/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B-turkish-triplet-matryoshka-v2 (HF, Apache-2.0) — already exists: fine-tuned on 215,676 Turkish triplets ('vodex-turkish-triplets-large', telecom domain) with MatryoshkaLoss+CachedMultipleNegativesRankingLoss across 1024/768/512/256 dims, batch 2,048, lr 5e-5, 1 epoch. Reported metrics are only in-domain triplet accuracy (99.8%+ at all dims vs 88.7% base init) — NO TR-MTEB or other standardized benchmark score is published for this checkpoint.
findings.source: huggingface.co/seroe/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B-turkish-triplet-matryoshka-v2 (model card, fetched directly)
findings.relevance: Existence-proof that Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B (the lab's planned base per KB) is already being independently adapted to a sibling Turkic language by hobbyists, but with an in-domain-only, non-rigorous eval — the lab's rigorous TR-MTEB-style evaluation of a Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B Turkish fine-tune remains an open, unclaimed comparison point relevant to validating that the same recipe transfers across the family.

findings.claim: [tr] TabiBERT (arXiv:2512.23065) is a ModernBERT-architecture Turkish foundation model reported to reach TR-MTEB retrieval NDCG@10 = 75.44, surpassing BERTurk's 74.84; a related ModernBERT-base checkpoint post-trained with a 'BGE-M3 guide' scores 55.67 MTEB/46.36 Legal-domain score, and newmindai/Mursit-Large-TR-Retrieval scores 56.87 MTEB/46.56 Legal.
findings.source: search-result snippets referencing arxiv.org/pdf/2512.23065 (PDF parsing failed; numbers not independently confirmed from the primary text)
findings.numbers: TabiBERT NDCG@10 75.44 vs BERTurk 74.84; ModernBERT+BGE-M3-guide 55.67 MTEB/46.36 Legal; Mursit-Large-TR-Retrieval 56.87 MTEB/46.56 Legal
findings.relevance: Suggests a NEWER (Dec 2025) modern-encoder-architecture Turkish retrieval model may be closing the gap with mE5/BGE-M3 specifically on retrieval, in contrast to TR-MTEB's 2025 finding that mE5-large still leads overall — worth a follow-up primary-source read before citing, since the source numbers here were not independently verified against the paper's own tables.

findings.claim: [tr] SQuAD-TR (machine-translated SQuAD2.0 via Amazon Translate, boun-tabi, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0) and STSb-TR (8,628 machine-translated STS-Benchmark pairs, 0-5 similarity scale, Beken Fikri et al. 2021) are the two most-used Turkish retrieval/STS resources feeding TR-MTEB's retrieval and STS tasks respectively — both are machine-translation-derived, and SQuAD-TR's NC-ND license blocks commercial reuse or redistribution of derivatives.
findings.source: tulap.cmpe.boun.edu.tr; github.com/boun-tabi/SQuAD-TR; hackmd.io/@data-tdd/r1zSlq5r5
findings.relevance: If the lab ever wants to reuse Turkish resources as auxiliary cross-lingual training signal for a Kazakh or pan-Turkic embedding model, SQuAD-TR's CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 license is a hard blocker for any commercially-released model — STSb-TR's license was not confirmed and should be checked before reuse.

recommendations: Port order for evallab's pinned protocols: Uzbek first (matches the live collaboration offer AND the curated-resource ranking, arXiv:2407.05006), but treat it as GREENFIELD retrieval infrastructure — Uzbek has zero KazQAD-analog retrieval/QA set and only one word-level-derived STS set (SimRelUz, sentence-adapted by AugSBERT-Uz). Concrete first step: run mE5-large and BGE-M3 on SimRelUz-sentence under evallab's own pinned protocol (no such baseline is published anywhere) before any 'beat mE5' claim for Uzbek is made — this is the exact kazembed-v5-shaped gap AugSBERT-Uz left open.

Azerbaijani second: reuse LocalDoc-Azerbaijan/STS-Benchmark (SICK-R + STS12/13/15/16-az) as an immediate, zero-build-cost STS eval, but re-run it under evallab's own harness first — the published result (mE5-small 0.7577 beating mE5-large 0.6960) is anomalous and should not be cited until independently reproduced.

For the atlas's Kazakh-vs-family positioning chapter, use TUMLU/TUMLU-mini (arXiv:2502.11020) as the primary NUMERIC anchor (native, non-MT, 9-language, multi-model) rather than the qualitative 'Rising Star/Hopeful/Scraping-By' labels from arXiv:2407.05006 — the two sources measure different things (LLM knowledge vs data/tooling maturity) and should be presented as two distinct axes, not merged into one ranking.

Explicitly separate 'curated task-dataset depth' (Kazakh clearly #1 of Uzbek/Kyrgyz/Turkmen) from 'raw CC-100 pretraining-corpus volume' (Azerbaijani's 783M tokens exceeds Kazakh's 476M) in any resource-ratio table in the survey — conflating them would produce a factually wrong 'Kazakh is the most-resourced non-Turkish Turkic language' claim that a reviewer with CC-100 numbers could immediately falsify.

For decision 3 (unclaimed pan-Turkic benchmark territory): mteb/TurkicClassification (ba/kk/ky, classification-only, license 'unknown', ~2,050 rows/lang) is the only non-Turkish pan-Turkic MMTEB task found — a genuinely novel, upstream-mergeable lab artifact would be a pan-Turkic RETRIEVAL or STS suite (kk+uz+az+ky at minimum, reusing KazQAD's query-construction methodology plus AugSBERT-Uz's BM25-mining recipe for Uzbek and LocalDoc's STS sets for Azerbaijani) submitted as an MMTEB PR — this task type is currently completely empty for the family outside Turkish and Kazakh.

Do not frame a future Turkish-language embedding effort as a target for the lab — TR-MTEB (26 datasets, EMNLP 2025) already shows a dedicated 34.2M-pair Turkish effort losing to mE5-large by 3.4pt Mean(Task)/4.5pt retrieval; this is now a TWO-language-family confirmation (kk + tr) of the KB's 'from-scratch loses to mE5' finding and should be cited as corroborating, not just Kazakh-specific, evidence in the SLM/embedding papers.

Before citing TabiBERT's 75.44 NDCG@10 (vs BERTurk 74.84) as evidence that Turkish retrieval is closing the mE5 gap, do a direct primary-source PDF read (WebFetch failed to parse it in this sweep) — if verified, it would be the first Turkic-family counter-example to the 'mE5 still wins' pattern and deserves a dedicated look before the atlas's pan-Turkic embedding chapter is finalized.

findings.claim: [uz] CulturaX's Uzbek slice is the smallest of the four candidates: 75,250,787 tokens across 87,219 documents, per the dataset's own per-language statistics table.
findings.source: HF dataset card uonlp/CulturaX (README.md language stats table); paper arXiv:2309.09400 (Nguyen et al., CulturaX, LREC-COLING 2024)

findings.claim: [uz][kk] CC-100 (the XLM-R paper's corpus) reports Uzbek at 91M tokens / 0.7 GiB, built from a single 2018 CommonCrawl snapshot via cc-net; the same table gives Kazakh 476M tokens / 6.4 GiB in the same era-matched pipeline — i.e. Uzbek was ~5.2x smaller than Kazakh in this single-snapshot 2019-era source.

findings.relevance: Confirms the Kazakh-KB-known 'Kazakh 5.8x smaller than Turkish' framing extends consistently: in this OLDER single-snapshot corpus family Uzbek trails Kazakh by a similar multiplier region (~5x), but this era is now superseded by FineWeb2 below.

findings.claim: [uz][kk] FineWeb2 (2025, 96 CommonCrawl snapshots 2013-2024, per-language-tuned filtering+global dedup) is the largest and most current CC-derived source, and gives EXACT per-script counts: uzn_Latn train = 687,002,994 words / 1,233,463 docs / 4.45GB raw text (1.90GB parquet); uzn_Cyrl train = 544,866,919 words / 1,357,811 docs / 6.12GB raw text (1.83GB parquet). Combined both scripts = 1,231,869,913 words (~1.23B) / 2,591,274 docs / 10.57GB text — this is the true source of the '~1.109B' figure in the question (a rounding/earlier-commit variant of the current combined-script sum, or possibly Latin-only-plus-test).
findings.source: Penedo et al. 2025, 'FineWeb2: One Pipeline to Scale Them All', arXiv:2506.20920; official per-language CSV github.com/huggingface/fineweb-2/blob/main/fineweb2-language-distribution.csv (fetched raw, rows for uzn_Latn/uzn_Cyrl train+test+removed); dataset ODC-By license

findings.relevance: This is the number the lab should treat as ground truth for 'realistic Uzbek web-text budget' if porting the FineWeb2/pinned-protocol pipeline — reported 'words' (whitespace tokens), NOT subword/BPE tokens, so expect ~1.2-1.6x more actual training tokens after tokenization (not directly measured for Uzbek; flagged uncertain by extrapolation only).

findings.claim: [uz][kk] Apples-to-apples same-pipeline comparison (FineWeb2 CSV): Kazakh kaz_Cyrl train = 1,876,843,453 words / 3,344,366 docs / 20.67GB text / 6.33GB parquet. findings.source: github.com/huggingface/fineweb-2/blob/main/fineweb2-language-distribution.csv (rows kaz_Cyrl vs uzn_Latn/uzn_Cyrl), same source as above
