The '~37x worse' claim is only defensible if the port pipeline is restricted to CulturaX specifically (75M tok) vs Kazakh's own CulturaX-scale pool — it is NOT true of the best available raw web data (FineWeb2).

findings.claim: [uz][kk][ky][az] The original mT5-era mC4 (2020, pre-CulturaX, single-snapshot generation) reports Uzbek = 0.9B tokens / 0.8M pages (0.46% of mT5 mixture) vs Kazakh 3.1B tokens / 2.4M pages (0.65%), Kyrgyz 1.0B tokens / 1.0M pages (0.50%), Azerbaijani 4.4B tokens / 5.3M pages (0.82%), Turkish 71B tokens / 88M pages (1.93%).
findings.source: Xue et al. 2020, 'mT5: A Massively Multilingual Pre-trained Text-to-Text Transformer', arXiv:2010.11934, Table 6 (fetched PDF directly, verified row values)
findings.numbers: uz 0.9B tok/0.8M pages; kk 3.1B tok/2.4M pages; ky 1.0B tok/1.0M pages; az 4.4B tok/5.3M pages; tr 71B tok/88M pages
findings.relevance: Shows Uzbek and Kyrgyz sit in the same low-resource tier (~0.9-1.0B mC4 tokens each), both well below Kazakh/Azerbaijani and far below Turkish — useful for Decision 1 ranking of port order if FineWeb2-scale corpora are unavailable for some candidate language and mC4/CulturaX-class resources must be used instead.

findings.claim: [uz] The '~5B tokens' TahrirchiBERT figure is NOT a comparable web-crawl-only number: it draws on tahrirchi/uz-crawl (1,618,035 docs = 1,250,018 news + 368,017 Telegram-blog docs, 5.1GB total disk, sourced from 57 news sites + 128 curated Telegram channels — proprietary scraping, not CommonCrawl) plus a Latin-normalized subset of tahrirchi/uz-books (~40,000 OCR'd books, 16.98GB downloaded / 32.95GB generated across Cyrillic-OCR and Latin versions, with acknowledged noisy Tesseract OCR quality).
findings.source: Mamasaidov & Shopulatov 2023 (Tahrirchi), corpus described via HF dataset cards tahrirchi/uz-crawl and tahrirchi/uz-books, and characterized (incl. '5B tokens ≈18.5GB', OCR noise caveat) in Israilova et al. 2025 'BBPOS: BERT-based Part-of-Speech Tagging for Uzbek', arXiv:2501.10107

findings.relevance: The 5B-token number should NOT be used as 'Uzbek's true monolingual pretraining corpus size' for a web-crawl-style port (KazQAD-style retrieval / Less-is-More recipe assumes CC-style web text); it mixes non-CC proprietary Telegram scraping and noisy OCR'd book text with distinct quality/legal-provenance profiles, and is not license-clear for redistribution the way FineWeb2 (ODC-By) is.

findings.claim: [uz] Verdict on reconciliation: treat FineWeb2's exact figures (687M words Latin-only script / ~1.23B words combining Latin+Cyrillic, both CC-derived, per-language filtered, ODC-By licensed, exactly reproducible via the published CSV) as the canonical 'true monolingual pretraining-corpus size' estimate for Uzbek web text — NOT CulturaX's 75M (artifact of aggressive dedup over few snapshots), NOT CC-100's 91M (single stale 2018 snapshot), and NOT Tahrirchi's 5B (different source mix, OCR noise, unclear license for full redistribution).
findings.source: Synthesis of the four sources above; FineWeb2 CSV is the only one offering exact, script-separated, recently-crawled, license-clear numbers verifiable independently of the paper's prose
findings.numbers: Recommended canonical estimate: 687M words (uzn_Latn only) to 1.23B words (uzn_Latn+uzn_Cyrl combined), ~10.6GB raw text, ODC-By license
findings.relevance: Directly unblocks Decision 1: an Uzbek port on FineWeb2 data is workable at roughly HALF-to-two-thirds of Kazakh's own FineWeb2 scale (1.52x-2.73x smaller, not 15x-66x), which supports treating it as a 'workable Kazakh-order scale' port rather than a low-data/synthetic-pair-only effort — provided the pipeline is built on FineWeb2, not CulturaX.

recommendations: Build the Uzbek port's pretraining/retrieval-corpus pipeline on FineWeb2 (uzn_Latn + optionally uzn_Cyrl configs), NOT CulturaX or CC-100 — FineWeb2 is ~9-16x larger than CulturaX's Uzbek slice and ~7-13x larger than CC-100's, is the most recently crawled (2013-2024, 96 snapshots), per-language filtered, and ODC-By licensed for clean redistribution.

When deciding language port order for the pinned KazQAD-style/MTEB-style protocols, use the FineWeb2 apples-to-apples ratio (kk:uz = 1.52x combined-script, 2.73x Latin-only) rather than the CC-100-era ratio (5.2x) or the mC4-2020-era ratio (3.4x) — the resource gap has narrowed substantially in the newest corpus and does not justify treating Uzbek as a 'low-data/synthetic-pair-only' effort.

Do not cite the Tahrirchi '5B tokens' figure as directly comparable to Kazakh's own web-crawl-only corpus size in the atlas/survey — flag it explicitly as a mixed-source (Telegram + OCR'd books) number with a distinct, noisier provenance, separate from the CC-lineage figures.

For the atlas/survey's Kazakh-vs-Turkic-family resource-ratio table, report BOTH the FineWeb2 numbers (current, apples-to-apples, smallest gap) and the CC-100/mC4 numbers (historical, larger gap) side by side rather than picking one — the two eras disagree by nearly an order of magnitude on the size of the gap, which is itself a citable finding about how crawl-recency/dedup methodology affects perceived resource inequality for Turkic languages.

Re-verify the exact subword/BPE token count (not just whitespace 'words') for the Uzbek FineWeb2 subset before finalizing any token-budget number in a paper — the reported 687M/545M are word counts; the true fertility-adjusted token count for Uzbek agglutinative morphology is currently unmeasured and should get its own dedicated fertility study (mirroring the Kazakh 4.7-4.9 tok/word finding) rather than an assumed 1.2-1.6x multiplier.

Does CulturaX's 'uz' config combine Latin+Cyrillic scripts or only one — the HF card did not disambiguate script, which matters for reconciling its 75M-token figure against FineWeb2's script-separated 687M(Latn)/545M(Cyrl)?

What license terms attach to the Tahrirchi uz-crawl/uz-books corpora (proprietary Telegram scraping + OCR'd books) — is redistribution/inclusion in a lab pipeline permissible, or is it eval/reference-only?

gapFills.area: Non-Kazakh Turkic NLP landscape — embedding retrieval axis: does mE5-large's retrieval dominance survive in-family? (Turkish deep-dive; Uzbek/pan-Turkic scan)

findings.claim: [tr] On TR-MTEB's RETRIEVAL-SPECIFIC column (not aggregate), multilingual-e5-large IS beaten — but only by OpenAI's proprietary text-embedding-3-small, not by any dedicated Turkish/Turkic model. Full retrieval column from the paper's own Table 2: mE5-large 63.74, text-embedding-3-small 64.99 (+1.25), mE5-base 58.29, gte-multilingual-base 57.51, mE5-large-instruct 57.21, mE5-small 56.53. TR-MTEB's own purpose-built Turkish embedder (BERTurk-base 110M, contrastively pretrained on 34.2M Turkish pairs + supervised fine-tuned) scores only 52.75 retrieval — LOSES to mE5-large by 10.99 points despite winning Pair-Classification (71.03 vs 65.01) and STS (78.44 vs 81.18 is close).
findings.source: aclanthology.org/2025.findings-emnlp.471 (TR-MTEB, EMNLP 2025 Findings, Baysan & Gungor), Table 2 — fetched and OCR'd directly from PDF
findings.numbers: Retr. column: mE5-large 63.74; text-embedding-3-small 64.99; mE5-base 58.29; gte-multilingual-base 57.51; mE5-large-instruct 57.21; mE5-small 56.53; turkish-embedding-model-fine-tuned (110M) 52.75; turkish-embedding-model (contrastive-only) 52.54; paraphrase-multilingual-mpnet-base-v2 49.27
findings.relevance: Directly answers the sweep question with a primary source: mE5-large's retrieval crown in the Turkic family is NOT unbroken in absolute terms, but the only challenger is a general-purpose SOTA proprietary model, not a Turkic-specialized one — so the lab's 'beat mE5-large on KazQAD' target remains meaningfully hard and unclaimed by any dedicated-Turkic effort so far.

findings.claim: [tr] TabiBERT's headline '75.44 NDCG@10, surpassing BERTurk's 74.84' retrieval claim (arXiv:2512.23065) is NOT a counter-example to mE5-large's dominance — it never compares against mE5-large, text-embedding-3-small, BGE-M3, or any dedicated text-embedding model at all. Its retrieval evaluation ('TabiBench', Appendix A.1.6/Table 11) is restricted to 5 BERT-family encoder foundation models: TurkishBERTweet (163M, IR 68.40 weighted-avg... actually per-dataset weighted avg 68.40 total metric not IR-only, see numbers field), YTU-Cosmos-BERT (111M, 74.29), BERTurk (110M, 74.84), TabiBERT (149M, 75.44), mmBERT (307M, higher, exact IR number for mmBERT not fully captured but total-avg 79.26). Dataset set: BiText/MsMarco-TR/Scifact-TR/Fiqa-TR/NFCorpus-TR/Quora-TR (translated BEIR subset via TR-MTEB group).
findings.source: arxiv.org/pdf/2512.23065 (TabiBERT: A Large-Scale ModernBERT Foundation Model and Unified Benchmarking Framework for Turkish), directly downloaded and pdftotext-parsed, Table 11 + prose (lines ~2317-2440 of extracted text)
findings.numbers: IR NDCG@10 weighted avg: TurkishBERTweet 68.40, YTU-Cosmos-BERT 74.29, BERTurk 74.84, TabiBERT 75.44, mmBERT not isolated in extract (total avg 79.26). No mE5/OpenAI/BGE baseline present anywhere in the 33-page paper (grep confirmed zero mentions of 'e5' or 'E5').
findings.relevance: This resolves the KB's standing flag ('TabiBERT failed PDF verification in every sweep') definitively: TabiBERT is genuinely NOT a valid counter-example to mE5-large's retrieval dominance — it is an encoder-vs-encoder comparison at a different weight class (110-307M BERT-style) that simply never tested against the SOTA embedding models the lab is targeting. Any future lab citation of TabiBERT as 'beating mE5' would be a factual error and should be actively suppressed.

findings.claim: [tr] The instruction-tuned variant multilingual-e5-large-instruct — often assumed to be the stronger/newer mE5 variant — actually scores WORSE than plain multilingual-e5-large on retrieval specifically in Turkish (57.21 vs 63.74, a 6.53-point gap), even though it wins some other task types (Classification 73.70 vs 71.77, Clustering 61.78 vs 60.42).
findings.source: aclanthology.org/2025.findings-emnlp.471, Table 2
findings.numbers: Retr.: mE5-large 63.74 vs mE5-large-instruct 57.21 (-6.53); Class.: 71.77 vs 73.70 (+1.93 for instruct)
findings.relevance: The lab's canonical embedding target is plain mE5-large, not the instruct variant — this confirms that choice is retrieval-optimal and that the KB's Armenian/Belebele-kk numbers (which used mE5-large-instruct for some rows) should not be conflated with the base-model retrieval baseline the lab is trying to beat.

findings.claim: [uz] No Uzbek-specific retrieval benchmark, embedding leaderboard, or mE5-large head-to-head comparison surfaced in this sweep (web search for 'Uzbek text embedding retrieval NDCG mE5 2026' returned only generic multilingual-mE5 claims with zero Uzbek-specific numbers). Combined with KB's existing Less-is-More finding that Cyrillic-script low-resource languages sharing a script with a high-resource neighbor are explicitly flagged as UNTESTED by that paper's own authors, the Uzbek retrieval gap is currently completely unmeasured in the literature.
findings.source: WebSearch queries 'Uzbek text embedding model retrieval NDCG mE5 2026' and 'Turkic MTEB pan-Turkic embedding benchmark Kyrgyz Azerbaijani Tatar' (no primary source found; absence-of-evidence claim)
findings.numbers: N/A — zero published NDCG/MRR numbers found for Uzbek retrieval with any embedder
findings.relevance: For decision (1): porting KazQAD-style retrieval + Less-is-More to Uzbek would be a genuinely first-of-kind artifact (no prior Uzbek retrieval-embedding benchmark exists to replicate/beat), unlike Turkish where TR-MTEB + TabiBERT already occupy the space. This strengthens the case for prioritizing the live Uzbek collaboration offer as the first port target.

findings.claim: [pan-turkic] Existing pan-Turkic evaluation resources found (mteb/TurkicClassification on HF; TUMLU benchmark covering 9 Turkic languages — az, crh, tr, ug, uz, kaa, ky, kk, tt — with 38K multiple-choice questions) are classification/knowledge-QA benchmarks, NOT retrieval/embedding benchmarks. No pan-Turkic retrieval or embedding-specific benchmark (i.e., a Turkic-family analogue of KazQAD or TR-MTEB's retrieval split, spanning multiple Turkic languages at once) was found to exist as of this sweep.
findings.source: HF dataset mteb/TurkicClassification; github.com/ceferisbarov/TUMLU; aclanthology.org/2025.acl-long.1112 (TUMLU paper, ACL 2025)
findings.numbers: TUMLU: 9 languages, 38K MC questions (knowledge/language-understanding, not retrieval)
findings.relevance: For decision (3): the retrieval axis of pan-Turkic benchmarking is unclaimed territory family-wide, not just for Kazakh — even Turkish (the best-resourced Turkic language) only has a single-language retrieval benchmark (TR-MTEB), and no pan-Turkic retrieval MTEB exists. A Turkic-wide retrieval benchmark (built on the lab's KazQAD-style protocol methodology) would be genuinely novel and could be a higher-leverage lab artifact than a Kazakh-only one — but is a much larger scope commitment.

findings.claim: [tr] TR-MTEB's own specialized Turkish embedding models (contrastively pretrained from BERTurk on 34.2M weakly-supervised Turkish pairs, then supervised fine-tuned) underperform mE5-large on EVERY task category except Pair Classification and are dramatically worse at Bitext Mining (37.7-86.88 vs mE5-large's 99.43), because monolingual training provides no cross-lingual signal — confirming that a from-scratch or single-language-fine-tuned embedder trades away cross-lingual/bitext capability for modest task-specific gains.
findings.source: aclanthology.org/2025.findings-emnlp.471, Table 2 and Section 4 discussion ('Bitext Mining Challenge')
findings.numbers: Bitext: turkish-embedding-model-fine-tuned 86.88 / turkish-embedding-model (contrastive only) 37.7 vs mE5-large 99.43 and LaBSE 99.53; overall Mean(Task): mE5-large 66.82 vs turkish-embedding-model-fine-tuned 63.42
findings.relevance: Directly informs the lab's own architecture choice: if the Kazakh embedding effort ever considers a from-scratch or monolingual-only fine-tune path (vs. Less-is-More's approach of lightly adapting mE5-base while keeping its multilingual backbone), the Turkish precedent shows monolingual specialization sacrifices bitext/cross-lingual retrieval (relevant given heavy kk/ru code-switching) for gains that don't even reach mE5-large's aggregate score.

recommendations: Update the KB's TR-MTEB node (arXiv/ACL 2025.findings-emnlp.471) to add the RETRIEVAL-SPECIFIC column breakdown (currently only the aggregate 61.77-vs-61.41-vs-61.58 style numbers or generic 'did not surpass mE5' framing are recorded) — the retrieval axis specifically shows mE5-large at 63.74, beaten only by text-embedding-3-small (64.99), with the Turkish-specific model at 52.75.

Correct/annotate any lab framing that cites TabiBERT (arXiv:2512.23065) as evidence against mE5-large's retrieval dominance — it is a category error (BERT-encoder-vs-BERT-encoder comparison, never tested against mE5-large or any SOTA embedding model). This closes the KB's standing 'TabiBERT failed PDF verification' flag with a definitive negative result.

For decision (1) — port the KazQAD-style retrieval protocol + Less-is-More recipe to Uzbek FIRST, ahead of other Turkic languages: no Uzbek retrieval-embedding benchmark or mE5-large comparison exists yet (unlike Turkish, which already has TR-MTEB + TabiBERT occupying the space), so an Uzbek KazQAD-analogue would be genuinely first-of-kind and pairs with the live collaboration offer.

For decision (2)/paper framing — position Kazakh's retrieval-embedding maturity relative to Turkish (the family's most-resourced language): Turkish already has a dedicated retrieval benchmark (TR-MTEB) and a from-scratch encoder (TabiBERT) attempting to beat mE5-large's retrieval score, yet NEITHER a Turkish-specialized model has actually surpassed mE5-large on retrieval; Kazakh (KazQAD) is earlier-stage (no dense embedder has even been formally evaluated under a fixed protocol per KB). This gives the atlas a clean 'behind Turkish in benchmark maturity, but the underlying retrieval-superiority problem is unsolved even where the benchmark exists' framing.

For decision (3) — a pan-Turkic retrieval/embedding benchmark (unlike TUMLU/TurkicClassification, which are knowledge/classification-only) is unclaimed territory across the WHOLE family, not just Kazakh; flag this as a candidate high-leverage lab artifact but treat as a large-scope commitment requiring its own design-panel before greenlighting, per the apparatus freeze.

findings.claim: [az][pan-turkic] The closest prior-art threat — 'Knowledge Distillation for Embeddings of Low-Resource Turkic Family Languages' (Aghalarov, Mammadov, Huseynova, Baku Higher Oil School) — is confirmed real, published, and its headline 89% figure is a RAG top-1 retrieval accuracy on a 100-question Azerbaijani LEGAL QA set (Jina-v3 Multi-Task model), not a KazQAD/MTEB-style full-corpus retrieval metric. Full numbers from primary source (read all 14 pages of the PDF): BGE-M3 Azerbaijani STS 79.3->85.0 (+5.7pts, new SOTA on local benchmark) while retaining 98.6% of original English MTEB STS score (74.1->73.1). Jina-v3 Multi-Task: AZ-STS 84.8, BeleBele-az 90.3, English-STS 75.6 (vs vanilla Jina-v3 84.0/88.2/77.1). RAG pipeline (LLaMA-3.3-70B, Milvus, 100 legal FAQ questions, 2 human raters, Cohen's kappa 0.82): Jina Multi-Task Top-1 89.0%/Top-3 95.1%, human eval avg score 1.92/2, 94% 'Excellent'; vanilla Jina baseline was already 86.8% Top-1/84% Excellent -- so the KD gain over a strong off-the-shelf baseline is only +2.2pp Top-1 / +10pp Excellent, not a dramatic leap.
findings.source: Aghalarov et al. 2026, GU J Sci Part A 13(1):334-347, DOI 10.54287/gujsa.1844025 (full PDF read, all 14 pages)
findings.numbers: AZ-STS 79.3->85.0 (BGE-M3); English MTEB retention 98.6%; RAG Top-1 89.0%/Top-3 95.1% (Jina MT) vs vanilla Jina 86.8%/89.9%; %Excellent 94 vs 84 vanilla
findings.relevance: Directly answers the research question: quantifies exactly what the Azerbaijani paper claims and shows the 89% figure is domain-specific (legal RAG), not a general Turkic retrieval SOTA, and the delta over vanilla off-the-shelf embeddings is modest -- weakens (but does not eliminate) the pre-emption risk for a Kazakh/pan-Turkic embedding-distillation claim.

findings.claim: [az][pan-turkic] The Azerbaijani paper's Turkic-generalizability claim is EXPLICITLY ASPIRATIONAL, not tested: verbatim from the Conclusion, 'While Azerbaijani served as our case study, the framework has broad implications for other low-resource languages in the Turkic family, including Turkish, Kazakh, Uzbek, Kyrgyz, and Turkmen... We anticipate that the performance gains observed for Azerbaijani will transfer to other Turkic languages facing similar data scarcity challenges.' No Kazakh data, model, or benchmark appears anywhere in the paper -- zero Kazakh evaluation, zero Kazakh training data, zero Kazakh-specific results. The method (MSE distillation from a frozen English teacher + multi-task bilingual contrastive loss on translated SNLI, alpha=0.3, on 5x RTX4090) is a straightforward cross-lingual KD recipe with no Kazakh-specific innovation.
findings.source: Aghalarov et al. 2026, GU J Sci Part A 13(1):334-347, Conclusion section (p.345-346), full PDF read
findings.numbers: 0 Kazakh data points; 300k EN-AZ Wikipedia parallel corpus; 300k translated SNLI pairs (NLLB-200 3.3B); alpha=0.3 chosen via 5-point sweep (0.1/0.3/0.5/0.7/0.9)
findings.relevance: This is the single most decision-critical finding: the paper does NOT pre-empt a Kazakh embedding-distillation claim on the merits -- it only asserts transfer without evidence. A lab artifact that actually trains and measures on Kazakh (via evallab's pinned KazQAD protocol) would be the first REAL Turkic-family test of this class of recipe, not a duplicate.

It has NEVER been tested on any Turkic language. This is a direct, load-bearing gap: the exact recipe the lab plans to port to Kazakh/Uzbek has zero prior Turkic validation.

findings.numbers: 10k synthetic pairs -> 11-12% avg benchmark improvement, 20%+ relative retrieval improvement, matches 1M-pair baseline; base model mE5; languages: Armenian + 1 unspecified unique-script LRL (NOT Turkic)

Tatar Wikipedia shows 708,887 articles / 216.1M words, MORE than Turkish (689,022 articles / 192.2M words) — almost certainly a bot-stub artifact (cf. Cebuano Wikipedia's well-documented bot-inflation pattern) and should NOT be read as Tatar having more organic content than Turkish.
findings.source: Live query to kk/az/uz/tr/ky/tt.wikipedia.org MediaWiki API (action=query&meta=siteinfo&siprop=statistics), 2026-07-05.
findings.relevance: Third independent, live-current source triangulating the same direction as CC-100 and FineWeb2 — Azerbaijani leads Kazakh in raw text depth even though Kazakh has more Wikipedia pages; also flags a Tatar-article-count trap the atlas must not cite naively.

findings.claim: [az][kk][tr][uz][ky][uig][kaa][crh(Crimean Tatar)][tt] On TUMLU-mini (native-language-authored, non-translated, 4-choice MCQA across 8 Turkic languages, 5-shot), Azerbaijani BEATS Kazakh on every one of the 5 evaluated models, not the reverse: Claude-3.5-Sonnet az 84.4 vs kk 83.0; GPT-4o az 82.4 vs kk 81.0; Gemma-2-9B az 53.7 vs kk 49.1; Llama-3.1-8B az 48.4 vs kk 46.4; Qwen2.5-7B az 48.0 vs kk 45.0. The paper's own difficulty caveat ('Uzbek and Turkish datasets are particularly difficult because those questions are designed to mirror university entrance examinations') applies to Uzbek/Turkish, NOT to Azerbaijani/Kazakh — both of which the paper says derive from 'community-developed materials with varying rigor' — so the Az>Kk gap is NOT explained away by the paper's stated confound; it stands as a genuine (if modest, 1.4-4.6pp) Azerbaijani edge on the one native-authored shared benchmark that exists.
findings.source: TUMLU: A Unified and Native Language Understanding Benchmark for Turkic Languages (arXiv:2502.11020 / ACL 2025), Table 2, verified via direct fetch of arxiv.org/html/2502.11020.
findings.numbers: Az vs Kk per model: Claude 84.4/83.0; GPT-4o 82.4/81.0; Gemma-2-9B 53.7/49.1; Llama-3.1-8B 48.4/46.4; Qwen2.5-7B 48.0/45.0. TUMLU-mini per-lang Q counts: az 700, kk 700, tr 700, uz 700, ky 698, tt 700, crh 417, kaa 215, uig 494.
findings.relevance: This directly falsifies the sweep's prior framing that Kazakh is '#1' on curated-task accuracy — on the one benchmark built for genuinely fair cross-Turkic comparison, Azerbaijani is ahead, not Kazakh. The atlas cannot claim Kazakh leads on the accuracy axis.

findings.claim: [kk][az] Kazakh DOES lead on a different, distinct axis: breadth of the dedicated NLP research/benchmark ECOSYSTEM (count and diversity of native, purpose-built datasets and models), not raw volume or shared-benchmark accuracy. Kazakh has at least 8 dedicated artifacts with papers: KazNERD (112,000+ sentences, 25 entity classes), KazQAD (~6,000 questions, ~12,000 passage-relevance judgments), KazParC (371,902 parallel kk-en-ru-tr sentences), KazMMLU (23,000 MCQs), KazSAnDRA (sentiment), plus THREE dedicated decoder LLMs: Sherkala-8B/Sherkala-Chat (adapted Llama-3.1), SozKZ (587M from-scratch), KazByte (byte-adapter Qwen). The comparable Azerbaijani effort found (aLLMA family, arXiv:2407.02337) is ENCODER-ONLY (aLLMA-Small 45.9M / Base 135.2M / Large 369.5M params, still training at publication) trained on the DOLLMA corpus (651.1M words) with benchmarks AZE-SCI (5.76k), AZE-NSP (9.15k), CB-MCQ (released but 'all tested models failed to learn this... even at a basic level' per the authors), WikiANN-az NER (12k), plus MOSTLY TRANSLATED tasks (SQuAD-az 54.1k, MRPC-az 3.67k) rather than natively authored ones — no dedicated Azerbaijani DECODER/generative LLM was found in this search.
findings.source: KazNERD/KazQAD/KazParC/KazMMLU per KB (arXiv:2111.13419, 2404.04487, 2403.19399, 2502.12829); Sherkala arXiv:2503.01493; SozKZ arXiv:2603.20854 (KB); KazByte arXiv:2603.27859 (KB, title only); Azerbaijani: 'Open foundation models for Azerbaijani language' arXiv:2407.02337, fetched directly.
findings.numbers: kk: KazNERD 112K sent/25 classes; KazQAD 6K Q/12K judgments; KazParC 371,902 pairs; KazMMLU 23K Q; 3 decoder LLMs (8B, 587M, adapter). az: DOLLMA 651.1M words; aLLMA 45.9M/135.2M/369.5M (encoder-only); AZE-SCI 5.76K; AZE-NSP 9.15K; SQuAD-az 54.1K (translated); 0 dedicated decoder LLMs found.
findings.relevance: This is Kazakh's genuinely defensible leadership claim for the atlas — narrowly scoped to 'dedicated benchmark/model ecosystem breadth,' not to raw data volume or shared-benchmark accuracy, where Azerbaijani leads. This scoping is what makes the atlas claim falsification-proof.

findings.claim: [kk][az][uz] RECONCILED single-axis verdict: Kazakh is NOT ahead of Azerbaijani when reduced to one axis at a time on data volume or accuracy — Azerbaijani leads Kazakh on CC-100 tokens (1.64x), FineWeb2 2024-snapshot volume (1.65-2.17x), Wikipedia total words (1.93x), and TUMLU-mini native-benchmark accuracy (ahead on all 5 tested models, +1.4 to +4.6pp). Kazakh's only defensible lead is ecosystem breadth (dedicated dataset/model count), which is a research-output metric, not a resource-volume or capability metric. The previously-considered 'Kazakh is the most-resourced non-Turkish Turkic language' claim is FALSE as stated and must be rewritten as: 'Kazakh has the most extensive dedicated NLP research/benchmark ecosystem among non-Turkish Turkic languages, but trails Azerbaijani on both raw text volume (all three corpora checked) and shared native-benchmark accuracy (TUMLU-mini).'
findings.source: Synthesis of the four findings above (arXiv:1911.02116 Table 6; HF fineweb-2 datasets-server; live Wikipedia API; arXiv:2502.11020 Table 2).
findings.numbers: Volume ratios az:kk = 1.64x (CC-100 tok), 1.65-2.17x (FineWeb2), 1.93x (Wikipedia words); accuracy az>kk on 5/5 TUMLU models by 1.4-4.6pp
findings.relevance: This is the falsifiable, defensible ranking statement Decision 2 needs — it survives a reviewer holding the CC-100 table AND the FineWeb2/Wikipedia/TUMLU tables, because all four independent sources agree on direction.

findings.claim: [uz] Uzbek's raw web footprint is surprisingly SMALL relative to its ~34-35M speaker population (roughly 2.5-2.7x Kazakh's ~13M speakers): FineWeb2 shows Uzbek (uzn_Latn+uzn_Cyrl combined, reflecting the ongoing Latin/Cyrillic script split) at only 2.62M docs/4.05 GB, LESS than Kazakh's 3.38M docs/6.86 GB despite the larger population — and Uzbek scores WORST of the 4 major Turkic languages on TUMLU-mini (69.1-36.1 range across models, below Kazakh/Azerbaijani/Turkish on every model). This is relevant to the live Uzbek collaboration offer: Uzbek is comparably or more resource-constrained than Kazakh on raw web text, meaning KazQAD-style retrieval and the Less-is-More embedding recipe would face an EQUALLY or MORE severe low-resource regime porting to Uzbek, not an easier one.
findings.source: HF datasets-server fineweb-2 per-config size query (uzn_Latn, uzn_Cyrl); TUMLU Table 2 (arXiv:2502.11020).
findings.numbers: uz FineWeb2 combined 2.62M docs/4.05GB vs kk 3.38M docs/6.86GB; uz TUMLU: Claude 69.1, GPT-4o 65.4, Gemma-2-9B 36.1, Qwen2.5-7B 34.6, Llama-3.1-8B 29.9 (lowest of az/kk/tr/uz on every model)
findings.relevance: Directly informs Decision 1 (which Turkic language to port protocols to first) — Uzbek is not a 'higher-resource, easier port' target; a lab port there inherits comparable data scarcity to Kazakh plus a Latin/Cyrillic script bifurcation the Kazakh work does not have to handle (yet).

recommendations: Atlas positioning (Decision 2): replace any single-axis 'Kazakh is the most-resourced non-Turkish Turkic language' claim with the reconciled multi-axis statement (finding 6) — Kazakh leads on dedicated-ecosystem breadth only; Azerbaijani leads on raw volume (3 independent corpora) and TUMLU accuracy (5/5 models). Cite arXiv:1911.02116 Table 6 + fineweb-2 datasets-server + live Wikipedia stats + arXiv:2502.11020 Table 2 together so no single-source rebuttal is possible.

Decision 1 (protocol porting): do not treat Uzbek as an easier/higher-resource target than Kazakh — FineWeb2 shows Uzbek's combined Latin+Cyrillic web footprint (2.62M docs/4.05GB) is SMALLER than Kazakh's (3.38M docs/6.86GB) despite ~2.5x the population, and Uzbek scores lowest of the 4 major Turkic languages on TUMLU-mini across every model tested. A KazQAD-style retrieval port to Uzbek should budget for comparable-to-worse data scarcity plus an active Latin/Cyrillic script-split problem Kazakh does not have.

Decision 1 (protocol porting), secondary: Azerbaijani (not Uzbek) may be the objectively higher-resource, lower-risk first port given its 1.6-2.2x larger web corpus and better-performing existing models on the shared TUMLU benchmark — worth a direct cost-benefit note in the design panel even if the live collaboration offer is Uzbek-specific.

Decision 3 (pan-Turkic benchmark territory): TUMLU-mini is native-authored and covers 8 languages including Kazakh but has NOT been evaluated on any <=1B model of any kind (KB confirms no <=1B model tested on Kazakh TUMLU-mini) — running the lab's own <=600M model on TUMLU-mini across all 8 languages once trained would be a genuinely novel, currently-empty cell in the literature and a natural pan-Turkic companion result to the KazMMLU number.

Flag for the atlas: do not cite raw Wikipedia article counts as a resource-depth proxy without the word-count normalization — Tatar's 708,887 articles (more than Turkish) is very likely bot-stub inflation (cf. Cebuano Wikipedia precedent) and Kazakh's higher article count than Azerbaijani (244K vs 216K) inverts once measured by total words (39.9M vs 76.9M).
open_questions: Does a dedicated Azerbaijani decoder/generative LLM exist that this sweep missed (only encoder-only aLLMA was found via arXiv:2407.02337)? A Russian- or Azerbaijani-language search pass could surface local (Baku-based) efforts not indexed well in English arXiv search.

Are there more recent (2025-2026) Azerbaijani-specific benchmark papers beyond aLLMA/DOLLMA (2024) that would change the ecosystem-breadth axis? This sweep's search budget covered one primary paper only.

What is Turkish's exact FineWeb2 doc/byte count (the datasets-server /size query timed out due to corpus size) — needed to complete the full 8-language FineWeb2 table for the atlas rather than relying on CC-100 (2018) alone for Turkish.

Does TUMLU's 'community-developed materials with varying rigor' caveat for Azerbaijani/Kazakh conceal an asymmetry specifically favoring Azerbaijani question quality/difficulty (as opposed to genuine model competence driven by more Az training data)? The paper doesn't quantify inter-rater difficulty calibration between az and kk subsets specifically, so the TUMLU accuracy gap's causal source (data volume vs. question calibration) remains not fully disentangled.

gapFills.area: Turkic NLP landscape — cheap tokenizer-surgery+offline-distillation recipe (arXiv:2605.29992) vs canonical Less-is-More (arXiv:2603.22290) for Cyrillic/agglutinative/code-switched Kazakh

findings.claim: [tr] The tokenizer-surgery + offline-distillation recipe was validated EXCLUSIVELY on Latin-script Turkish (STSb-TR, TR-MTEB-26-tasks); the paper contains zero mention of Kazakh, Russian, or any Cyrillic-script language anywhere in the full text, and zero discussion of code-switching. Cross-script/Cyrillic transfer to Kazakh is entirely unestablished by the source paper itself — the 'transfers to Kazakh' recommendation is pure extrapolation, not evidence.
findings.source: arXiv:2605.29992 (Bayram, Diri, Yıldırım, 'Adapting Multilingual Embedding Models to Turkish via Cross-Lingual Tokenizer Surgery and Offline Distillation', submitted 2026-05-28, preprint, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, no peer-review venue stated); full-text checked at arxiv.org/html/2605.29992
findings.numbers: 0 mentions of Kazakh/Cyrillic/code-switching in full text; teacher=EmbeddingGemma-300M (256K SentencePiece vocab); student vocab pruned 256K->131,072
findings.relevance: The Uzbek-collab and pan-Turkic porting decision needs evidence the recipe survives a script change (Cyrillic) plus a code-switching regime (kk/ru); neither exists. Treating this as validated-for-Kazakh would be citing a paper for something it never tested.

findings.claim: [tr] The recipe's teacher is EmbeddingGemma-300M, NOT mE5-base (the lab's canonical Less-is-More base) — so 'replacing Less-is-More with tokenizer-surgery' actually means swapping the base architecture (Gemma3 decoder-derived, 300M, 256K vocab) AND the recipe simultaneously, not a like-for-like recipe substitution on the same backbone.
findings.source: arXiv:2605.29992 full text (arxiv.org/html/2605.29992), Methodology section
findings.numbers: Teacher: EmbeddingGemma-300M = 196.6M embedding params + 104.0M backbone, 768-dim output, 2,048-token input cap; Student: ~200M, 131,072 vocab, 8,192-token context
findings.relevance: Any lab decision to adopt this recipe is really a decision to adopt EmbeddingGemma as teacher, which the lab's own KB already found to be a WEAKER low-resource-language performer than mE5 (see next finding) — this is a compounding risk, not a clean recipe swap.

findings.claim: [pan-turkic] Under the lab's own canonical Less-is-More protocol (10k noisy synthetic pairs, same recipe applied to both bases for comparability), EmbeddingGemma-300M underperformed mE5-base on the nearest available Cyrillic/LRL analogue (Armenian) retrieval: 65.22 (main) / 75.00 (merged) vs mE5's 79.35 (main) / 78.80 (merged) — EmbeddingGemma needed 1M pairs to reach mE5's 10k-pair result (77.06 vs 76.42 avg, per prior KB finding). Since the tokenizer-surgery recipe distills FROM EmbeddingGemma, the student is capped by ("bounded by the semantic space of", the surgery paper's own words) an already-inferior-on-LRL teacher.
findings.source: arXiv:2603.22290 (Less is More, Navasardyan et al., Metric AI Lab) full text arxiv.org/html/2603.22290, Table 1; cross-referenced against arXiv:2605.29992 teacher identity and its own stated 'semantic ceiling' limitation
findings.numbers: Armenian retrieval @10k pairs: mE5-base 79.35/78.80 (main/merged) vs EmbeddingGemma-300M 65.22/75.00; EmbeddingGemma needs 1M pairs (77.06 avg) to match mE5's 10k-pair result (76.42 avg)
findings.relevance: Chaining tokenizer-surgery onto EmbeddingGemma imports a documented LRL-retrieval weakness into any Kazakh adaptation, directly undermining the lab's retrieval-first (KazQAD/MTEB-style) canonical protocol.

findings.claim: [tr] Within the surgery paper's own results, the student's gain over teacher is concentrated in STS (+4.6 abs, 77.5 vs 72.9) and NLI (+7.3 abs, 67.9 vs 60.6), but it LOSES to the teacher on Retrieval (72.2 vs 75.9, -3.7 abs) and on the overall TR-MTEB mean (63.9 vs 65.2, achieving only '98.0% of teacher'). Retrieval is precisely the axis the lab's canonical protocols (KazQAD, MTEB-style) are built around.
findings.source: arXiv:2605.29992 full text, Benchmark Results tables (STSb-TR, TR-MTEB 26 tasks)
findings.numbers: TR-MTEB: student 63.9% mean (rank 7/26), Retrieval 72.2%; teacher (EmbeddingGemma-300M) 65.2% mean (rank 4/26), Retrieval 75.9%; STSb-TR student 77.55/77.45 (P/S) vs teacher 73.84/72.92
findings.relevance: Even in-distribution (Turkish, Latin script, the paper's best case) the recipe's demonstrated strength is semantic similarity/NLI, not retrieval — the wrong axis for the lab's canonical KazQAD-style deliverable.

findings.claim: [tr] The surgery paper's own stated limitation directly predicts Kazakh-specific failure: pruning vocab 256K->131,072 tokens 'reduces the model's capacity to represent non-target languages... performance on lower-resource non-target languages may degrade.' A Turkish-optimized 128K vocab was built by extracting the top 64K frequent tokens from a Turkish-only corpus (Cosmos Turkish Corpus) plus multilingual tokens from a 40-language Wikipedia frequency analysis (Kazakh not named as one of the 40). Applying the SAME (Turkish) tokenizer to Kazakh, rather than building a dedicated Kazakh-corpus vocab, would incur exactly this stated degradation; building a dedicated Kazakh version is unverified but architecturally analogous work, not yet done by anyone.
findings.source: arXiv:2605.29992 full text, Limitations section + Tokenizer Construction section
findings.numbers: Vocab: 256K (teacher) -> 131,072 (student); 64K top-frequency Turkish tokens seeded from Cosmos Turkish Corpus; ~580K total distillation training rows (Turkish+English capped 100K each, other 38 languages capped 10K each)
findings.relevance: For a Kazakh port, this is a build-from-scratch-tokenizer exercise (like SozKZ's from-scratch BPE, already in KB) grafted onto a distillation step — not a drop-in reuse of the published Turkish artifact. Feasibility is plausible given Kazakh/Turkish share Turkic agglutinative typology, but zero empirical evidence exists for the Kipchak branch (Kazakh) vs the paper's Oghuz branch (Turkish) target.

findings.claim: [pan-turkic] No head-to-head between the tokenizer-surgery recipe and Less-is-More exists in the literature: arXiv:2605.29992 does not cite, benchmark against, or discuss 'Less is More' (arXiv:2603.22290) at all, despite both being 2026 low-cost embedding-adaptation papers. The two recipes are also not directly comparable on compute cost from published numbers: surgery = $5-20 total / ~4 hrs on 1x A100-80GB (fully documented); Less-is-More = <$20 for the translation/generation phase only (10k pairs via Gemini 2.5 Flash) with fine-tuning run on 16x MI250x GPUs but NO GPU-hours or wall-clock time disclosed for the fine-tune itself.
findings.source: arXiv:2605.29992 full text (no citation of arXiv:2603.22290 found); arXiv:2603.22290 full text (arxiv.org/html/2603.22290), compute/training section
findings.numbers: Surgery: $5-20, ~4 GPU-hrs, 1x A100-80GB. Less-is-More: <$20 (data-gen only, Gemini 2.5 Flash), fine-tune on 16x MI250x GPUs, batch 512, lr 7e-5, 5 epochs, GPU-hours unreported
findings.relevance: The 'four researchers recommend adopting/benchmarking' claim has no literature support for a comparison — any head-to-head would be a genuinely novel evallab experiment, not a replication of a published result; cost claims used to justify a switch cannot currently be verified as apples-to-apples.

findings.claim: [pan-turkic][kk-anchor] The canonical Less-is-More recipe's own authors already flag the exact Kazakh-relevant gap as open and untested — 'It remains unclear if this noisy alignment holds for low-resource Cyrillic languages [sharing a script with a high-resource neighbor]' — and nothing in arXiv:2605.29992 closes that gap since it never touches a Cyrillic language either. Both the canonical recipe AND the challenger recipe are equally out-of-distribution for Kazakh/Kyrgyz/Tatar/Bashkir-class languages (Cyrillic, high-resource-neighbor code-switching, Kipchak agglutination).
findings.source: arXiv:2603.22290 full text, Discussion/Limitations (already in lab KB, re-confirmed); arXiv:2605.29992 full text (no Cyrillic content, confirmed above)
findings.numbers: Less-is-More validated only on Armenian (hye, unique script) and Georgian (kat, unique script) retrieval; Turkish paper validated only on Latin-script Turkish
findings.relevance: This is the decisive finding for the lab's recipe decision: swapping canonical to tokenizer-surgery would trade one untested-for-Kazakh recipe for another equally untested-for-Kazakh recipe, with the added downside of a documentedly weaker-on-LRL teacher (EmbeddingGemma) and a retrieval-axis weakness in-domain.

recommendations: Do NOT replace the canonical Less-is-More/mE5-base recipe with the tokenizer-surgery+offline-distillation recipe based on current evidence: it is unvalidated on any Cyrillic, agglutinative-Kipchak, or code-switched language, its published teacher (EmbeddingGemma-300M) is already shown in the lab's own KB to underperform mE5 on the closest LRL analogue (Armenian retrieval, 65.22 vs 79.35 at 10k pairs), and its one in-domain weak axis (retrieval, -3.7 abs vs teacher) is exactly the lab's canonical target axis (KazQAD-style).

If the tokenizer-surgery MECHANISM (cheap vocab pruning + mean-composition init + offline cosine distillation, $5-20/4 GPU-hrs) is still attractive for its cost profile, evaluate it as a variant with a STRONGER retrieval teacher than EmbeddingGemma — e.g. distill from mE5-large-instruct or BGE-M3 (KB: 0.8949 / 0.9017 nDCG@10 on Kazakh Belebele retrieval) rather than from EmbeddingGemma; this specific configuration has never been tried by anyone and would be a genuinely novel evallab experiment, not a replication.

Before any design-panel decision to adopt/benchmark this recipe, run it as a proper evallab ablation on Kazakh (Cyrillic + kk/ru code-switch) rather than trusting the Turkish result to transfer — budget it as one 'apparatus on credit' item only if it is the next concrete blocker to a measurement, per the campaign's apparatus freeze.

For the Uzbek-collaboration porting question, prioritize Less-is-More over tokenizer-surgery as the first-choice recipe to port, since Less-is-More at least documents a full noisy-synthetic-pair protocol with disclosed hyperparameters (even though GPU-hours are undisclosed), while tokenizer-surgery requires building an entirely new teacher+vocab pipeline with no Turkic-Cyrillic precedent.
open_questions: Does the tokenizer-surgery recipe's degradation from vocab pruning (256K->128K) apply symmetrically if English is dropped from the retained set in favor of Russian (needed for kk/ru code-switching), or does Russian's own high resource level in the teacher's original 256K vocab make it a cheaper 'already-present' language to retain than Kazakh was for Turkish's English?

What are the actual GPU-hours/wall-clock cost for the Less-is-More fine-tuning step (16x MI250x, batch 512, 5 epochs) — needed to make a fair $-for-$ comparison against tokenizer-surgery's disclosed $5-20/4hrs?

Would a dedicated Kazakh-corpus tokenizer-surgery (analogous to the paper's Cosmos-Turkish-Corpus top-64K-token extraction) built on the lab's own ~9-10B token Kazakh corpus outperform reusing a generic multilingual vocab, and by how much — this requires an in-house experiment, no published number exists for any Kipchak language.

Is TR-MTEB's retrieval-task weakness (student 72.2% vs teacher 75.9%) driven by the linear-only pooling/projection layers (paper's own stated limitation) or by the vocab pruning itself — this matters because if it's the linear projection, a KazQAD-focused implementation could add task-specific fine-tuning to recover retrieval performance without touching the tokenizer-surgery step.
